bal.17.so17: I bow to Hanumān, son of the Wind, a fire to the forest of the wicked, full of wisdom.
In the house of his heart Śrī Rāma dwells, holding his bow and arrows.
kishkindha.29.do29: When the Lord grew as he bound Bali, his body became too vast to describe.
Within two ghaṛīs (under an hour) I ran round it seven times.
kishkindha.30.cau1: Aṅgada said: I could get across, but I have some doubt in my mind about coming back.
Jāmbavān said: You are fit for everything, but you are the leader of all of us; how can we send you?
kishkindha.30.cau2: Jāmbavān, king of the bears, said: Listen, Hanumān. Why have you fallen silent, mighty one?
You are the son of the Wind and as strong as the Wind; you are a treasury of intelligence, discernment and realised knowledge.
kishkindha.30.cau3: What task in the world is so hard that you cannot do it, dear one?
You were born for Śrī Rāma's work. As soon as he heard this, Hanumān became as huge as a mountain.
kishkindha.30.cau4: His body, the colour of gold, blazed with splendour, as though he were a second king of mountains.
Roaring like a lion again and again, he said: I could leap across the salt ocean in play.
kishkindha.30.cau5: I could kill Rāvaṇa along with his helpers, then uproot Trikūṭa and bring it here.
Jāmbavān, I ask you: give me fitting counsel.
kishkindha.30.cau6: Jāmbavān said: Dear one, all you need do is go and see Sītā, then come and give us news of her.
After that the lotus-eyed Lord will do the rest by the strength of his own arms, taking the monkey army along only for sport.
kishkindha.30.cha1: With the monkey army Śrī Rāma will destroy the demons and bring Sītā back.
Gods, sages, Nārada and others will tell of his fair fame, which makes the three worlds pure.
A person who hears it, sings it, tells it and understands it reaches the supreme state.
Tulasīdāsa, a bee hovering at Śrī Rāma's lotus feet, sings it.
kishkindha.30.do30क: The fame of Śrī Rāma is the remedy for worldly existence.
Men and women who listen to it have all their wishes fulfilled by Śrī Rāma, slayer of Triśirā.
kishkindha.30.so30ख: Dark of body as a blue lotus, more beautiful than ten million Kāmadevas:
listen to the host of virtues of him whose name is a hunter to the birds of sin.
sundar.0.shloka1: I bow to him who is serene, eternal, immeasurable and sinless, the giver of the peace of liberation,
ceaselessly served by Brahmā, Śiva and Śeṣa, king of serpents, known through the Vedānta and pervading all;
who is called Rāma, the Lord of the world, teacher of the gods, Hari who through māyā (his power of illusion) appears as a man;
the mine of compassion, the best of the Raghus, the crest-jewel of kings.
sundar.0.shloka2: O Lord of the Raghus, there is no other longing in my heart.
This is the truth, and you dwell in all as their inner Self.
O best of the Raghus, grant me devotion in its fullness.
Make my mind free of desire and the other faults.
sundar.0.shloka3: I salute the son of the Wind: the home of matchless strength, his body shining like a mountain of gold,
a fire to the forest of the demons, foremost among the wise,
the treasury of every virtue, lord of the monkeys,
dear devotee of the Lord of the Raghus.
sundar.1.cau1: Jāmbavān's words were pleasing, and Hanumān was delighted at heart to hear them.
He said: Brothers, wait for me till then, bearing hardship and living on tubers, roots and fruit,
sundar.1.cau2: until I return from seeing Sītā. The work will be done; a special joy fills me.
With these words he bowed his head to everyone and, holding Śrī Rāma in his heart, set off in joy.
sundar.1.cau3: On the shore of the ocean stood a fine mountain. Hanumān leapt onto it for sport.
Remembering Śrī Rāma again and again, the mighty son of the Wind sprang up with tremendous force.
sundar.1.cau4: The mountain on which Hanumān planted his feet as he set off sank at once into the netherworld.
As Śrī Rāma's unfailing arrow flies, so Hanumān sped on.
sundar.1.cau5: The Ocean, considering that he was the messenger of Śrī Rāma, said: Maināka, be the one to relieve his weariness.
sundar.1.do1: Hanumān touched Maināka with his hand, bowed to him, and said:
Until Śrī Rāma's work is done, how can I rest?
sundar.2.cau1: The gods watched the son of the Wind on his way, and to find out how great his strength and wisdom were,
they sent Surasā, the mother of serpents. She came and spoke these words.
sundar.2.cau2: Today the gods have given me my food. On hearing her words, Hanumān said:
When I have done Śrī Rāma's work and come back and told the Lord the news of Sītā,
sundar.2.cau3: After that I will come and enter your mouth; this is the truth, mother, so let me go.
But on no account would she let him pass. Hanumān said: Then why do you not swallow me?
sundar.2.cau4: She opened her mouth a yojana wide (a yojana is some eight miles), and Hanumān made his body twice that size.
She stretched her mouth to sixteen yojanas; at once the son of the Wind grew to thirty-two.
sundar.2.cau5: However wide Surasā made her mouth, Hanumān showed a form twice as large.
When her mouth reached a hundred yojanas, the son of the Wind took on a very tiny form.
sundar.2.cau6: Going into her mouth, he came back out, then bowed his head to her and asked leave to go.
She said: The gods sent me to learn the secret of your wisdom and strength, and I have learnt it.
sundar.2.do2: You will accomplish all of Śrī Rāma's work, treasury of strength and wisdom that you are.
Blessing him, she went away, and Hanumān went on his way rejoicing.
sundar.3.cau1: A demoness lived in the ocean who caught the birds of the air by sorcery.
When creatures flew through the sky, she would see their shadows in the water
sundar.3.cau2: and seize the shadow, so that they could not fly away; in this way she always fed on those that travel the sky.
She tried the same trick on Hanumān, and he saw through her deceit at once.
sundar.3.cau3: Having killed her, the brave and steady-minded son of the Wind reached the far shore of the ocean.
Arriving there, he saw the beauty of the forest, where bees hummed, greedy for honey.
sundar.3.cau4: Trees of many kinds were lovely with fruit and flowers, and the flocks of birds and herds of animals delighted his heart.
Ahead of him he saw a huge mountain, and casting off fear he ran and climbed it.
sundar.3.cau5: Umā, in this there is no greatness of Hanumān's own; it is the glory of the Lord, which devours even Death.
Climbing the mountain, he saw Laṅkā, a fortress so extraordinary that words cannot describe it.
sundar.3.cau6: It is very lofty, with the ocean on all four sides, and its rampart of gold blazes with light.
sundar.3.cha1: Laṅkā's wall is of gold, set with gems of every colour, and within it stand many fine mansions.
With its crossroads, markets, good roads and lanes, the city is beautifully laid out in every way.
Who could count its herds of elephants, horses and mules, its foot soldiers and its many chariots?
The bands of demons who take many forms, and their army of immense strength, are beyond describing.
sundar.3.cha2: Woods, gardens, groves, flower gardens, lakes, wells and stepwells adorn it.
Maidens of men, nāgas, gods and gandharvas charm the minds of sages with their beauty.
In places, wrestlers of immense strength, with huge bodies like mountains, are roaring.
In many arenas they grapple and challenge one another in many ways.
sundar.3.cha3: Millions of warriors of fearsome build guard the city with care on all four sides.
In places the wicked demons are devouring buffaloes, humans, cows, donkeys and goats.
For this reason Tulasīdāsa has told a little of their story:
With Śrī Rāma's arrows as their place of pilgrimage they will give up their bodies and surely attain salvation.
sundar.3.do3: Seeing the city's many guards, Hanumān reflected:
I will take a very small form and make my way into the city by night.
sundar.4.cau1: Taking a form the size of a mosquito, Hanumān set out for Laṅkā, remembering the Lord in human form.
A demoness named Laṅkinī said: Are you going in without a thought for me?
sundar.4.cau2: You fool, do you not know my secret? Thieves, as many as there are, are all my food.
The great Hanumān struck her a single blow with his fist, and she tumbled to the ground, vomiting blood.
sundar.4.cau3: Then Laṅkinī recovered and rose, and with joined palms she pleaded in fear:
When Brahmā granted Rāvaṇa his boon, he told me a sign as he was leaving:
sundar.4.cau4: When a monkey's blow leaves you reeling, know then that the demons are destroyed.
My merit is very great, dear one, for I have seen Śrī Rāma's messenger with my own eyes.
sundar.4.do4: Dear one, put the joys of heaven and of liberation together on one side of a scale.
All of them together do not weigh as much as the joy of a moment in the company of the good.
sundar.5.cau1: Enter the city and do all your work, keeping the king of Kosala in your heart.
Poison turns to nectar, enemies act as friends, the ocean shrinks to a cow's hoofprint and fire grows cool,
sundar.5.cau2: and Mount Sumeru becomes like a speck of dust, Garuḍa, for one on whom Śrī Rāma has looked with grace.
Hanumān took a very small form and entered the city, remembering the Lord.
sundar.5.cau3: He searched palace after palace and saw countless warriors everywhere.
Then he went into the palace of Rāvaṇa, so wondrous that it cannot be described.
sundar.5.cau4: Hanumān saw Rāvaṇa lying asleep, but Sītā was not to be seen in that palace.
Then he saw a lovely house with a separate temple of Śrī Hari built in it.
sundar.5.do5: The house was marked with emblems of Śrī Rāma's weapons, and its beauty was beyond words.
Seeing clumps of fresh tulasī there, Hanumān, the best of monkeys, was overjoyed.
sundar.6.cau1: Laṅkā is the home of hosts of demons; how could a good person live here?
So Hanumān began to reason in his mind, and at that very moment Vibhīṣaṇa awoke.
sundar.6.cau2: He called the Lord to mind, saying Rāma, Rāma, and Hanumān was glad at heart, knowing him for a good man.
I will make a point of making myself known to him; a good man brings no harm to one's work.
sundar.6.cau3: Taking the form of a brāhmaṇa, Hanumān spoke to him, and on hearing him Vibhīṣaṇa rose and came there.
He bowed, asked after his welfare and said: Brāhmaṇa, tell me your story and make it clear.
sundar.6.cau4: Are you one of the servants of Śrī Hari? A great love is rising in my heart.
Or else, are you Śrī Rāma himself, who loves the humble, come to make me blessed?
sundar.6.do6: Then Hanumān told him all of Śrī Rāma's story, and his own name.
At this, both of them thrilled from head to foot, and remembering the Lord's many virtues their minds were lost in them.
sundar.7.cau1: Listen, son of the Wind, to how I live here: like the poor tongue among the teeth.
Dear one, will the Lord of the Sun's line ever know me to be without a protector and be gracious to me?
sundar.7.cau2: My body is tāmasic, of the nature of darkness; I have no spiritual practice, and my mind has no love for the lotus feet of the Lord.
Yet now, Hanumān, I have taken heart, for without the grace of Śrī Hari one does not meet saints.
sundar.7.cau3: It is because Śrī Rāma has been gracious to me that you have sought me out and shown yourself to me.
Listen, Vibhīṣaṇa, to the Lord's way: he always loves his servants.
sundar.7.cau4: Tell me, what high and noble birth is mine? I am a restless monkey, lowly in every way.
Whoever takes our name in the morning goes without food that day.
sundar.7.do7: Listen, my friend: lowly as I am, even on me Śrī Rāma has shown his grace.
As he remembered the Lord's virtues, Hanumān's eyes filled with tears.
sundar.8.cau1: Those who know such a master and still forget him and wander about, how should they not be miserable?
Telling thus of Śrī Rāma's many virtues, he found a peace beyond words.
sundar.8.cau2: Then Vibhīṣaṇa told him everything: how Janaka's daughter was living there.
Then Hanumān said: Listen, brother, I wish to see Mother Jānakī.
sundar.8.cau3: Vibhīṣaṇa explained every means to him, and Hanumān, son of the Wind, took leave of him and set out.
Taking the same form again, he went to the place in the Aśoka grove where Sītā was living.
sundar.8.cau4: Seeing her, he bowed to her in his heart. She sits on as the watches of the night go by.
Her body is wasted, her hair is a single matted braid, and in her heart she repeats Śrī Rāma's virtues one after another.
sundar.8.do8: Her eyes rest on her own feet, her mind is lost in Śrī Rāma's lotus feet.
Seeing Jānakī in such distress, the son of the Wind was filled with grief.
sundar.9.cau1: He stayed hidden among the leaves of the tree, thinking: Well, what am I to do now?
Just then Rāvaṇa came there, dressed in finery, with many women.
sundar.9.cau2: In many ways the wicked one tried to win Sītā over, using conciliation, gifts, intimidation and sowing discord.
Rāvaṇa said: Listen, fair-faced and clever one: Mandodarī and all my other queens
sundar.9.cau3: I shall make your maidservants; this is my vow. Only look my way once.
Holding up a blade of grass as a screen, and remembering her most loving lord, the king of Avadh, Sītā spoke:
sundar.9.cau4: Listen, Rāvaṇa: does a lotus ever open in the light of a firefly?
Sītā went on: Understand this in your mind. Wretch, you have no thought of Śrī Rāma's arrows.
sundar.9.cau5: Fool, you carried me off when I was left alone. Vile, shameless creature, have you no shame?
sundar.9.do9: Hearing himself likened to a firefly and Śrī Rāma to the sun,
and hearing such harsh words, Rāvaṇa drew his sword and, stung with fury, said:
sundar.10.cau1: Sītā, you have insulted me. I will cut off your head with this cruel sword.
Otherwise, do as I say at once, fair one, or you will lose your life.
sundar.10.cau2: Rāvaṇa, the Lord's arm is as lovely as a garland of dark lotuses, and like an elephant's trunk.
Either that arm will be around my neck or your dreadful sword. Listen, fool: this vow of mine is true.
sundar.10.cau3: Candrahāsa (Rāvaṇa's sword), take away my anguish, born of the fire of separation from Śrī Rāma.
Your edge is cool, keen and fine. Sītā said: Take away the weight of my sorrow.
sundar.10.cau4: Hearing her words, he then rushed at her to kill her, but Mandodarī, Maya's daughter, reasoned with him and gave him wise counsel.
He summoned all the demonesses and said: Go and terrify Sītā in every way you can.
sundar.10.cau5: If within a month she has not done as I say, then I will take my sword out and kill her.
sundar.10.do10: Rāvaṇa went back to his palace.
Here a band of demonesses take on many hideous forms and terrify Sītā.
sundar.11.cau1: One demoness, named Trijaṭā, loved Śrī Rāma's feet and was wise in discernment.
She called them all together, told them her dream and said: Serve Sītā and so do yourselves good.
sundar.11.cau2: In my dream a monkey burned Laṅkā and slew the whole demon army.
Rāvaṇa is riding a donkey, naked, his ten heads shaven and his twenty arms cut off.
sundar.11.cau3: In this state he is going towards the south, and it seems that Vibhīṣaṇa has gained Laṅkā.
Śrī Rāma's sovereignty has been proclaimed through the city, and then the Lord has sent for Sītā.
sundar.11.cau4: I tell you this dream aloud: within a few days it will come true.
Hearing what she said, they all grew afraid and threw themselves at the feet of the daughter of Janaka.
sundar.11.do11: Then they all went off this way and that, and Sītā thought anxiously:
When the month is over, the vile demon will kill me.
sundar.12.cau1: Sītā said to Trijaṭā, her hands folded: Mother, in my misfortune you are my companion.
Quickly find me some way to give up this body; this unbearable separation can be borne no longer.
sundar.12.cau2: Bring wood and build a pyre, and then, mother, set it alight.
Wise one, prove my love true. Who could bear to hear words that pierce the ears like a spike?
sundar.12.cau3: Hearing her words, Trijaṭā clasped her feet and comforted her, telling her of the Lord's glory, strength and fair fame.
Listen, gentle lady: at night no fire can be found. With these words she went back to her own home.
sundar.12.cau4: Sītā said: Fate has turned against me. I shall find no fire, and my pain will not end.
Embers are plainly to be seen in the sky, yet not a single star comes down to earth.
sundar.12.cau5: The moon is made of fire, yet it does not shower fire on me, as though it knew me for an unlucky one.
Hear my plea, Aśoka tree: be true to your name (Aśoka, without sorrow) and take my sorrow away.
sundar.12.cau6: Your new leaves are like fire: give me fire, and do not drive my suffering to its last extreme.
Seeing Sītā so overwhelmed by separation, Hanumān felt that moment pass like an aeon.
sundar.12.so12: Then Hanumān, having thought it over in his heart, dropped the ring down to her.
It was as if the Aśoka had given her an ember: she rose joyfully and caught it up in her hand.
sundar.13.cau1: Then she saw the lovely ring, engraved with Śrī Rāma's name and exceedingly beautiful.
Recognising it, she gazed at it in wonder, her heart stirred by joy and sorrow together.
sundar.13.cau2: Who could defeat Śrī Rāma, the unconquerable? And no magic illusion could make a ring like this.
While Sītā turned many thoughts over in her mind, Hanumān spoke in a sweet voice.
sundar.13.cau3: He began to describe Śrī Rāma's virtues, and as soon as she heard them Sītā's sorrow fled.
She listened with ears and mind intent, and he told her the whole story, starting from the very beginning.
sundar.13.cau4: The one who has told this lovely story, nectar to the ears, why does he not show himself, brother?
Then Hanumān came close to her. She turned her face away and sat, wondering in her mind.
sundar.13.cau5: Mother Jānakī, I am the messenger of Śrī Rāma; I swear it truly by the Lord, the treasury of compassion.
Mother, I brought this ring: Śrī Rāma gave it so that you would know me by it.
sundar.13.cau6: Tell me, how did man and monkey come together? And he told her the story of how that companionship had come about.
sundar.13.do13: Hearing Hanumān's loving words, Sītā felt trust rise in her heart.
She knew that he was a servant, in thought, deed and word, of the ocean of mercy.
sundar.14.cau1: Recognising him as a devotee of Hari, Sītā felt a deep and intense love; tears came to her eyes, and the hair on her body stood on end.
Hanumān, dear one, I was drowning in the ocean of separation, and you have become a ship for me.
sundar.14.cau2: Now tell me, and may I be a sacrifice for you, how Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara and home of joy, fares with his younger brother.
Śrī Rāma is tender-hearted and compassionate; why, Hanumān, has he put on such hardness?
sundar.14.cau3: Does Śrī Rāma, whose very nature it is to give joy to his servants, ever think of me?
Dear one, will my eyes ever be cooled by gazing on his dark and tender form?
sundar.14.cau4: No words would come, and her eyes filled with tears: Alas, my Lord, you have forgotten me utterly!
Seeing Sītā so overwhelmed by the pain of separation, Hanumān spoke to her gently and humbly.
sundar.14.cau5: Mother, the Lord is well, and his younger brother with him; but he, the abode of grace, grieves at your grief.
Mother, do not be downcast at heart: Śrī Rāma's love is twice as great as yours.
sundar.14.do14: Mother, take heart now and listen to Śrī Rāma's message.
Saying this, Hanumān was overcome, his voice faltering and his eyes brimming with tears.
sundar.15.cau1: This is what Śrī Rāma said: Sītā, in separation from you, all things have turned contrary for me.
The trees' new leaves seem like fire, night is like the night of doom, and the moon like the sun.
sundar.15.cau2: Beds of blue lotuses seem a forest of spears, and the clouds seem to rain boiling oil.
Things that once did me good now give me pain, and the breeze, cool, gentle and fragrant, is like a serpent's breath.
sundar.15.cau3: Grief grows a little lighter even by being told, but whom shall I tell? No one understands it.
Beloved, the truth of the love between you and me is known to my mind alone.
sundar.15.cau4: And that mind stays always with you; from this much alone, know the essence of my love.
Hearing the Lord's message, Sītā was so immersed in love that she was no longer aware of her body.
sundar.15.cau5: Hanumān said: Mother, take heart, and remember Śrī Rāma, who gives joy to his servants.
Call to mind the majesty of Śrī Rāma, and hearing my words, give up your faint-heartedness.
sundar.15.do15: The demon hordes are like moths, and Śrī Rāma's arrows like fire.
Mother, take heart: think of the demons as already burnt.
sundar.16.cau1: Had Śrī Rāma received news of you, he would have made no delay.
Jānakī, once the sun of Śrī Rāma's arrows rises, where will the darkness of the demon hosts be?
sundar.16.cau2: Mother, I would take you with me right now; but the Lord has not commanded it, I swear by Śrī Rāma.
Mother, be patient a few days more; Śrī Rāma will come with the monkeys.
sundar.16.cau3: He will slay the demons and take you away, and Nārada and others will sing his fame in all three worlds.
Son, the monkeys are all like you, and the demons are very mighty warriors.
sundar.16.cau4: There is great doubt in my heart. Hearing this, Hanumān revealed his own true body.
Vast as a golden mountain, fearsome in battle: a hero of immense strength.
sundar.16.cau5: Then trust came into Sītā's mind, and Hanumān, son of the Wind, again took on a small form.
sundar.16.do16: Listen, Mother: a monkey has no great strength or wisdom.
Yet by the Lord's might even the tiniest snake can eat up Garuḍa.
sundar.17.cau1: Sītā's heart was content as she heard Hanumān's words, steeped in devotion, glory, splendour and strength.
Knowing him to be dear to Śrī Rāma, she blessed him: Dear one, may you be a treasury of strength and good character.
sundar.17.cau2: Son, may you be free from age and death and a treasury of virtues, and may Śrī Rāma show you great affection.
Hearing with his own ears the wish that the Lord might be gracious to him, Hanumān was utterly immersed in love.
sundar.17.cau3: Time after time Hanumān laid his head at her feet; then, folding his hands, he said:
Mother, now I have achieved all I could wish for; your blessing is famed as one that never fails.
sundar.17.cau4: Listen, Mother: seeing the lovely fruit on these trees, I feel very hungry.
Listen, son: those who keep watch over the grove are demons, great and mighty warriors.
sundar.17.cau5: Mother, I have no fear of them, if it pleases you at heart.
sundar.17.do17: Seeing that Hanumān was skilled in intelligence and in strength, Sītā said: Go, dear one.
Keep Śrī Rāma's feet in your heart and eat the sweet fruit.
sundar.18.cau1: He bowed his head, set off and entered the garden. He ate the fruit and began to break the trees.
Many warriors stood guard there; some he killed, and some went off and raised the alarm.
sundar.18.cau2: My lord, a huge monkey has come and ravaged the Aśoka grove.
He has been eating the fruit and tearing up the trees, and he has crushed the guards one after another and thrown them to the ground.
sundar.18.cau3: Hearing this, Rāvaṇa sent many warriors. At the sight of them Hanumān roared.
He slew all the demons; a few, left half-dead, ran off crying out.
sundar.18.cau4: Then Rāvaṇa sent Akṣaya Kumāra, who set out with countless fine warriors.
Seeing him approach, Hanumān grasped a tree and challenged him; he felled him and let out a mighty roar.
sundar.18.do18: Some he killed, some he crushed, some he seized and ground into the dust.
Some once more went and cried: My lord, the monkey's strength is enormous.
sundar.19.cau1: Hearing that his son had been slain, Rāvaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, was enraged and sent the mighty Meghanāda:
Do not kill him, my son; bind him. Let us see this monkey and where he comes from.
sundar.19.cau2: Indrajit, the matchless warrior, set out, anger welling up in him when he heard his brother had been killed.
Hanumān saw that a fearsome warrior had come; gnashing his teeth, he roared and rushed at him.
sundar.19.cau3: He uprooted an enormous tree and left the son of the lord of Laṅkā without a chariot.
The great warriors who were with him Hanumān seized one after another and crushed against his own body.
sundar.19.cau4: Having felled them, he closed with Meghanāda, and the two fought like a pair of mighty elephants.
Hanumān struck him with his fist and went and climbed a tree; for a moment Meghanāda lay senseless.
sundar.19.cau5: Getting up again, he wove many illusions, yet the son of the Wind could not be defeated.
sundar.19.do19: He aimed the weapon of Brahmā, and Hanumān thought to himself:
If I do not honour Brahmā's arrow, its boundless glory will be lost.
sundar.20.cau1: He struck Hanumān with Brahmā's arrow; even in falling, Hanumān destroyed the host.
Seeing Hanumān fall senseless, Meghanāda bound him with a serpent noose and took him away.
sundar.20.cau2: Listen, Pārvatī: by repeating his name the wise cut the bonds of worldly existence.
Could his messenger ever fall into bonds? It was for the Lord's work that Hanumān let himself be bound.
sundar.20.cau3: Hearing that Hanumān had been bound, the demons came running, and all of them gathered in the court to see the spectacle.
Hanumān came there and saw Rāvaṇa's court; its grandeur was beyond words.
sundar.20.cau4: Gods and the guardians of the quarters stood humbly with joined palms, all of them watching his brow in fear.
Seeing such power, Hanumān felt no fear at all, as Garuḍa is fearless in the midst of a host of serpents.
sundar.20.do20: Looking at Hanumān, Rāvaṇa laughed, uttering words of abuse.
Then he remembered his son's death, and grief rose in his heart.
sundar.21.cau1: Rāvaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, said: Monkey, who are you? On whose strength did you lay waste the grove?
Or is it that you have never heard of me? I see you are utterly without fear, you wretch.
sundar.21.cau2: What offence did the demons commit, that you killed them? Tell me, wretch, have you no care for your life?
Hear me, Rāvaṇa: the one whose strength enables māyā to fashion the hosts of universes;
sundar.21.cau3: through whose strength, ten-headed one, Brahmā creates, Hari preserves and Śiva dissolves;
through whose strength the thousand-faced Śeṣa holds up on his head the universe itself, its mountains and forests too;
sundar.21.cau4: who, as protector of the gods, takes bodies of many kinds, and who teaches wretches like you a lesson;
who broke the unyielding bow of Śiva and with it crushed the pride of the assembled kings;
sundar.21.cau5: who slew Khara, Dūṣaṇa, Triśirā and Vālī, every one of them a warrior of matchless strength;
sundar.21.do21: by the merest fraction of whose strength you conquered all creation, moving and unmoving:
I am the messenger of him whose beloved wife you have carried off and brought here.
sundar.22.cau1: I know your greatness: you had a fight with Sahasrabāhu.
In battle with Vāli you won fame. Hearing Hanumān's words, Rāvaṇa laughed them off.
sundar.22.cau2: I ate the fruit, my lord, because I was hungry, and being a monkey by nature I broke the trees.
Everyone holds his own body most dear, master; those who walk the wrong path began to strike me.
sundar.22.cau3: I struck those who struck me, and for that your son bound me.
Being bound does not shame me at all: I want to do my own Lord's work.
sundar.22.cau4: With joined hands I make this request, Rāvaṇa: put aside your pride and listen to my counsel.
Think of your own lineage and see; give up your delusion and worship him who takes away his devotees' fear.
sundar.22.cau5: He is the one of whom even Death is sorely afraid, Death who devours gods, demons and all that moves and does not move.
Never make an enemy of him. At my word, give Sītā back.
sundar.22.do22: Śrī Rāma protects those who bow to him; he is an ocean of compassion, the slayer of Khara.
If you go to him for refuge, the Lord will forget your offences and keep you safe.
sundar.23.cau1: Keep the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma in your heart, and hold unshaken rule over Laṅkā.
The fame of the sage Pulastya is a spotless moon: do not become a blemish on that moon.
sundar.23.cau2: Without the name of Śrī Rāma speech has no beauty; put away pride and delusion, reflect and see.
Enemy of the gods, a fine woman decked with every ornament is not beautiful without clothes.
sundar.23.cau3: The wealth and power of one who has turned from Śrī Rāma slip away even as he holds them; to have them is as good as not having them.
Rivers with no spring at their source dry up the moment the rains have passed.
sundar.23.cau4: Listen, Rāvaṇa, I say this on oath: for one who turns from Śrī Rāma there is no protector at all.
Not even a thousand Śivas, Viṣṇus and Brahmās could save you, the enemy of Śrī Rāma.
sundar.23.do23: Give up the darkness of pride, which springs from delusion and brings much pain.
Worship the Lord Śrī Rāma, Lord of the Raghus and ocean of mercy.
sundar.24.cau1: Though Hanumān had spoken words for his highest good, steeped in devotion, discernment, dispassion and right counsel,
the arch-proud Rāvaṇa replied with a laugh: So we have found ourselves a monkey for a guru, and a very learned one.
sundar.24.cau2: Death has come close to you, wretch; that is why, vile creature, you set about teaching me.
Hanumān said: It will be the other way round; I have seen plainly that your mind is deluded.
sundar.24.cau3: Hearing Hanumān's words, Rāvaṇa was greatly vexed and said: Why do you not take this fool's life at once?
At this the demons ran to kill him, and just then Vibhīṣaṇa came with his ministers.
sundar.24.cau4: Bowing his head, he pleaded at length: Killing an envoy goes against right policy.
My lord, give him some other punishment. All of them said: Brother, that is sound advice.
sundar.24.cau5: On hearing this Rāvaṇa laughed and said: Maim the monkey and send him back.
sundar.24.do24: Let me make it clear to you all: a monkey's heart is set on its tail.
Steep cloth in oil, tie it round his tail, and then set it alight.
sundar.25.cau1: When the tailless monkey goes back there, the fool will bring his master here.
Let me see the might of the one he has praised so much.
sundar.25.cau2: Hearing this, Hanumān smiled to himself: I see that Sarasvatī has come to help.
The demons, hearing Rāvaṇa's words, set about that very plan, the fools.
sundar.25.cau3: Not a cloth, not a drop of ghee or oil was left in the city, yet the tail kept growing, for Hanumān was at play.
The townsfolk came to watch the fun; they kicked him and laughed at him a great deal.
sundar.25.cau4: Drums were beaten and all clapped their hands; after parading him through the city they set his tail alight.
Seeing the flames take hold, Hanumān at once made himself very small.
sundar.25.cau5: Hanumān slipped free of his bonds and climbed onto the golden upper storeys, and the demon women were frightened.
sundar.25.do25: At Śrī Hari's prompting, the forty-nine winds rose up at that very moment.
Hanumān gave a great laugh and roared, and grew until he touched the sky.
sundar.26.cau1: His body was huge yet utterly light, and he ran leaping from one mansion to the next.
The city burned and its people were in distress, as countless fearsome flames leapt and lunged.
sundar.26.cau2: Alas, father! Alas, mother! Such cries were heard: Who will save us now?
We said so: this is not a monkey at all; it is some god who has taken a monkey's form.
sundar.26.cau3: Such is the fruit of slighting a holy man: the city burned like a city with no one to protect it.
In the blink of an eye he burned the city down; only Vibhīṣaṇa's house did not burn.
sundar.26.cau4: He was the messenger of the one who created fire; that is why, Pārvatī, he did not burn.
Turning this way and that, he burned the whole of Laṅkā, and then leapt down into the middle of the ocean.
sundar.26.do26: He put out the fire on his tail, shook off his weariness, took a small form once more.
He stood with joined hands before Sītā, daughter of Janaka.
sundar.27.cau1: Mother, give me some token, as Śrī Rāma gave me one.
Then she took off her crest-jewel and gave it to him, and Hanumān, son of the Wind, received it with joy.
sundar.27.cau2: Dear son, give him my obeisance and say this: My Lord, you are in every way fulfilled, wanting nothing.
Keeping to your name as the one who is kind to the lowly, my Lord, take away my heavy affliction.
sundar.27.cau3: Dear son, tell the story of Jayanta, son of Indra, and make the Lord recall the might of his arrow.
Should my Lord not come within a month, he will find me alive no more.
sundar.27.cau4: Tell me, Hanumān, how am I to stay alive? Now you too, dear son, speak of going.
Seeing you brought my heart relief; now the same days and the same nights will be mine again.
sundar.27.do27: Hanumān comforted Sītā in many ways and gave her courage.
Then he bowed low at her lotus feet and set out to go to Śrī Rāma.
sundar.28.cau1: As he set out he gave a tremendous, thunderous roar; on hearing it, the demon women miscarried.
He leapt across the ocean, came to this shore, and let the monkeys hear his cry of joy.
sundar.28.cau2: All were overjoyed to see Hanumān; the monkeys felt then that they had been born again.
His face was glad and his body shone with splendour: he had done Śrī Rāma's work.
sundar.28.cau3: They all met him and were overjoyed, like a writhing fish that finds water.
Joyfully they set off towards Śrī Rāma, asking about and recounting all that had newly happened.
sundar.28.cau4: Then they all went into Madhuvana and, with Aṅgada's leave, ate the sweet fruit.
When the guards tried to stop them, they struck them with their fists, and the guards all ran away.
sundar.28.do28: They went and cried out: The crown prince is laying the grove waste.
Hearing it, Sugrīva rejoiced: the monkeys had come back with the Lord's work done.
sundar.29.cau1: Had they not found news of Sītā, could they have eaten Madhuvana's fruit?
The king was turning this over in his mind when the monkeys arrived with their whole company.
sundar.29.cau2: On arriving, they all bowed their heads at his feet, and the king of the monkeys greeted each of them with great love.
He asked how they fared; they said: Seeing your feet, all is well; by Śrī Rāma's grace the task has gone exceptionally well.
sundar.29.cau3: My lord, it was Hanumān who did the work, and he saved the lives of all the monkeys.
Hearing this, Sugrīva embraced him once more and set off with the monkeys to Śrī Rāma.
sundar.29.cau4: As Śrī Rāma watched the monkeys approach with the work done, his heart was filled with special joy.
The two brothers were sitting on a slab of crystal; every one of the monkeys went up and fell at their feet.
sundar.29.do29: Śrī Rāma, compassion embodied, embraced them all with love.
He asked after their welfare. They said: My Lord, we are well now, having looked upon your lotus feet.
sundar.30.cau1: Jāmbavān said: O Lord of the Raghus, listen.
One to whom you show mercy, my Lord, enjoys good fortune and well-being always and without end; gods, men and sages are pleased with him.
sundar.30.cau2: He alone is victorious and humble, an ocean of virtues, and his fair fame shines through the three worlds.
By the Lord's grace the whole task has been accomplished; today our birth has borne fruit.
sundar.30.cau3: My Lord, what the son of the Wind has done could not be told even with a thousand mouths.
Then Jāmbavān related to Śrī Rāma the splendid deeds of Hanumān.
sundar.30.cau4: As he heard them, they delighted the heart of the compassionate Lord, and joyfully he clasped Hanumān to his heart again and asked:
Tell me, dear one, how does Sītā live, and how does she keep herself alive?
sundar.30.do30: Your name keeps watch day and night, meditation on you is the door.
Her eyes, fixed on her own feet, are the lock: by what way could her life escape?
sundar.31.cau1: When I took my leave, she gave me her crest-jewel. Śrī Rāma received it and held it to his heart.
My Lord, with both her eyes full of tears, the daughter of Janaka spoke a few words.
sundar.31.cau2: Clasp the feet of the Lord and his younger brother. O friend of the lowly, you who take away the distress of those who bow to you:
in mind, deed and word I love your feet; what offence of mine, my Lord, has made you abandon me?
sundar.31.cau3: One fault of mine I admit: when I was parted from you, my life did not leave me.
But the offence, my Lord, lies with my eyes: they stubbornly stop my life as it tries to go out.
sundar.31.cau4: Separation is a fire, my body is cotton and my breath is the wind: the body would burn up in a moment.
But my eyes, for their own sake, keep shedding tears, so the fire of separation cannot burn my body.
sundar.31.cau5: Sītā's suffering is immense; O you who are compassionate to the lowly, it is better left untold.
sundar.31.do31: O treasury of compassion, every single moment passes for her like an aeon.
Set out quickly, my Lord, conquer the host of the wicked by the strength of your arms, and bring her back.
sundar.32.cau1: Hearing of Sītā's grief, the Lord, the abode of bliss, felt his lotus eyes fill with tears:
Can anyone who in word, body and mind has me for refuge meet with calamity even in a dream?
sundar.32.cau2: Hanumān said: My Lord, that alone is calamity, when one does not remember and worship you.
What does the demon count for, my Lord? You will conquer the enemy and bring Sītā back.
sundar.32.cau3: Listen, Hanumān: among gods, men and sages, no one who wears a body has done me such a service as you.
What can I do for you in return? My mind cannot even face you.
sundar.32.cau4: Listen, my son: I am not free of my debt to you; I have thought it over in my mind and seen that it is so.
Again and again the protector of the gods gazes at Hanumān; his eyes brim with tears and his whole body thrills.
sundar.32.do32: Hearing the Lord's words and seeing his face and his body, Hanumān was overjoyed;
overcome with love, he fell at his feet: Save me, save me, O Lord!
sundar.33.cau1: Again and again the Lord tries to raise him, but Hanumān, lost in love, has no wish to rise.
The Lord's lotus hand rests on Hanumān's head: recalling that scene, Śiva, the lord of Gaurī, was rapt.
sundar.33.cau2: Then, steadying his mind, Śaṅkara went on with the most beautiful story.
The Lord raised Hanumān, embraced him, and taking his hand seated him right beside himself.
sundar.33.cau3: Tell me, Hanumān: Laṅkā, guarded by Rāvaṇa, is a most formidable fortress; how did you burn it?
Seeing that the Lord was pleased, Hanumān spoke these words, free of all pride.
sundar.33.cau4: The great prowess of a monkey is just this: he goes from one branch to another.
That I leapt across the ocean and burnt the city of gold, slew hosts of demons and laid waste the grove,
sundar.33.cau5: All of that was your glorious power, O Lord of the Raghus; none of it, my Lord, was any greatness of mine.
sundar.33.do33: My Lord, nothing is out of reach for one to whom you are favourable.
By your power, cotton can indeed burn up the fire beneath the ocean.
sundar.34.cau1: My Lord, be gracious and grant me devotion that gives the greatest joy and never fails.
Hearing Hanumān's utterly guileless words, Pārvatī, the Lord then said: So be it.
sundar.34.cau2: Umā, one who has come to know Śrī Rāma's nature cares for nothing but worship.
Whoever takes this dialogue to heart has won devotion to the feet of Śrī Rāma.
sundar.34.cau3: Hearing the Lord's words, the hosts of monkeys cry: Glory, glory, glory to the compassionate Lord, the root of joy!
Then Śrī Rāma summoned the monkey king Sugrīva and told him: Prepare to march.
sundar.34.cau4: Why should there be any delay now? Give the monkeys their orders at once.
Seeing this wonder, the gods rained down flowers in plenty and, rejoicing, went from the sky to their homes.
sundar.34.do34: The king of the monkeys sent for them at once, and the troop leaders came in throngs:
hosts of monkeys and bears of many colours and matchless strength.
sundar.35.cau1: They bow their heads at the lotus feet of the Lord; the mighty bears and monkeys roar.
Śrī Rāma looked over the entire monkey army, turning his lotus eyes on it in grace.
sundar.35.cau2: Strengthened by Śrī Rāma's grace, the great monkeys seemed like mighty mountains that had grown wings.
Then Śrī Rāma joyfully set out, and many fair and auspicious omens appeared.
sundar.35.cau3: For one whose glory is wholly auspicious, it is only the rule that good omens attend his setting out.
Sītā learnt that the Lord had set out: her left limbs throbbed, as though telling her so.
sundar.35.cau4: Every good omen that came to Sītā was, for Rāvaṇa, an ill omen.
The army marched; who could describe it to the end? Monkeys and bears beyond number roar.
sundar.35.cau5: Their nails are their weapons; bearing mountains and trees, they move as they please through the sky and over the earth.
The bears and monkeys roar like lions; the elephants of the quarters stagger and trumpet.
sundar.35.cha1: The elephants of the quarters trumpet, the earth sways, the mountains rock and the oceans heave.
The gandharvas, the gods, the sages, the nāgas and the kinnaras rejoice at heart; their sorrows are over.
Fierce monkey warriors gnash their teeth, and many millions upon millions rush onward;
with cries of glory to Śrī Rāma of mighty majesty they sing the many virtues of the Lord of Kosala.
sundar.35.cha2: Śeṣa, the noble lord of serpents, cannot bear the weight and swoons again and again;
again and again he grips the hard back of the tortoise with his teeth. How fine he looks!
It is as if, knowing Śrī Rāma's splendid march to be a most lovely setting-forth,
the king of serpents were inscribing it, unfading and holy, on the tortoise's shell.
sundar.35.do35: In this way the Lord, the treasury of mercy, went and made camp on the shore of the ocean,
and the many heroic bears and monkeys began to eat fruit here and there.
sundar.36.cau1: Over there, ever since Hanumān burnt Laṅkā and went away, the demons have lived in dread.
In their homes they all think: there is no saving the race of demons.
sundar.36.cau2: When he whose messenger's strength is beyond description comes himself, what good can come to the city?
Hearing the townspeople's talk from her messengers, Mandodarī grew all the more distressed.
sundar.36.cau3: In private, with joined palms, she fell at her husband's feet and spoke words steeped in wise counsel:
My husband, give up your hostility to Śrī Hari; take to heart what I say, for it is greatly for your good.
sundar.36.cau4: His messenger's deeds, when they so much as think of them, make the demons' wives miscarry.
Call your minister and send his wife back in the minister's care, my husband, if you wish for your own good.
sundar.36.cau5: To the lotus-forest of your race Sītā has come like a winter night, bringing it grief.
Listen, my lord: unless you give Sītā back, not even Śiva and Brahmā can do you any good.
sundar.36.do36: The arrows of Śrī Rāma are like a host of snakes, and the throng of demons like frogs.
Before they swallow them up, give up your obstinacy and make some effort.
sundar.37.cau1: The wicked one heard her words, and he, notorious throughout the world for his arrogance, laughed:
Truly, a woman's nature is timid; even in good times she is afraid; her heart is very faint.
sundar.37.cau2: If the monkey army comes, the poor demons will have something to eat and live on.
That the wife of one in terror of whom the guardians of the worlds tremble should be afraid is a great joke.
sundar.37.cau3: With these words he laughed, clasped her to his breast and, showing her still greater affection, went off to the assembly.
Mandodarī was anxious at heart, thinking that fate had turned against her husband.
sundar.37.cau4: As he sat in the assembly, news reached him that the whole army had come to the far shore of the ocean.
He asked his ministers: Tell me what course is right. They all laughed: Simply stay silent and at ease.
sundar.37.cau5: When you conquered gods and demons it cost you no effort; what do men and monkeys count for?
sundar.37.do37: If minister, physician and guru, these three, speak pleasing words out of fear or hope,
then kingdom, dharma and body, these three, soon perish.
sundar.38.cau1: That very state of things had come about for Rāvaṇa: his ministers praise him, making sure he hears it.
Seeing his opportunity, Vibhīṣaṇa came and laid his head at the feet of his brother.
sundar.38.cau2: Then, with another bow, he sat down in his own seat and, once given leave, spoke:
Gracious one, since you have asked me for my counsel, I speak for your good, dear brother, as far as my understanding allows.
sundar.38.cau3: One who wishes for his own welfare, good fame, good sense, a happy destiny and joys of many kinds,
he should turn away, my lord, from the forehead of another man's wife, as one turns away from the moon of the fourth day.
sundar.38.cau4: Though one be sole lord of the fourteen worlds, he does not last if he is at enmity with living beings.
A man may be an ocean of virtues and accomplished, yet if he has even a little greed, no one calls him good.
sundar.38.do38: Desire, anger, pride and greed are all, my lord, paths to hell.
Give them all up and worship Śrī Rāma, whom the saints worship.
sundar.39.cau1: Dear brother, Śrī Rāma is not merely a king of men: he is lord of all the worlds, the Death even of Death.
He is Brahman, the Lord, free from all ills and unborn, all-pervading, unconquerable, without beginning and without end.
sundar.39.cau2: The ocean of mercy, who works for the good of the earth, the brāhmaṇas, the cows and the gods, has taken a human body.
He delights his devotees, destroys the hosts of the wicked and guards the Vedas and dharma. Listen, brother.
sundar.39.cau3: Give up your enmity and bow your head to him; Śrī Rāma ends the suffering of all who bow to him.
My lord, give Sītā back to the Lord, and worship Śrī Rāma, who loves without any motive.
sundar.39.cau4: The Lord does not cast off even one who carries the sin of having wronged the whole world, once he goes to him for refuge.
The very Lord whose name ends the three afflictions has appeared; understand this in your heart, Rāvaṇa.
sundar.39.do39क: Rāvaṇa, I fall at your feet over and over and entreat you:
cast off pride, delusion and arrogance, and worship the Lord of Kosala.
sundar.39.do39ख: The sage Pulastya sent this message by way of his own disciple.
Dear brother, finding a good moment, I have told it straight away to you, my lord.
sundar.40.cau1: Mālyavān was a minister of great wisdom. He was much pleased to hear these words, and said:
Dear one, your younger brother is an ornament of good counsel; take to heart what Vibhīṣaṇa is saying.
sundar.40.cau2: Rāvaṇa said: These two fools are praising the enemy. Will no one take them away? Is anyone there?
Mālyavān then went home, and Vibhīṣaṇa, joining his palms, spoke again:
sundar.40.cau3: Good sense and ill sense dwell in every heart, my lord; so say the Purāṇas and the Vedas.
Where there is good sense, there is prosperity of every kind; where there is ill sense, calamity comes in the end.
sundar.40.cau4: A perverse ill sense has settled in your heart, so you take a well-wisher for a foe and an enemy for a friend.
Sītā is the night of doom for the race of demons, and it is she whom you love so greatly.
sundar.40.do40: Dear brother, I clasp your feet and ask you: grant this for love of me.
Give Sītā to Śrī Rāma, so that no harm comes to you.
sundar.41.cau1: Vibhīṣaṇa spoke words of right counsel, in agreement with the wise, the Purāṇas and the Vedas.
On hearing them, Rāvaṇa rose in fury and said: Wretch, your death is now close at hand.
sundar.41.cau2: Fool, you have always lived because I let you live, and yet, simpleton, you favour the enemy's side.
Tell me, wretch: who is there in the world whom I have not conquered by the strength of my arms?
sundar.41.cau3: You live in my city and love those ascetics. Fool, go and join them, and preach your counsel to them.
With these words he kicked him, and his younger brother clasped his feet again and again.
sundar.41.cau4: Umā, this is the greatness of a saint: he does good even to one who does him harm.
Vibhīṣaṇa said: You stand in a father's place for me; you were right to strike me. But it is in worshipping Śrī Rāma that your good lies, my lord.
sundar.41.cau5: With his ministers, Vibhīṣaṇa rose into the sky and went off, saying this for all to hear:
sundar.41.do41: Śrī Rāma is the Lord whose resolve always comes true, and your court is in the grip of death.
I go now to take refuge with Śrī Rāma; do not lay the blame on me.
sundar.42.cau1: As soon as Vibhīṣaṇa set off, saying this, all of them were doomed to die.
Pārvatī, scorn shown to a holy man at once destroys every good.
sundar.42.cau2: The moment Rāvaṇa cast Vibhīṣaṇa off, the luckless king lost all his splendour.
Vibhīṣaṇa set out joyfully for Śrī Rāma, cherishing many hopes in his heart.
sundar.42.cau3: I shall go and see those lotus feet, rosy and soft, that bring joy to his servants:
the feet whose touch saved the sage's wife, Ahalyā, and which made the Daṇḍaka forest holy.
sundar.42.cau4: The feet that Sītā, Janaka's daughter, holds to her heart, that ran over the ground after the deceitful deer,
that bloom as lotuses in the lake that is Śiva's heart: what good fortune! I shall see those very feet.
sundar.42.do42: The feet on whose sandals Bharata has set his mind:
today I shall go and behold those feet with these eyes of mine.
sundar.43.cau1: Thinking such loving thoughts, Vibhīṣaṇa soon reached this shore of the ocean.
The monkeys saw him approaching and thought he must be an important envoy of the enemy.
sundar.43.cau2: Keeping him there, they went to the king of the monkeys and reported everything to him.
Sugrīva said: O Lord of the Raghus, hear this: Rāvaṇa's brother is here to meet you.
sundar.43.cau3: The Lord said: Friend, what do you make of it? The king of the monkeys said: Listen, O king of men:
no one can see through the wiles of the demons. Who knows why this shape-changer has come?
sundar.43.cau4: The wretch has come to learn our secrets; I think we should keep him in bonds.
The Lord said: Friend, you have weighed the policy well, but I am pledged to remove the fear of whoever comes to me for refuge.
sundar.43.cau5: Hanumān rejoiced at the Lord's words: the Lord is loving to those who seek his refuge.
sundar.43.do43: Those who abandon one who has come to them for refuge, judging that he may do them harm,
they are base and full of sin; there is harm in even looking at them.
sundar.44.cau1: Even one who bears the guilt of killing millions of brāhmaṇas I do not abandon once he comes to me for refuge.
The moment a soul turns to face me, the sins of millions of births are destroyed.
sundar.44.cau2: It is the very nature of a sinner that worship of me never pleases him.
If he were truly wicked at heart, would he come before me?
sundar.44.cau3: Only one whose mind is pure finds me; deceit, cunning and fault-finding do not please me.
Should Rāvaṇa have sent him here to learn our secrets, still, king of the monkeys, we have nothing to fear and nothing to lose.
sundar.44.cau4: Friend, Lakṣmaṇa can kill in the blink of an eye every demon there is in the world.
And if he has come to me for refuge out of fear, I will guard him as I guard my own life.
sundar.44.do44: The abode of mercy said with a smile: Bring him in either case.
Crying victory to the compassionate Lord, Sugrīva set off, taking Aṅgada and Hanumān with him.
sundar.45.cau1: Respectfully placing him in front, the monkeys went to where Śrī Rāma, the mine of compassion, was.
From far off Vibhīṣaṇa saw the two brothers, who give the gift of joy to the eyes.
sundar.45.cau2: Then, as he looked upon Śrī Rāma, abode of all beauty, he stood rooted, gazing unblinking, his eyelids held still.
The Lord's arms were long, his eyes like red lotuses, his body dark, freeing from fear those who bow to him.
sundar.45.cau3: His shoulders were like a lion's and his broad chest shone; his face would charm the hearts of countless gods of love.
Vibhīṣaṇa's eyes filled with tears and his whole body thrilled; steadying his mind, he spoke gently:
sundar.45.cau4: My Lord, I am the brother of Rāvaṇa, and was born in the race of demons, O protector of the gods.
By nature I am fond of sin, and my body is of the dark quality (tamas), as the owl loves the darkness.
sundar.45.do45: I have come, Lord, having heard with my ears your fair fame, that you destroy the distress of worldly existence.
Save me, save me, remover of suffering, giver of joy to those who seek refuge, O hero of the Raghus.
sundar.46.cau1: Seeing him prostrate himself after these words, the Lord rose at once, full of joy.
The humble words pleased the Lord's heart; he gathered him in his mighty arms and held him to his heart.
sundar.46.cau2: Meeting him together with his younger brother, he seated him close by, and the Lord, who takes away his devotees' fear, said:
Tell me, Lord of Laṅkā, how you and your family are; you live in an evil place.
sundar.46.cau3: You dwell day and night among a company of the wicked; how do you keep to dharma, friend?
Your ways are all known to me: you are deeply versed in right conduct, and wrong does not please you.
sundar.46.cau4: Even a dwelling in hell is better, dear one; may the Creator never grant the company of the wicked.
Vibhīṣaṇa said: O Lord of the Raghus, now that I have seen your feet I am well, for you have shown me mercy, knowing me as your servant.
sundar.46.do46: A soul knows no well-being, and its mind no rest even in a dream,
until it gives up desire, the home of sorrow, and worships Śrī Rāma.
sundar.47.cau1: Many wicked ones, greed, delusion, envy, pride and vanity, dwell in the heart
for as long as Śrī Rāma, holding his bow and arrows, with a quiver at his waist, does not dwell there.
sundar.47.cau2: Attachment is a pitch-dark night at its height, which delights the owls of craving and aversion.
It lives in a soul's mind only until the Lord's majesty rises there like the sun.
sundar.47.cau3: Now I am well and my great fears are gone, O Rāma, for my eyes have seen your lotus feet.
O compassionate Lord, the one to whom you are gracious is never touched by the three kinds of worldly pain.
sundar.47.cau4: I am a demon of very base nature and have never done a good deed.
Yet the Lord, whose form does not come even into the meditation of sages, has joyfully clasped me to his heart.
sundar.47.do47: What good fortune is mine, boundless beyond measure, O Rāma, mass of grace and joy:
with my own eyes I have seen the pair of lotus feet that Brahmā and Śiva serve.
sundar.48.cau1: Listen, friend: I tell you my own nature, which Kākabhuśuṇḍi, Śiva and Pārvatī know.
If a man who is the enemy of all creation, moving and unmoving, comes in fear, looking to me for refuge,
sundar.48.cau2: and leaves behind pride, delusion, deceit and guile of every kind, I make him at once like a saint.
Mother, father, brother, son, wife, body, wealth, house, friends and family:
sundar.48.cau3: one who gathers up the threads of attachment to all of these, twists them into a cord and with it ties his mind to my feet;
who sees all with an equal eye, wants nothing at all, and whose mind holds no joy, grief or fear —
sundar.48.cau4: such a good man lives in my heart just as wealth lives in the heart of the greedy.
Saints like you are dear to me; it is for no one else's sake that I take on a body.
sundar.48.do48: Those who worship God with form and attributes, who are intent on the good of others and firm in right conduct and in their observances:
such men, who love the feet of brāhmaṇas, are as dear to me as my own life.
sundar.49.cau1: Listen, lord of Laṅkā: all these virtues are yours, and so you are exceedingly dear to me.
Hearing Śrī Rāma's words, all the troops of monkeys cry: Glory to the sum of all mercy!
sundar.49.cau2: As Vibhīṣaṇa listens to the Lord's words he cannot have enough of them, knowing them to be nectar to the ears.
Again and again he clasps the Lord's lotus feet; the boundless love in his heart cannot be held within it.
sundar.49.cau3: Listen, my Lord, master of all that moves and does not move, protector of those who bow before you, you who know every heart from within:
at first there was some desire in my heart, but it has been carried away by the river of love for the Lord's feet.
sundar.49.cau4: Now, compassionate Lord, give me devotion to you, which makes one pure and is ever dear to Śiva's mind.
The Lord, unshaken in battle, said: So be it, and at once called for water from the ocean.
sundar.49.cau5: Friend, though you have no desire, the sight of me never fails to bear fruit in this world.
With these words Śrī Rāma anointed him with the tilaka, and a boundless shower of flowers fell from the sky.
sundar.49.do49क: Vibhīṣaṇa was burning in the fire of Rāvaṇa's anger, which the fierce wind of his own breath had fanned;
Śrī Rāma saved him and gave him a kingdom that would never be broken.
sundar.49.do49ख: The wealth that Śiva gave Rāvaṇa when he offered up his ten heads,
that same wealth Śrī Rāma gave to Vibhīṣaṇa, and gave it with diffidence.
sundar.50.cau1: Those who leave such a Lord and worship another are beasts without tail or horns.
Knowing Vibhīṣaṇa for his own devotee, the Lord took him as his own; and the Lord's nature delighted the whole monkey race.
sundar.50.cau2: Then the Lord, who knows all and dwells in every heart, who is every form and yet free of all and detached,
the upholder of right counsel, who for a purpose became a man and destroys the race of demons, spoke these words:
sundar.50.cau3: Listen, heroes, king of the monkeys and lord of Laṅkā: how is this deep ocean to be crossed?
It teems with crocodiles, serpents and fish of every kind; it is fathomless, and hard to cross in every way.
sundar.50.cau4: Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, said: O Lord of the Raghus, listen. Your arrow could dry up ten million oceans.
Even so, policy teaches that one should go to the Ocean and make a humble request.
sundar.50.do50: My Lord, the Ocean is a revered elder of your line. He will think it over and tell you a way,
and the entire army of bears and monkeys will get across the ocean without effort.
sundar.51.cau1: Friend, the way you have told me is a good one; let it be tried, if fate is on our side.
This counsel did not please Lakṣmaṇa; hearing Śrī Rāma's words, he was deeply troubled.
sundar.51.cau2: My Lord, what reliance can be placed on fate? Dry up the ocean; let your mind be roused to anger.
Fate is the one prop of a coward's mind; it is the idle who keep crying out, Fate, fate.
sundar.51.cau3: On hearing this Śrī Rāma laughed and said: That is just what I shall do; keep your mind steady.
With these words the Lord reassured his younger brother and went down to the ocean.
sundar.51.cau4: First he bowed his head in salutation; then he spread kuśa grass on the shore and sat down.
When Vibhīṣaṇa came to the Lord, Rāvaṇa had sent spies after him.
sundar.51.do51: Disguised in the bodies of monkeys, they watched all that took place,
and in their hearts they praised the virtues of the Lord and the love he bears for one who comes to him for refuge.
sundar.52.cau1: They began to praise Śrī Rāma's nature openly, and in their great love they forgot to keep up their disguise.
Then the monkeys knew them for the enemy's spies, tied them all up and took them before Sugrīva, king of the monkeys.
sundar.52.cau2: Sugrīva said: Listen, all you monkeys: mutilate these demons and send them back.
At Sugrīva's words the monkeys rushed at them, bound them and led them round the whole camp.
sundar.52.cau3: The monkeys began to beat them in many ways; though they cried out piteously, still the monkeys would not release them.
Then they cried: Whoever cuts off our noses and ears, we charge him by the Lord of Kosala.
sundar.52.cau4: Hearing this, Lakṣmaṇa called them all to him. He was moved to pity, and with a laugh had them set free at once, and said:
Put this letter into Rāvaṇa's hand and tell him: Read Lakṣmaṇa's words, you destroyer of your own race.
sundar.52.do52: And give that fool my generous message by word of mouth:
Hand Sītā back and come and meet Śrī Rāma, or else your death has come.
sundar.53.cau1: At once the spies bowed their heads at Lakṣmaṇa's feet and set out, recounting a tale of virtues.
Telling of Śrī Rāma's glory all the way, they came to Laṅkā and bowed their heads at Rāvaṇa's feet.
sundar.53.cau2: Rāvaṇa laughed and asked: Śuka, why don't you tell me how you are?
Then give me news of Vibhīṣaṇa, whose death has drawn very near.
sundar.53.cau3: The fool gave up Laṅkā, where he lived in royal state; now the wretch will be crushed like a weevil in the barley.
Then tell me about the army of bears and monkeys: cruel death has impelled it to march here.
sundar.53.cau4: That poor soft-hearted Ocean has become the guardian of their lives.
And then tell me about those ascetics, whose hearts are full of dread of me.
sundar.53.do53: Have you met them, or did they turn back as soon as my fair fame reached their ears?
Why don't you tell me of the might and splendour of the enemy's army? Your mind seems utterly dazed.
sundar.54.cau1: My lord, as graciously as you have asked, so accept what I tell you, setting your anger aside.
When your younger brother went over to them, Rāma anointed him with the tilaka the moment he arrived.
sundar.54.cau2: As soon as the monkeys heard we were spies sent by Rāvaṇa, they tied us up and made us suffer in many ways.
They started cutting off our ears and noses, and only when we bound them by an oath in Rāma's name did they let us go.
sundar.54.cau3: You asked about Rāma's army, my lord: a thousand million mouths could not describe it.
Its bears and monkeys are of many colours, with fearsome faces, huge and terrifying.
sundar.54.cau4: He who burned the city and killed your son has the least strength of all those monkeys.
There are warriors of countless names, tough and terrible, huge and mighty, with the strength of countless elephants.
sundar.54.do54: Among them are Dvivida and Mainda, Nīla and Nala, Aṅgada and Gada, Vikaṭāsya
and Dadhimukha, Kesarī, Niśaṭha and Śaṭha, and Jāmbavān — every one of them a mountain of strength.
sundar.55.cau1: All these monkeys are equal to Sugrīva, and there are millions like them; who could count so many?
By Rāma's grace their strength is beyond compare; they think of the three worlds as no more than a blade of grass.
sundar.55.cau2: This I have heard with my own ears, Rāvaṇa: the monkey troop-leaders number eighteen padmas (a padma being an immense number).
In that army, my lord, there is no monkey who would not defeat you in battle.
sundar.55.cau3: In utter fury they all wring their hands, but Rāma gives them no order.
They will dry up the ocean, fish, serpents and all, or else fill it in with great mountains,
sundar.55.cau4: and crush Rāvaṇa and grind him into the dust: such are the words all the monkeys speak.
Fearless by nature, they roar and threaten, as though they longed to swallow Laṅkā whole.
sundar.55.do55: The monkeys and bears are all heroes by nature, and over their heads besides is the Lord Rāma.
Rāvaṇa, they could conquer ten million Deaths in battle.
sundar.56.cau1: The splendour, strength and wisdom of Rāma are so vast that a hundred thousand Śeṣas (the thousand-headed serpent) could not sing of them.
He can dry up a hundred oceans with a single arrow, yet, skilled in policy as he is, he asked your brother's counsel.
sundar.56.cau2: On his advice he is asking the Ocean for a way across, with mercy in his heart.
Hearing this, Rāvaṇa laughed: With wits like these, no wonder he has made monkeys his allies.
sundar.56.cau3: Relying on the word of a born coward, he has taken to sulking and pestering the Ocean like a spoilt child.
Fool, why do you sing false praises? I have taken the measure of my enemy's strength and wit.
sundar.56.cau4: Where in the world can victory and glory be found for one whose counsellor is the timid Vibhīṣaṇa?
At these words of the wicked one the spy grew angrier, and judging the moment right, he drew out the letter.
sundar.56.cau5: Rāma's younger brother gave me this letter. My lord, have it read out and let it cool your breast.
Rāvaṇa laughed and took it in his left hand, and the fool called his minister and had him begin to read it.
sundar.56.do56क: Fool, do not humour your mind with mere talk and so bring your race to ruin.
Opposing Śrī Rāma, you will find no escape, even if you take refuge with Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Śiva.
sundar.56.do56ख: Either give up your pride and, like your younger brother, become a bee at the Lord's lotus feet,
or else, wicked one, become a moth with all your race in the flame of Śrī Rāma's arrows.
sundar.57.cau1: Hearing the letter, Rāvaṇa was afraid at heart, but with a smile on his face he said for all to hear:
Like someone lying flat on the ground reaching up to seize the sky: such is the big talk of the younger ascetic.
sundar.57.cau2: Śuka said: My lord, every word of it is true; set aside your proud nature and understand it.
Put away your anger and hear what I say: my lord, give up your enmity with Śrī Rāma.
sundar.57.cau3: Śrī Rāma's nature is very gentle, though he is king of all the worlds.
The moment you meet him the Lord will show you grace; he will not keep a single offence of yours in his heart.
sundar.57.cau4: Hand Sītā over to Śrī Rāma; my lord, do this much that I ask.
When Śuka spoke of giving Sītā back, the wicked Rāvaṇa kicked him.
sundar.57.cau5: Śuka bowed his head to Rāvaṇa's feet and went to where Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, was.
He bowed to him and told his story, and by Śrī Rāma's grace he regained his own true state.
sundar.57.cau6: Pārvatī, by the curse of the sage Agastya he had become a demon; before that he had been a wise sage.
Bowing again and again at Śrī Rāma's feet, the sage went back to his hermitage.
sundar.57.do57: The dull Ocean would not heed the entreaty, and three days went by.
Then Śrī Rāma said in anger: Without fear there is no love.
sundar.58.cau1: Lakṣmaṇa, bring the bow and arrows; let me dry up the ocean with the fire of an arrow.
Entreaty to the wicked, love for the crooked, fine counsel to one who is a miser by nature,
sundar.58.cau2: talk of wisdom to one wrapped up in attachment, praise of dispassion to the very greedy,
talk of calm to the wrathful and the story of Śrī Hari to the lustful: all these bear the same fruit as seed sown in barren ground.
sundar.58.cau3: With these words Śrī Rāma strung his bow, and this view pleased Lakṣmaṇa.
The Lord fitted a terrible arrow, and flames rose within the ocean's heart.
sundar.58.cau4: Crocodiles, serpents and shoals of fish were thrown into distress. When the Ocean knew that the creatures were burning,
he filled a golden platter with gems of many kinds and, setting aside his pride, came in the form of a brāhmaṇa.
sundar.58.do58: However much one waters it, with endless care, a banana plant bears fruit only when it is cut.
Listen, Garuḍa: the base do not heed a humble request; they bend only when rebuked.
sundar.59.cau1: The Ocean, afraid, took hold of the Lord's feet: Forgive all my faults, my Lord.
Sky, wind, fire, water and earth, my Lord, are by their very nature dull in what they do.
sundar.59.cau2: Impelled by you, māyā brought them forth for the work of creation; so all the scriptures sing.
Whatever the Lord has commanded for each, each finds happiness in keeping to it.
sundar.59.cau3: My Lord, you did well to teach me a lesson; yet the bounds were set by you as well.
A drum, the unlettered, a śūdra, an animal and a woman: all of these are meant to receive instruction.
sundar.59.cau4: Through the Lord's might I shall dry up, and the army will get across, but there is no glory for me in that.
The Lord's command cannot be set aside, the Vedas sing; whatever pleases you, I will do it at once.
sundar.59.do59: Hearing these most humble words, the compassionate Lord smiled and said:
Dear one, tell me the way by which the monkey army may cross.
sundar.60.cau1: My Lord, the monkeys Nīla and Nala are two brothers who received a sage's blessing in childhood.
At their touch, even massive mountains will float upon the ocean through your glory.
sundar.60.cau2: I too, holding the Lord's greatness in my heart, will help as far as my strength allows.
Have the ocean bridged in this manner, my Lord, so that the three worlds may sing this fair renown.
sundar.60.cau3: With this arrow, my Lord, slay the wicked men who live on my northern shore, heaps of sin that they are.
Hearing of the pain in the Ocean's heart, the compassionate Śrī Rāma, steadfast in battle, took it away at once.
sundar.60.cau4: Seeing Śrī Rāma's mighty strength and valour, the Ocean rejoiced and was at ease.
He told the Lord all the deeds of those wicked men, bowed at his feet and departed.
sundar.60.cha1: The Ocean went to his own home, and this counsel pleased Śrī Rāma.
This story washes away the impurity of the Kali age; the servant Tulasīdāsa has sung it as far as his understanding allows.
The virtues of Śrī Rāma are a home of happiness; they put doubt to rest and destroy sorrow.
Foolish mind, let go of every hope and every reliance, and sing and hear them always.
sundar.60.do60: Singing the praises of Śrī Rāma brings every blessing.
Whoever listens to them with reverence crosses the ocean of worldly existence without a boat.
lanka.0.shloka1: I bow to Śrī Rāma, whom Śiva, the foe of Kāma, worships, who takes away the fear of worldly existence and is a lion to the maddened elephant of Death;
the lord of yogīs, reached through knowledge, the treasury of virtues, unconquered, beyond attributes and changeless;
beyond māyā (the Lord's power of illusion), lord of the gods, intent on slaying the wicked, the one God of the assembled brāhmaṇas;
fair as a rain-laden cloud, lotus-eyed, God in the form of a king of the earth.
lanka.0.shloka2: I praise Śaṅkara, whose most beautiful body gleams like a conch and the moon, who wears a tiger's skin,
who is adorned with serpents dreadful as Death, and to whom the Gaṅgā and the moon are dear;
the lord of Kāśī, who quells the flood of the sins of the Kali age, the wish-fulfilling tree of all that is good;
worthy of praise, the husband of Girijā, the treasury of virtues, the destroyer of Kāma.
lanka.0.shloka3: Śambhu, who grants the good even liberation, so hard to attain,
and who punishes the wicked: may that Śaṅkara spread blessing upon me.
lanka.0.dou1: The instant, the twinkling of an eye, the atom of time, the age, the year and the aeon are his fierce arrows,
and Time is his bow: why, my mind, do you not worship that Śrī Rāma?
lanka.0.sou1: Hearing the Ocean's words, the Lord Śrī Rāma called his ministers and said:
What use is delay now? Make a bridge for the army to cross by.
lanka.0.sou2: Jāmbavān, with joined palms, said: Listen, O banner of the solar race.
My Lord, your name is a bridge; mounting it, people cross the ocean of worldly existence.
lanka.1.cau1: How long can it take to cross this little ocean? Hearing this, Hanumān, son of the Wind, said:
The Lord's glory is a mighty submarine fire; long ago it drank up the ocean's water.
lanka.1.cau2: Then it was filled again by the streams of tears wept by your enemies' wives, and that made it salt.
Hearing this hyperbole of Hanumān's, the monkeys looked towards Śrī Rāma and were delighted.
lanka.1.cau3: Jāmbavān summoned the brothers Nala and Nīla, told them all that had passed, and said:
Remember Śrī Rāma's glory in your minds and build the bridge; it will cost you no labour.
lanka.1.cau4: Then he called together the hosts of monkeys and said: Listen, all of you, to a small request of mine.
Hold Śrī Rāma's lotus feet in your hearts, bears and monkeys, and play a game.
lanka.1.cau5: Run, you formidable troops of monkeys, and bring trees and mountains by the heap.
Hearing this, the monkeys and bears set off with a roar, crying: Glory to the hero of the Raghus, the treasure-house of might!
lanka.1.do1: Mountains and trees of great height they lift as if in play,
and bring and give them to Nala and Nīla, who shape them well and build the bridge.
lanka.2.cau1: The monkeys bring huge mountains, and Nala and Nīla catch them like balls.
Seeing the bridge so beautifully built, the Lord, the treasury of mercy, smiled and said:
lanka.2.cau2: This land is supremely lovely and excellent; its boundless glory cannot be described.
I will install Śiva here; that is the dearest wish of my heart.
lanka.2.cau3: Hearing this, Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, sent out many messengers, who summoned all the great sages and brought them.
Śrī Rāma installed the liṅga, worshipped it with due rites, and said: No one is as dear to me as Śiva.
lanka.2.cau4: One who is hostile to Śiva and calls himself my devotee will not reach me even in a dream.
One who turns away from Śaṅkara and yet wants devotion to me is bound for hell, a fool of little understanding.
lanka.2.do2: Those to whom Śaṅkara is dear but who are hostile to me, and those hostile to Śiva who are my servants,
dwell in a terrible hell for a whole aeon.
lanka.3.cau1: Those who behold Rāmeśvara will leave the body and go to my realm.
And one who brings Gaṅgā water and offers it to him will attain sāyujya, the liberation of union with me.
lanka.3.cau2: One who serves him free of desire and without guile will be given devotion to me by Śaṅkara.
Whoever looks upon the bridge I have built will cross the ocean of worldly existence without effort.
lanka.3.cau3: Śrī Rāma's words pleased everyone at heart, and the great sages went back each to his own hermitage.
Pārvatī, this is the way of Śrī Rāma: he always loves those who bow before him.
lanka.3.cau4: The skilful Nīla and Nala built the bridge, and by Śrī Rāma's grace their fame shone bright.
Stones that sink and drag others down became like ships.
lanka.3.cau5: This wonder is not set down to the ocean's credit; nor is it the stones' own property, nor the monkeys' doing.
lanka.3.do3: By the glory of Śrī Rāma, stones floated on the ocean.
Dull of mind are those who forsake Śrī Rāma and go to worship some other lord.
lanka.4.cau1: The bridge was built and made very strong, and the sight of it pleased the Lord, the treasury of mercy.
The army set out, beyond all description, and the hosts of monkey warriors roared.
lanka.4.cau2: Climbing up beside the bridgehead, the compassionate Śrī Rāma gazed at the vastness of the ocean.
To see the Lord, the source of compassion, all the hosts of sea creatures rose into view.
lanka.4.cau3: There were sea monsters, crocodiles, fish of many kinds and serpents, with huge bodies a hundred yojanas long.
Some were such as could swallow even these, and even they lived in fear of yet others.
lanka.4.cau4: They gazed at the Lord and would not move even when driven off; their hearts were glad and all were happy.
They hid the water from sight, lost in wonder as they beheld the form of Śrī Hari.
lanka.4.cau5: On the Lord's command the army moved off; who could tell how vast the monkey host was?
lanka.4.do4: The bridge grew so crowded that some monkeys flew by the path of the sky;
others climbed onto the sea creatures and crossed over on them.
lanka.5.cau1: Seeing this sport, the two brothers, the compassionate Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, set out smiling.
Śrī Rāma crossed over with the army; the throng of monkey chiefs was past all telling.
lanka.5.cau2: Across the ocean the Lord made camp and gave all the monkeys his command:
Go and eat the good fruit and roots. At this the bears and monkeys rushed off in every direction.
lanka.5.cau3: For Śrī Rāma's sake every tree bore fruit, in season or out, setting aside the course of time.
They ate the sweet fruit, shook the trees and hurled mountain peaks towards Laṅkā.
lanka.5.cau4: Wherever they found a demon wandering about, they would all surround him and lead him a merry dance;
then they bit off his nose and ears, told him of the Lord's fair fame, and only then let him go.
lanka.5.cau5: Those whose noses and ears had been cut off told Rāvaṇa all that had happened.
As soon as he heard that the ocean had been bridged, Rāvaṇa cried out in alarm with all ten mouths:
lanka.5.do5: Has he bound Vananidhi, Nīranidhi, Jaladhi, Sindhu and Vārīśa?
Has he truly bound Toyanidhi, Kampati, Udadhi, Payodhi and Nadīśa (all names of the ocean)?
lanka.6.cau1: Then, aware of his own agitation, he laughed it off, made light of his fear, and went home.
Mandodarī heard that the Lord had come and had had the ocean bridged as if in sport.
lanka.6.cau2: Taking her husband by the hand, she brought him to her own palace and spoke in the sweetest words.
With her head bowed at his feet she spread out the end of her sari and said: My love, set your anger aside and hear what I have to say.
lanka.6.cau3: My lord, enmity should be made only with one who can be beaten by wit or strength.
And what is the difference between you and Śrī Rāma? Truly, that between a firefly and the sun.
lanka.6.cau4: He who slew the mighty Madhu and Kaiṭabha and destroyed the great heroes, the sons of Diti;
who bound Bali and killed the thousand-armed Sahasrabāhu: he it is who has come down to take away the burden of the earth.
lanka.6.cau5: My lord, do not set yourself against him in whose hands lie time, karma and every living being.
lanka.6.do6: Bow your head at Śrī Rāma's lotus feet and give Sītā back to him.
Hand the kingdom over to your son, go to the forest and worship Śrī Rāma.
lanka.7.cau1: My lord, Śrī Rāma is merciful to the lowly; even a tiger will not eat one who comes before it.
All that you ought to do you have done; you have conquered gods, demons and all that moves and does not move.
lanka.7.cau2: Rāvaṇa, the saints teach this rule: in the fourth stage of life a king should go to the forest.
There, my husband, worship him who creates, sustains and destroys.
lanka.7.cau3: That same Śrī Rāma loves those who bow before him; worship him, my lord, giving up all attachment.
He for whom the great sages labour, and for whom kings renounce their thrones and become ascetics,
lanka.7.cau4: that same Lord of Kosala, Śrī Rāma, has come to show you mercy.
If you take my advice, my love, your fair fame will be supremely holy in all three worlds.
lanka.7.do7: So saying, her eyes brimming with tears, clasping his feet and trembling all over, she said:
My lord, worship Śrī Rāma, so that my good fortune as a wife may never fail.
lanka.8.cau1: Then Rāvaṇa raised Maya's daughter to her feet, and the wicked one began to boast of his power:
Listen, my dear, you are afraid for nothing. Who in all the world is a warrior to match me?
lanka.8.cau2: Varuṇa, Kubera, the Wind, Yama, Death and all the guardians of the quarters I have conquered by the strength of my arms.
Gods, demons and men are all in my power; what cause is there for you to be afraid?
lanka.8.cau3: He reassured her in many ways, then went back and took his seat in the council.
Mandodarī understood in her heart: he is in the grip of Death, and so this pride has risen in him.
lanka.8.cau4: Coming into the council, he asked his ministers: How shall we fight the enemy?
The ministers said: Listen, king of the demons. Why do you keep asking this, my lord?
lanka.8.cau5: Tell us, what is there to fear that needs any thought? Men, monkeys and bears are our food.
lanka.8.do8: Hearing what they all said, Prahasta spoke with joined palms:
My lord, do nothing against sound policy; your ministers have very little sense.
lanka.9.cau1: These foolish ministers say only what pleases their master; my lord, going on like this will not carry us through.
A single monkey leapt the ocean and came here, and everyone sang of his deeds in their hearts.
