lanka.9.cau2: Was none of you hungry then? When he was setting the city ablaze, why did none of you catch him and eat him?
Pleasant to hear but bringing sorrow later: such is the counsel these ministers have given their master.
lanka.9.cau3: He who in sport had the ocean bridged and has come down with his army on Mount Suvela —
tell me, brothers, is he a man, that we shall eat him? They all talk with puffed-out cheeks.
lanka.9.cau4: Father, hear what I say with full respect, and do not take me in your mind for a coward.
People who hear and speak pleasing words are found in crowds in this world.
lanka.9.cau5: But those who hear and speak words that are harsh to the ear yet supremely for one's good are few, my lord.
Listen to sound policy: first send an envoy, then give back Sītā and make friends.
lanka.9.do9: If they get the woman back and go home, do not prolong the quarrel;
if not, father, meet them face to face on the field of battle and strike them down without yielding.
lanka.10.cau1: My lord, if you accept this advice of mine, you will win good fame in the world either way.
Rāvaṇa said angrily to his son: Fool, who put such notions into your head?
lanka.10.cau2: Is doubt rising in your heart already? My son, you have turned out a blight at the root of the bamboo.
Hearing his father's harsh and terrible words, Prahasta set off for home, saying bitter words as he went:
lanka.10.cau3: How should good counsel take hold of you, any more than medicine of one in the grip of Death?
Seeing that it was evening, the ten-headed Rāvaṇa set off for his palace, gazing at his twenty arms.
lanka.10.cau4: On a peak of Laṅkā stood a mansion, where gatherings of dance and song, most wonderful, were held.
Rāvaṇa went and sat in that palace, and the kinnaras began to sing of his many virtues.
lanka.10.cau5: Cymbals, drums and vīṇās are playing, and skilled apsarās (heavenly dancers) dance.
lanka.10.do10: He lives in ceaseless pleasure, like a hundred Indras;
a most mighty enemy stands over his head, yet he feels neither worry nor fear.
lanka.11.cau1: Here Śrī Rāma came down on Mount Suvela with his army in a great throng.
He saw a very lofty peak, supremely lovely, level and especially bright.
lanka.11.cau2: There Lakṣmaṇa arranged and spread with his own hands tender shoots and lovely flowers from the trees.
Over them lies a fine, soft deerskin, and on that seat the compassionate Lord sits.
lanka.11.cau3: The Lord rests his head in the lap of Sugrīva, king of the monkeys; his bow lies on his left and his quiver on his right.
With both lotus hands he is setting an arrow straight, while Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, takes counsel close at his ear.
lanka.11.cau4: The fortunate Aṅgada and Hanumān are pressing his lotus feet in many ways.
Behind the Lord sits Lakṣmaṇa in the hero's posture, quiver at his waist, bow and arrow in his hands.
lanka.11.do11क: Thus sits Śrī Rāma, home of grace, beauty and virtue.
Blessed are those who remain ever absorbed in meditating on him thus.
lanka.11.do11ख: Looking to the east, the Lord saw that the moon had risen,
and said to them all: Look at the moon, fearless as a lion.
lanka.12.cau1: Dwelling in the mountain cave of the eastern quarter, a mass of supreme might, splendour and strength,
this lion, the moon, has torn open the brow of the maddened elephant of darkness and roams the forest of the sky.
lanka.12.cau2: The stars strewn across the sky are pearls, the adornment of the lovely lady Night.
The Lord said: Brothers, what is the darkness in the moon? Each of you tell me what you think.
lanka.12.cau3: Sugrīva said: Listen, O Lord of the Raghus: what shows in the moon is the shadow of the earth.
Someone said: Rāhu struck the moon, and that darkness still lies on its breast.
lanka.12.cau4: Another said: When Brahmā made Rati's face, he took away the moon's finest part.
That hole shows in the moon's heart, and through it the shadow of the sky is seen.
lanka.12.cau5: The Lord said: The moon's own brother is poison; it holds him very dear and has given him a home in its heart.
Spreading its host of poisoned rays, it scorches men and women parted from those they love.
lanka.12.do12क: Hanumān said: Listen, my Lord: the moon is your beloved servant.
Your image dwells in its heart, and that darkness is its reflection.
lanka.12.do12ख: Hearing the words of the son of the Wind, the all-wise Śrī Rāma smiled.
Then, looking towards the south, the Lord, the treasury of grace, said:
lanka.13.cau1: Look, Vibhīṣaṇa, at the southern quarter: clouds are massing and lightning plays.
The dark cloud thunders softly, sweetly; may no storm of hard hail follow.
lanka.13.cau2: Vibhīṣaṇa said: Listen, compassionate Lord: this is neither lightning nor a bank of clouds.
On a peak of Laṅkā stands a palace, where Rāvaṇa is watching a show of dance and song.
lanka.13.cau3: Over his head he bears a huge royal umbrella, dark as a cloud: that seems the black bank of cloud.
Mandodarī's earrings, my Lord, seem the flash of lightning.
lanka.13.cau4: Hear me, king of the gods: matchless cymbals and drums are beating there, and the sweet sound is theirs.
Seeing Rāvaṇa's pride, the Lord smiled; he strung his bow and set an arrow to it.
lanka.13.do13क: Then with a single arrow he struck down Rāvaṇa's umbrella and crowns and Mandodarī's earrings.
They fell to the ground before everyone's eyes, and no one knew the secret of it.
lanka.13.do13ख: Having played this wonder, Śrī Rāma's arrow came back and slipped into the quiver.
Seeing the revelry so badly spoiled, Rāvaṇa's whole assembly was filled with alarm.
lanka.14.cau1: The earth did not quake, nor did any strong wind blow; no eye saw missile or weapon.
Each of them thought anxiously within: a dreadful and grievous ill omen has occurred.
lanka.14.cau2: Seeing the assembly afraid, the ten-headed Rāvaṇa laughed and spoke words with a clever turn:
For one to whom even the falling of his heads has always been auspicious, how can falling crowns be an ill omen?
lanka.14.cau3: Go to your homes, each of you, and sleep. They all bowed their heads and went home.
Ever since the earring fell to the earth, anxiety had lodged in Mandodarī's heart.
lanka.14.cau4: With tears in her eyes and both palms joined, she said: Lord of my life, listen to my plea.
My husband, give up your hostility to Śrī Rāma; do not cling to your obstinacy, thinking him a man.
lanka.14.do14: Believe my words: the jewel of Raghu's line has the universe for his form;
the Vedas see a world in each and every limb of his.
lanka.15.cau1: Pātāla is his feet, the realm of Brahmā his head, and the other worlds rest on his various limbs;
the play of his brows is dread Death, the sun his eyes, and the banks of cloud his hair.
lanka.15.cau2: The Aśvins are his nostrils, and night and day the endless blinking of his eyes;
the ten directions are his ears, say the Vedas; the wind is his breath, and the Veda his own speech.
lanka.15.cau3: Greed is his lip, Yama his fearsome teeth; māyā is his laughter, the guardians of the quarters his arms;
fire is his mouth, Varuṇa his tongue; creation, preservation and dissolution are his activity.
lanka.15.cau4: The eighteen bhāras of plants (all vegetation) are the rows of hair on his body, the mountains his bones, the rivers the web of his veins;
his belly is the ocean, his lower organs the hells. The Lord is the whole world; why imagine any further?
lanka.15.do15क: His ego is Śiva, his intellect Brahmā, his mind the moon, and his citta (inner heart) the Great One (Viṣṇu);
that same Lord, Śrī Rāma, whose form is all that moves and does not move, dwells here as a man.
lanka.15.do15ख: Listen, lord of my life: weigh this, and give up your enmity with the Lord;
love the feet of Śrī Rāma, so that I am not made a widow.
lanka.16.cau1: Hearing his wife's words, Rāvaṇa laughed and said: Ah, how mighty is the power of delusion!
All say truly of a woman's nature that eight faults dwell in her heart always:
lanka.16.cau2: rashness, falsehood, fickleness, deceit, fear, lack of discernment, impurity and pitilessness.
You have sung of the enemy's whole form and told me of a very great fear.
lanka.16.cau3: My dear, all that is by its very nature under my control; by your favour I understand it now.
I have seen through your cleverness, dear: this is your way of telling of my greatness.
lanka.16.cau4: Your talk is deep, doe-eyed one: a joy to understand, and on hearing it fear is dispelled.
Mandodarī concluded in her mind that her husband was in the grip of Death, and so his reason had gone astray.
lanka.16.do16क: Amusing himself in many such ways, Rāvaṇa saw the morning come.
Fearless by nature and blind with pride, the lord of Laṅkā went to the assembly.
lanka.16.so16ख: The cane neither flowers nor fruits, though the clouds rain nectar on it;
so a fool's heart does not awaken, though he meet a guru like Brahmā.
lanka.17.cau1: Here, at dawn, Śrī Rāma woke, called all his counsellors and asked their advice:
Tell me quickly, what plan should we follow? Jāmbavān bowed his head at his feet and said:
lanka.17.cau2: Listen, all-knowing one, dweller in every heart, treasury of wisdom, strength, splendour, dharma and virtue.
I give my counsel as my understanding allows: send Aṅgada, son of Vāli, as your envoy.
lanka.17.cau3: The good counsel pleased everyone. Śrī Rāma, the treasury of compassion, said to Aṅgada:
Son of Vāli, home of wisdom, strength and virtue, go to Laṅkā, dear one, on my errand.
lanka.17.cau4: What need is there to explain at length to you? I know that you are very shrewd.
Talk with the enemy in such a way that our work is done and his good is served as well.
lanka.17.so17क: Taking the Lord's command upon his head and bowing to his feet, Aṅgada rose and said:
O Lord Rāma, he alone on whom you bestow your grace becomes an ocean of virtues.
lanka.17.so17ख: All my master's work accomplishes itself; my Lord has only done me honour.
So reflecting, the crown prince thrilled in body and rejoiced in heart.
lanka.18.cau1: Saluting the Lord's feet and keeping his greatness in mind, Aṅgada set out, bowing his head to everyone.
With the Lord's glory in his heart, the son of Vāli, a bold and formidable fighter, was fearless by nature.
lanka.18.cau2: Just inside the city he ran into one of Rāvaṇa's sons, at his play.
Words led on to words and the quarrel grew; the strength of both was beyond measure, and both were young as well.
lanka.18.cau3: He raised a kick at Aṅgada; Aṅgada seized his leg, whirled him round and flung him down on the ground.
Seeing so mighty a warrior, the crowds of demons scattered every way, unable even to raise a cry.
lanka.18.cau4: No one told another the truth of it; realising that Rāvaṇa's son had been slain, they all kept silent.
A clamour went up through the city: the monkey who burnt Laṅkā has come.
lanka.18.cau5: In great fear they all wondered what the Creator would do now.
Without being asked they showed him the way; whoever Aṅgada looked at shrank and withered.
lanka.18.do18: Then, remembering Śrī Rāma's lotus feet, Aṅgada came to the doors of the court where the assembly sat.
Steadfast and heroic, a mass of strength, he stood with a lion's bearing and looked this way and that.
lanka.19.cau1: At once a demon was sent, and he gave Rāvaṇa the news.
Hearing it, the ten-headed Rāvaṇa laughed and said: Call him and bring him here; where does this monkey come from?
lanka.19.cau2: At his command many messengers ran and brought back Aṅgada, the elephant among monkeys.
Aṅgada saw the ten-faced Rāvaṇa sitting there like a mountain of soot come to life.
lanka.19.cau3: His arms were like trees and his heads like mountain peaks; the hair on his body was like creepers of many kinds.
His mouths, noses, eyes and ears looked like the caves and hollows of a mountain.
lanka.19.cau4: The son of Vāli, mighty and bold, went into the assembly without the least wavering of mind.
The courtiers rose at the sight of the monkey, and Rāvaṇa's heart filled with fierce anger.
lanka.19.do19: As a lion walks into a herd of maddened elephants, so Aṅgada went in,
and, remembering Śrī Rāma's glory in his mind, bowed his head and sat down in the assembly.
lanka.20.cau1: Rāvaṇa said: Who are you, monkey? Aṅgada said: Ten-headed one, I am the messenger of Śrī Rāma.
You were my father's friend, brother, and I have come here for your good.
lanka.20.cau2: You come of a noble line, a grandson of the sage Pulastya; you worshipped Śiva and Brahmā in many ways.
You won boons and achieved all you set out to do; you conquered the guardians of the worlds and all kings.
lanka.20.cau3: Whether from a king's pride or from delusion, you have stolen away Sītā, mother of the world.
Now hear the good counsel I give you: the Lord will forgive you all your offences.
lanka.20.cau4: Take a blade of grass between your teeth, hang an axe at your throat, and bring your family and your own wives with you;
with Janaka's daughter placed respectfully before you, go in this way, putting aside all fear,
lanka.20.do20: and cry: Protector of those who bow to you, jewel of Raghu's line, save me now, save me.
Hearing that cry of distress, the Lord will at once free you from fear.
lanka.21.cau1: Rāvaṇa said: Mind your words, monkey cub. Fool, do you not know me, the enemy of the gods?
Tell me your name, brother, and your father's: on what ground is this friendship to be owned?
lanka.21.cau2: Aṅgada said: My name is Aṅgada, and I am the son of Vāli. Did you ever meet him?
At Aṅgada's words Rāvaṇa grew uneasy and said: There was a monkey called Vāli; I knew of him.
lanka.21.cau3: So, Aṅgada, you are the son of Vāli? Wrecker of your house, you were born as a fire in the bamboo of your own line.
Better you had been lost in the womb; you were born for nothing, you who style yourself, from your own lips, an ascetic's messenger.
lanka.21.cau4: Now tell me, is Vāli well, and where is he? Then Aṅgada laughed and replied:
Let ten days pass; then you will be with Vāli, and can clasp your friend to your heart and ask him how he fares.
lanka.21.cau5: What sort of welfare comes of enmity with Śrī Rāma, he will tell you all of it himself.
Listen, fool: discord takes root only in the mind of one in whose heart Śrī Rāma does not dwell.
lanka.21.do21: True enough: I am the ruin of my race, and you, ten-headed one, are the guardian of yours.
Not even the blind and the deaf would say such a thing, and you have twenty eyes and twenty ears.
lanka.22.cau1: He whose feet Śiva, Brahmā, the gods and the hosts of sages long to serve —
by becoming his messenger have I sunk my family? With such a thought in it, does your heart not burst?
lanka.22.cau2: Hearing the monkey's harsh words, the ten-faced Rāvaṇa glared and said:
Villain, I am bearing every harsh word of yours; I know what policy and dharma require.
lanka.22.cau3: Aṅgada said: I too have heard of your righteousness: you stole another man's wife.
And how you guard an envoy I have seen with my own eyes. Keeper of the vow of dharma, why do you not go and drown yourself?
lanka.22.cau4: When you saw your sister without ears and nose, you weighed dharma and forgave.
Your righteousness is the talk of the whole world, and I too count myself lucky to have seen you.
lanka.22.do22क: Rāvaṇa said: Stop your prattle, dull brute of a monkey, you fool; look at my arms.
Every one of them is a Rāhu, ready to swallow the moon of the guardians' vast strength.
lanka.22.do22ख: And once, in the lake of the sky, resting on the lotuses of my hands,
Kailāsa, with Śiva upon it, shone like a swan.
lanka.23.cau1: Listen, Aṅgada: tell me, what warrior in your army will take me on?
Your master has lost his strength pining for his wife, and his younger brother is wretched and downcast with his grief.
lanka.23.cau2: You and Sugrīva are both trees on a riverbank; my younger brother too is a great coward.
The minister Jāmbavān is very old; how could he take to the field now?
lanka.23.cau3: Nala and Nīla know the craft of building. There is one monkey of great strength,
the one who came first and burnt the city. Hearing this, the son of Vāli said:
lanka.23.cau4: Tell me truly, lord of the demons: did a monkey really burn your city?
A little monkey burns the city of Rāvaṇa! Who would hear such a tale and call it true?
lanka.23.cau5: Rāvaṇa, that great warrior you were praising is a mere errand-runner of Sugrīva's.
A great walker is no fighter; he is the one we sent out to gather news.
lanka.23.do23क: So it is true that the monkey burnt the city without his master's leave;
for fear of that he never went back to Sugrīva, but stayed in hiding.
lanka.23.do23ख: All that you say is true, ten-headed one; hearing it, I feel no anger at all.
In our army there is no one whom it would become to fight with you.
lanka.23.do23ग: Friendship and enmity are for one's equals: that is what policy says.
If a lion killed frogs, would anyone think well of him?
lanka.23.do23घ: Though it would demean Śrī Rāma to kill you, and be a great wrong besides,
yet hear this, ten-headed one: the wrath of the warrior race is a terrible thing.
lanka.23.do23ङ: With sarcasm for a bow and words for arrows, the monkey set his enemy's heart on fire,
and the warrior ten-headed one seemed to pull the arrows out with the tongs of his retorts.
lanka.23.do23च: Then the ten-headed Rāvaṇa laughed and said: A monkey has one great virtue:
whoever keeps him, he tries every means to serve that master's good.
lanka.24.cau1: Bravo the monkey, who for his master's sake casts off shame and dances wherever he may be,
and with his capering wins the crowd and serves his master's turn: such is his skill in duty.
lanka.24.cau2: Aṅgada, your kind are loyal to their masters; why should you not sing your master's praises like this?
I value merit and am wise above all, so I pay no heed to your bitter harping.
lanka.24.cau3: Aṅgada said: Hanumān, son of the Wind, has told me the truth about your eye for merit.
He wrecked your grove, slew your son and set your city ablaze; even so, he did you no harm at all.
lanka.24.cau4: It was with that pleasing nature of yours in mind, ten-headed one, that I made so bold.
I have come and seen what Hanumān told me: you know neither shame nor wrath nor resentment.
lanka.24.cau5: With a mind like that, monkey, no wonder you devoured your father. So saying, Rāvaṇa laughed.
Aṅgada said: Having eaten my father I would have eaten you as well, but something has just occurred to me.
lanka.24.cau6: Base and arrogant as you are, I do not kill you, for I see in you a vessel of Vāli's spotless fame.
Say, Rāvaṇa, how many Rāvaṇas does the world hold? Listen to all those I have heard of with my own ears.
lanka.24.cau7: One went down to Pātāla to conquer Bali, and the children there kept him tied up in the stables.
Boys at play kept going up to him and hitting him; at last Bali was moved to pity and got him freed.
lanka.24.cau8: Then Sahasrabāhu caught sight of another, ran and seized him like some rare beast,
and took him home for amusement; it was the sage Pulastya who went and got him freed.
lanka.24.do24: Of one I am quite ashamed to speak: he spent his time in Vāli's armpit.
Which of these are you, Rāvaṇa? Put aside your temper and tell the truth.
lanka.25.cau1: Rāvaṇa said: Listen, fool: I am that mighty Rāvaṇa, the play of whose arms is known to Kailāsa, the mountain of Śiva;
whose valour is known to Śiva, Umā's lord, whom I worshipped with my heads offered up as flowers.
lanka.25.cau2: With my own hands I took off the lotuses of my heads and worshipped Śiva, the foe of Tripura, more times than can be counted.
The guardians of the quarters know the might of my arms, fool; it rankles in their hearts to this day.
lanka.25.cau3: The elephants of the quarters know how hard my chest is, from every time I went and fought them by force;
their fearsome tusks never broke into it, but snapped like radishes as they struck.
lanka.25.cau4: When I walk, the earth sways the way a small boat does when a maddened elephant climbs aboard;
I am that Rāvaṇa, renowned in the world for his power. Have you never heard of him, you lying babbler?
lanka.25.do25: You call that Rāvaṇa small and sing the praises of a man?
Uncouth, puny, wicked monkey, now I have seen what your wisdom is worth.
lanka.26.cau1: Hearing this, Aṅgada answered in anger: Mind your words, you vile, arrogant creature.
He whose axe was a fire to burn the vast, dense forest of Sahasrabāhu's arms,
lanka.26.cau2: whose axe was an ocean in whose sharp current countless kings drowned time after time:
the pride of that Paraśurāma fled at the mere sight of him. How is he a man, wretched ten-headed one?
lanka.26.cau3: You crooked fool, how is Śrī Rāma a man? Is Kāmadeva just a bowman, and the Gaṅgā just a river?
Is the wish-granting cow just a beast, the wish-granting tree just a tree, the giving of food just a gift, and nectar just a drink?
lanka.26.cau4: Is Garuḍa a bird, the thousand-headed Śeṣa a snake, and the wish-fulfilling gem a stone, ten-headed one?
Listen, dull-wit: is Vaikuṇṭha merely a world, and unfailing devotion to Śrī Rāma merely a gain?
lanka.26.do26: He churned your pride and that of your army, laid waste the grove and burnt the city,
and went away after killing your son: how, you fool, is Hanumān a monkey?
lanka.27.cau1: Listen, Rāvaṇa: give up your cunning. Why do you not worship Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy?
Wretch, if you have made yourself Śrī Rāma's enemy, neither Brahmā nor Rudra can protect you.
lanka.27.cau2: Fool, do not brag in vain. Enmity with Śrī Rāma will bring you to this:
struck by Śrī Rāma's arrows, your heads will fall in heaps on the ground before the monkeys,
lanka.27.cau3: and bears and monkeys will play polo with those many heads of yours for balls.
When Śrī Rāma is roused to anger in battle and his many terrible arrows fly,
lanka.27.cau4: will your mouth run on like this then? Think of this and worship the generous Śrī Rāma.
At these words Rāvaṇa blazed up, like a great fire on which ghee has been poured.
lanka.27.do27: Rāvaṇa said: I have a brother like Kumbhakarṇa, and my son is the famous foe of Indra.
Have you not heard of my prowess, how I conquered all things moving and unmoving?
lanka.28.cau1: Fool, he gathered monkeys to help him and bridged the ocean: that is all his greatness.
Many birds fly across the ocean, but listen, monkey: that does not make them all heroes.
lanka.28.cau2: My arms are oceans brimming with the water of strength, in which many brave gods and men have drowned.
They are twenty oceans, fathomless and boundless: what hero is there who could reach their farther shore?
lanka.28.cau3: I have made the guardians of the quarters carry water for me, and you, wretch, recite to me the fame of a king.
if he is truly a great warrior in battle, that master of yours whose praises you sing over and over,
lanka.28.cau4: then why does he send an envoy? Does it not shame him to make friends with his foe?
Look at these arms of mine that shook Mount Kailāsa, and then, foolish monkey, praise your master.
lanka.28.do28: What hero is there like Rāvaṇa? With his own hands he cut off his heads
and offered them into the fire time after time with great joy; Śiva, lord of Gaurī, is witness.
lanka.29.cau1: As my skulls burned, I saw the letters the Creator had written on my forehead.
Reading there my death at the hands of a man, I laughed, knowing the Creator's word to be false.
lanka.29.cau2: Even bearing that in mind, I feel no fear: old Brahmā wrote it with a mind gone astray.
Fool, casting off shame and honour, you speak again and again before me of another hero's strength.
lanka.29.cau3: Aṅgada said: Rāvaṇa, there is no one in the world as modest as you.
Modesty is your very nature; you never tell your own merits with your own mouth.
lanka.29.cau4: The tale of your heads and the mountain has stuck in your mind, so you have repeated it twenty times.
But that strength of arm you have kept buried in your heart, the strength by which you conquered Sahasrabāhu, Bali and Vāli.
lanka.29.cau5: Listen, dull-wit, have done now. Does anyone become a hero by cutting off heads?
A conjurer cuts up his whole body with his own hands, yet no one calls him a hero.
lanka.29.do29: Moths burn themselves in their infatuation, and herds of donkeys carry loads;
but they are not called heroes. Think it over and see, dull-wit.
lanka.30.cau1: Wretch, argue no further; hear my words and give up your pride.
Ten-headed one, I have not come as an envoy; Śrī Rāma sent me with this in mind.
lanka.30.cau2: The compassionate Lord says again and again that a lion wins no glory by killing a jackal.
Keeping the Lord's words in mind, fool, I have borne your harsh words.
lanka.30.cau3: Were it not so, I would have broken your face and taken Sītā by force.
Vile enemy of the gods, I knew your strength when you stole another's wife while no one was by.
lanka.30.cau4: You are king of the demons and full of pride; I am only the messenger of a servant of Śrī Rāma.
If I did not fear dishonouring Śrī Rāma, I would put on such a show before your eyes:
lanka.30.do30: I would dash you to the ground, kill your army and lay waste your town,
and take away Janaka's daughter, you fool, along with your young wives.
lanka.31.cau1: Even if I did this, there would be no glory in it; there is no manhood in killing the dead.
One who follows the left-hand path, one ruled by lust, one who is miserly, one utterly foolish, one very poor, one in disgrace, one very old,
lanka.31.cau2: one always sick, one always angry, one turned away from Viṣṇu, one hostile to the Vedas and the saints,
one who lives only to feed his body, a slanderer, and a mine of sin: these fourteen are as corpses while they live.
lanka.31.cau3: Thinking of this, wretch, I do not kill you; now do not stir up my anger.
Hearing this, the king of the demons, biting his lips and wringing his hands, said in fury:
lanka.31.cau4: Vile monkey, you want to die now; that is why you speak big words from a small mouth.
Dull monkey, the one on whose strength you prate so bitterly has no strength, glory, wit or splendour.
lanka.31.do31क: His father, finding him without merit or honour, sent him to live in the forest.
On him lie that grief, then separation from his young wife, and day and night his fear of me.
lanka.31.do31ख: Men like him whose strength makes you proud are many;
demons eat them day and night. Fool, give up your obstinacy and understand.
lanka.32.cau1: When he reviled Śrī Rāma, Aṅgada, best of the monkeys, grew furious.
Whoever hears Śrī Hari or Śiva reviled is guilty of a sin equal to slaying a cow.
lanka.32.cau2: The mighty monkey ground his teeth and furiously struck both his great arms on the ground.
The earth shook, the courtiers fell, and, seized by the wind of fear, they took to flight.
lanka.32.cau3: Rāvaṇa, falling, caught himself and stood up; his splendid crowns dropped to the earth.
Some he picked up and set right on his heads; some Aṅgada hurled across to the Lord.
lanka.32.cau4: Seeing the crowns coming, the monkeys fled: Heavens, are meteors falling in broad daylight?
Or has Rāvaṇa in his anger hurled four thunderbolts, that come rushing on so fast?
lanka.32.cau5: The Lord laughed and said: Have no fear in your hearts; these are not meteors or thunderbolts, nor Ketu nor Rāhu.
These are the crowns of ten-headed Rāvaṇa, flung this way by Vāli's son.
lanka.32.do32क: Hanumān, son of the Wind, leapt up, caught them in his hands, brought them and laid them by the Lord.
The bears and monkeys gazed at the marvel; the crowns shone like the sun.
lanka.32.do32ख: Over there, Rāvaṇa, in a rage, angrily told them all:
Seize the monkey, seize him and kill him. Hearing this, Aṅgada smiled.
lanka.33.cau1: Kill him, then all you warriors run at once and eat the bears and monkeys wherever you find them.
Go and rid the earth of monkeys, and take the two ascetic brothers alive.
lanka.33.cau2: Then the crown prince spoke again in anger: Are you not ashamed to keep wagging your jaws?
Shameless wrecker of your own line, cut your throat and die! Does your heart not burst at the sight of such strength?
lanka.33.cau3: You thief of women, walker on the evil path, wretch, heap of filth, dull-witted and lustful!
You babble abuse as if in delirium; wretched eater of men, death has you in its grip.
lanka.33.cau4: You will reap the fruit of this later, when the monkeys and bears land their blows on you.
Proud one, as you say such words, that Śrī Rāma is a man, how is it your tongues do not fall?
lanka.33.cau5: Your tongues will fall, without a doubt, and your heads with them, on the field of battle.
lanka.33.so33क: Ten-headed one, how is he a man, who slew Vāli with a single arrow?
Base-born dullard, you are blind with all twenty eyes; shame on your birth.
lanka.33.so33ख: The host of Śrī Rāma's arrows is thirsting for your blood.
It is for fear of that, vile demon of bitter babble, that I let you go.
lanka.34.cau1: I am able to break your teeth, but Śrī Rāma has not given me the order.
Such is my anger that I could smash all ten of your mouths, and seize Laṅkā and sink it in the ocean.
lanka.34.cau2: Your Laṅkā is like a cluster fig, and you all live inside it like insects, unafraid.
I am a monkey; eating the fruit would take me no time, but the generous Śrī Rāma has not given the order.
lanka.34.cau3: Hearing this clever talk, Rāvaṇa smiled: Fool, where did you learn so much lying?
Vāli never boasted like this; keeping company with ascetics, you have become a liar.
lanka.34.cau4: Aṅgada said: Twenty-armed one, I am truly a liar if I do not tear out your ten tongues.
Bearing in mind Śrī Rāma's glory, Aṅgada was filled with anger, and in the middle of the court he made a vow and planted his foot.
lanka.34.cau5: Aṅgada said: Fool, if you can move my foot, Śrī Rāma will turn back, and I have lost Sītā.
Rāvaṇa said: Listen, all you warriors: seize the monkey by the foot and dash him to the ground.
lanka.34.cau6: Indrajit and many other mighty warriors rose here and there, delighted.
They lunge with all their strength and many a device, but the foot does not move, and they sit down with bowed heads.
lanka.34.cau7: The enemies of the gods rise again and lunge, but the monkey's foot stays where it is,
just as, Garuḍa, men of false yoga cannot uproot the tree of delusion.
lanka.34.do34क: Millions of warriors as mighty as Meghanāda rose gladly.
They lunge, but the monkey's foot will not stir, and once more they bow their heads and sit.
lanka.34.do34ख: The monkey's foot does not leave the ground; seeing this, the enemy's pride fell away,
the foot held as a saint's mind holds to what is right in the face of countless obstacles.
lanka.35.cau1: Seeing Aṅgada's strength, they all lost heart; then, at his challenge, Rāvaṇa rose himself.
As he reached for the foot, Vāli's son said: Clutching my feet will not save you.
lanka.35.cau2: Why not go, fool, and take hold of Śrī Rāma's feet? Hearing this, he turned back, deeply abashed.
His lustre was lost and all his splendour gone; he looked like the moon in the middle of the day.
lanka.35.cau3: He sat down on the throne with his head bowed, as though he had lost all his wealth.
Śrī Rāma is the soul of the world and the lord of life; how can one who turns away from him find rest?
lanka.35.cau4: Umā, at the mere play of Śrī Rāma's eyebrow the universe comes into being and then perishes again.
He makes a thunderbolt of a blade of grass and grass of a thunderbolt; tell me, how could his messenger's vow fail?
lanka.35.cau5: Then Aṅgada spoke to him of right policy in many ways, but he would not listen: his death had drawn near.
Having churned up the enemy's pride, he proclaimed the Lord's fair fame, and with these words the son of King Vāli set off:
lanka.35.cau6: Until I have toyed with you on the battlefield and slain you, why should I praise myself now?
Aṅgada had already killed his son; hearing of it, Rāvaṇa was grieved.
lanka.35.cau7: Seeing Aṅgada's vow hold, all the demons were utterly shaken with fear.
lanka.35.do35क: Having trampled on the enemy's might, Vāli's son, that mass of strength, was filled with joy.
His body thrilling and his eyes wet with tears, he clasped Śrī Rāma's lotus feet.
lanka.35.do35ख: Seeing that evening had come, Rāvaṇa went to his palace in dejection.
There Mandodarī once more counselled him and said:
lanka.36.cau1: My husband, think it over and give up this folly; a war with Śrī Rāma does not become you.
Śrī Rāma's younger brother drew a little line, and even that you could not cross: such is your manhood.
lanka.36.cau2: Beloved, will you defeat in battle him whose messenger did all this?
That lion among monkeys leapt across the ocean in play and came fearlessly into your Laṅkā.
lanka.36.cau3: He killed the guards and laid the grove waste, and slew Akṣaya Kumāra before your very eyes.
He set the whole city on fire and left it in ashes; where then were your strength and your pride?
lanka.36.cau4: Now, my lord, stop these idle boasts, and give some thought in your heart to what I say.
Husband, Śrī Rāma is no ordinary king, so do not take him for one; he is Lord of everything that moves and everything that stands still, and his might has no equal: know that.
lanka.36.cau5: Mārīca knew the power of his arrows, yet you would not heed even what that lowly one told you.
In Janaka's assembly there were kings beyond counting, and you were there too, with all your vast and matchless strength.
lanka.36.cau6: There he broke the bow and married Jānakī; why then did you not beat him in battle?
Indra's son knows a little of his strength: he let him live, only catching him and putting out an eye.
lanka.36.cau7: You saw what became of Śūrpaṇakhā, and still there is little shame in your heart.
lanka.36.do36: He slew Virādha, killed Khara and Dūṣaṇa and struck down Kabandha as if in play;
he killed Vāli with a single arrow. Know him for who he is, O ten-headed one.
lanka.37.cau1: He had the ocean bridged with ease, and the Lord has come down with his army onto Mount Suvela;
that compassionate banner of the solar race sent an envoy for your own good —
lanka.37.cau2: an envoy who, in the middle of the assembly, crushed your strength as a lion crushes a herd of elephants.
He whose followers are Aṅgada and Hanumān, heroes most formidable and gallant in battle —
lanka.37.cau3: him, beloved, you keep calling a man, and you carry the load of pride, attachment and arrogance for nothing.
Alas, my husband, you have made an enemy of Śrī Rāma; in the grip of death, your mind cannot come to its senses.
lanka.37.cau4: Death does not take up a stick to strike anyone; it takes away his dharma, strength, intellect and judgement.
My lord, one whose death is drawing near falls into delusion, just as you have.
lanka.37.do37: Two of your sons are dead and the city is burnt; even now, beloved, bring this to an end.
My lord, worship Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, and gain a spotless name.
lanka.38.cau1: Hearing his wife's words, sharp as arrows, he rose at daybreak and went to the assembly.
He went and sat on the throne, swollen with pride; in his great arrogance he forgot all fear.
lanka.38.cau2: Here Śrī Rāma sent for Aṅgada; he came and bowed his head to the Lord's lotus feet.
Seating him close by with great honour, the compassionate Lord, slayer of Khara, smiled and said:
lanka.38.cau3: Son of Vāli, I am very curious; I ask you, my dear, tell me truly.
Rāvaṇa is the crown of the demon race, and the matchless might of his arms is renowned through the world.
lanka.38.cau4: You flung four of his crowns; tell me, my dear, how did they come into your hands? Aṅgada said:
Listen, all-knowing one, giver of joy to those who bow to you: they are not crowns but the four virtues of a king.
lanka.38.cau5: My Lord, the Vedas say that conciliation, gifts, force and division dwell in the heart of a king.
They are the fair feet of statecraft and dharma; knowing this in their hearts, they have come to my Lord.
lanka.38.do38क: The ten-headed Rāvaṇa has no dharma, has turned from the Lord's feet and is in the power of death.
So, hear me, Lord of Kosala: these virtues left him and came to you.
lanka.38.do38ख: Hearing this most clever answer, the noble Śrī Rāma smiled.
Then Vāli's son told him all the news of the fort.
lanka.39.cau1: When he had the news of the enemy, Śrī Rāma called all his counsellors to him.
Laṅkā has four formidable gates; consider how they should be attacked.
lanka.39.cau2: Then Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, Jāmbavān, king of the bears, and Vibhīṣaṇa remembered in their hearts the ornament of the solar race.
After deliberating they settled their plan and formed the monkey army into four divisions.
lanka.39.cau3: They made commanders as each was fit; then they called together all the troop leaders.
They spoke of the Lord's glory and instructed them all; hearing it, the monkeys rushed off with roars like lions.
lanka.39.cau4: Joyfully they bow their heads at Śrī Rāma's feet, and all the heroes rush on, carrying mountain peaks.
The bears and monkey chiefs roar and threaten: Glory to the hero of the Raghus, the Lord of Kosala!
lanka.39.cau5: Though they knew Laṅkā to be a most formidable fortress, the monkeys went on without fear, by the Lord's glory.
Massing like storm clouds, they hemmed it in on all four sides and sounded drums and kettledrums with their mouths.
lanka.39.do39: Glory to Śrī Rāma, glory to Lakṣmaṇa, glory to Sugrīva, king of the monkeys:
so the monkeys and bears, the very limit of great strength, roar their lion-roars.
lanka.40.cau1: A great tumult rose in Laṅkā, and Rāvaṇa, in his great arrogance, heard it.
Rāvaṇa said: Just look at the impudence of these monkeys. And with a laugh he called up the demon army.
lanka.40.cau2: These monkeys have come, driven by death, and my demons are all hungry.
Saying this, the fool burst into a loud laugh: Fate has sent us food without our leaving home.
lanka.40.cau3: Warriors, go out, all of you, in every direction; seize the bears and monkeys one by one and eat them all.
Umā, Rāvaṇa's pride was like that of the lapwing, which sleeps lying on its back.
lanka.40.cau4: Taking their orders, the demons set out, holding javelins and fine spears in their hands,
lances, maces, fierce axes, tridents, swords, iron clubs and lumps of mountain rock.
lanka.40.cau5: As foolish birds that feed on flesh swoop on a heap of red stones when they see it,
never thinking of the pain of a broken beak, so the senseless man-eaters rushed out.
lanka.40.do40: Mighty demon warriors, bearing bows, arrows and weapons of every kind,
staunch in battle and countless in number, climbed onto the battlements of the ramparts.
lanka.41.cau1: How do they look upon the battlements? As if clouds had settled on the peaks of Meru.
War drums and kettledrums are beating, and at their sound the warriors' hearts are eager.
lanka.41.cau2: Kettledrums and pipes sound without end; hearing them, the hearts of cowards split.
Going out, they saw the throngs of monkeys and the bear warriors with their huge bodies.
lanka.41.cau3: They charge on, making nothing of rough ravines; they grip the mountains, break them open and make their way through.
Millions of warriors gnash their teeth and roar; they bite their lips and hurl fierce threats.
lanka.41.cau4: On that side they call on Rāvaṇa, on this side on Śrī Rāma; with cries of victory, victory, the battle broke out.
The demons hurl down masses of peaks; the monkeys leap up, catch them and throw them back.
lanka.41.cha1: The fierce monkeys and bears lift pieces of mountain and hurl them at the fort.
They lunge, seize the demons by the feet, dash them to the ground, run off and challenge them again.
Most nimble and at the height of their vigour, they spring up and, in their fury, climbed onto the fort again and again.
Monkeys and bears climbed onto the mansions here and there and began to sing Śrī Rāma's praise.
lanka.41.do41: Then each monkey seized a demon and made off;
themselves on top and the demon warriors beneath, they come crashing to the ground.
lanka.42.cau1: Mighty through Śrī Rāma's glory, the monkey troops crush the hosts of demon warriors.
Again the monkeys climbed the fort here and there, crying: Glory to the hero of the Raghus, the sun of glory!
lanka.42.cau2: The demon hordes fled like banks of cloud before a strong wind.
A great cry of woe went up in the city; children and frightened women wept.
lanka.42.cau3: Together they all heap abuse on Rāvaṇa: in the midst of his reign this man has summoned death.
When he heard with his own ears that his army was breaking, the lord of Laṅkā turned the warriors back, in a rage.
lanka.42.cau4: Rāvaṇa said: Anyone I hear of turning his back on the battle, I will kill with my terrible sword.
You have eaten all I have and enjoyed every kind of pleasure, and now on the battlefield your lives have become dear to you!
lanka.42.cau5: Hearing such fierce words they all took fright, and the warriors, stung with shame, set off in anger.
To die facing the foe is a warrior's glory; so they let go of their love of life.
lanka.42.do42: Bearing many weapons, all the warriors closed in, issuing challenge after challenge.
Striking with iron clubs and tridents, they threw the bears and monkeys into distress.
lanka.43.cau1: Umā, the monkeys, distraught with fear, began to flee, though it is they who will win in the end.
Someone cried: Where are Aṅgada and Hanumān? And Nala, Nīla and the mighty Dvivida, where are they?
lanka.43.cau2: The mighty Hanumān, who was at the western gate, heard that his own army was in distress.
Meghanāda was fighting there; the gate would not break, and it was very hard going.
lanka.43.cau3: Great anger rose in the heart of Hanumān, son of the Wind, and the mighty warrior roared like Death.
Leaping, he came up onto the fort of Laṅkā, and, seizing a mountain, ran at Meghanāda.
lanka.43.cau4: He smashed the chariot, struck down the charioteer, and kicked Meghanāda in the chest.
Another charioteer, seeing him stunned, laid him in a chariot and at once brought him home.
lanka.43.do43: Aṅgada heard that Hanumān, son of the Wind, had gone onto the fort alone;
and Vāli's son, a gallant in battle, sprang up onto the fort as if it were a monkey's game.
lanka.44.cau1: Both monkeys, furious against the foe in battle, remembered within their hearts the glory of Śrī Rāma;
the two ran and climbed onto Rāvaṇa's palace, crying out the name of the Lord of Kosala.
lanka.44.cau2: They seized the palace and brought it down, pinnacle and all; seeing this, the king of the demons was afraid.
Crowds of women beat their breasts with their hands: Now two troublemaking monkeys have come!
lanka.44.cau3: With monkey antics they frighten them, and recite to them the fair fame of Śrī Rāma.
Then, taking hold of the golden pillars, they said: Now let the havoc begin.
lanka.44.cau4: Roaring, they dropped into the midst of the enemy's army and began to crush it with the great strength of their arms.
Kicking one and slapping another, they say: You do not worship Śrī Rāma; take the fruit of that.
lanka.44.do44: They crush one against another, and wrench off heads and hurl them.
The heads fall before Rāvaṇa as if pots of curd were bursting.
lanka.45.cau1: Whatever great chiefs they lay hands on, they seize by the feet and fling to where the Lord is.
Vibhīṣaṇa tells their names, and Śrī Rāma gives even them his own abode.
lanka.45.cau2: Wicked man-eaters who fed on the flesh of brāhmaṇas attain the state that yogīs pray for.
Umā, Śrī Rāma is tender-hearted, a mine of compassion: the demons remember me, though it is in enmity —
lanka.45.cau3: knowing this in his heart, he grants them the supreme state. Say, Bhavānī: who is as merciful as he?
Those who hear of such a Lord and still do not cast off delusion and worship him are dull-witted and most unfortunate.
lanka.45.cau4: The Lord of Avadh said: Aṅgada and Hanumān have entered the fort.
The two monkeys in Laṅkā look as splendid as two Mount Mandaras churning the ocean.
lanka.45.do45: With the might of their arms they ground the enemy's ranks to pieces; then, seeing that the day was ending,
the two leapt down, free of weariness, and returned to the Lord.
lanka.46.cau1: They laid their heads at the Lord's lotus feet, and the sight of such fine warriors gladdened Śrī Rāma's heart.
Śrī Rāma turned a gracious glance on the pair; their weariness was gone, and they were filled with the highest joy.
lanka.46.cau2: Knowing that Aṅgada and Hanumān had gone, the many bear and monkey warriors turned back too.
Gaining strength from the dusk, the demons rushed out, crying the name of Rāvaṇa.
lanka.46.cau3: Seeing the demon army, the monkeys turned round, and warriors clashed here and there, gnashing their teeth.
Both armies are strong; challenging again and again, the warriors fight on and will not own defeat.
lanka.46.cau4: The demons, all of them dark, are mighty heroes; the monkeys are of many hues and massive.
Each army is powerful, its fighters a match for the other's; showing their prowess, they battle in fury.
lanka.46.cau5: It is as if dense clouds of the rains and of autumn were fighting, driven on by the wind.
Seeing their army waver, the commanders Akampana and Atikāya worked māyā.
lanka.46.cau6: In the blink of an eye it grew very dark, and a rain of blood, stones and ashes began to fall.
lanka.46.do46: The monkey army saw thick darkness in all ten directions and was seized with panic.
No one can see anyone else, and everywhere they are crying out.
lanka.47.cau1: Śrī Rāma understood the whole secret, and sent for Aṅgada and Hanumān.
He told them everything and explained it; hearing it, the two great monkeys rushed off in anger.
lanka.47.cau2: Then the compassionate Lord smiled, strung his bow and at once let fly a fiery arrow.
Light spread and nowhere was there darkness, as doubts vanish when knowledge dawns.
lanka.47.cau3: With the light, the bears and monkeys ran forward joyfully, free of weariness and fear.
Hanumān and Aṅgada roared on the battlefield; at the sound of their shout the demons fled.
lanka.47.cau4: The bears and monkeys seize the fleeing warriors and dash them to the ground; wondrous are the deeds they do.
Grabbing them by the feet they throw them into the ocean, where crocodiles, serpents and fish catch them one by one and eat them.
lanka.47.do47: Some were killed, some wounded, and some fled and climbed back up the fort.
Having broken the strength of the enemy army, the bears and monkeys roar.
lanka.48.cau1: Knowing that night had come, all four divisions of the monkeys came to where the Lord of Kosala was.
Śrī Rāma looked on them all with grace, and at that very moment the monkeys were rid of their weariness.
lanka.48.cau2: Over there, Rāvaṇa summoned his ministers, told them all of the warriors who had been killed, and said:
The monkeys have destroyed half the army. Tell me quickly: what plan should we form?
lanka.48.cau3: Mālyavān was a very old demon, the father of Rāvaṇa's mother and an excellent minister.
He spoke words of right counsel, wholly pure: Dear one, hear a little advice from me.
lanka.48.cau4: Ever since you stole Sītā away to this place, ill omens have been appearing beyond all telling.
No one who turned against Śrī Rāma, whose fame the Vedas and Purāṇas have sung, has ever found happiness.
lanka.48.do48क: He who slew Hiraṇyākṣa together with his brother, and the mighty Madhu and Kaiṭabha —
that same Lord, the ocean of mercy, has come down as an incarnation.
lanka.48.do48ख: He is Death in form, the fire that burns the forest of the wicked, the home of virtues, knowledge itself made dense;
Śiva and Brahmā serve him. What enmity can there be with him?
lanka.49.cau1: Give up the enmity and give back Vaidehī; worship the treasury of mercy, the most loving one.
His words struck Rāvaṇa like arrows, and he said: Blacken your face and be gone, you wretch.
lanka.49.cau2: You have grown old, or else I would kill you. Now do not show yourself before my eyes.
Mālyavān reasoned in his mind that the treasury of mercy now meant to slay Rāvaṇa.
lanka.49.cau3: He rose and left, speaking harsh words. Then Meghanāda said in anger:
In the morning, watch my feats. I shall do a great deal; why say a little of it now?
lanka.49.cau4: Hearing his son's words, Rāvaṇa took heart, and lovingly sat him on his lap.
While they were still deliberating, day broke, and the monkeys again pressed at all four gates.
lanka.49.cau5: In anger the monkeys surrounded the impregnable fort, and a great uproar arose in the city.
Demons bearing all kinds of weapons ran out and toppled mountain peaks down from the fort.
lanka.49.cha1: They toppled peaks of mountains by the million, and missiles of many kinds flew.
They rumble like falling thunderbolts, and the warriors roar like the clouds of the world's dissolution.
The fierce monkey warriors close in and are cut, their bodies riddled with wounds, yet they do not flag.
Seizing rocks, they hurl them at the fort, and the demons are slain wherever they stand.
lanka.49.do49: Meghanāda heard with his own ears that the monkeys had come back and laid siege to the fort;
the warrior came down from the fort and, with drums beating, went out to face them.
lanka.50.cau1: Meghanāda said: Where are the two brothers, lords of Kosala, archers famed in every world?
Where are Nala, Nīla, Dvivida and Sugrīva? Where are Aṅgada and Hanumān, the utmost in strength?
lanka.50.cau2: Where is Vibhīṣaṇa, traitor to his brother? Today I will kill them all, and him above all, whatever it takes.
So saying, he set fierce arrows to the string and, in towering rage, drew it back to his ear.
lanka.50.cau3: He began to loose swarms of arrows, as if many winged serpents were rushing through the air.
Here and there monkeys were seen falling; at that time none could stand before him.
lanka.50.cau4: Monkeys and bears ran off in all directions; all of them forgot their wish to fight.
No monkey or bear could be found in the field whom he had not left with only his life remaining.
lanka.50.do50: He shot ten arrows into every one of them, and the monkey heroes lay on the ground.
Meghanāda, mighty and steadfast, gave a lion's roar and thundered.
lanka.51.cau1: Seeing the army in distress, Hanumān, son of the Wind, rushed forward in fury, as though Death itself were charging.
At once he tore up a huge mountain and in great rage flung it at Meghanāda.
lanka.51.cau2: Seeing it coming, he went up into the sky; his chariot, charioteer and horses were all destroyed.
Again and again Hanumān challenges him, but he does not come near, for he knew Hanumān's secret.
lanka.51.cau3: Meghanāda went near Śrī Rāma and hurled abuse of every kind.
He threw missiles, weapons and arms of every sort; the Lord, as if in play, cut them all down and warded them off.
lanka.51.cau4: Seeing the Lord's might, the fool was vexed, and began to work māyā in many ways —
as if someone were to play games with Garuḍa, holding up a tiny young snake to frighten him.
lanka.51.do51: He whose mighty māyā holds all, great and small, even Śiva and Brahmā, in its power —
to him the demon of crooked mind displays his own māyā.
lanka.52.cau1: He climbed into the sky and rained down embers in plenty, and streams of water burst forth from the earth.
Ghouls and she-ghouls of every kind danced about, raising the cry of kill and cut.
lanka.52.cau2: Now he rained down filth, pus, blood, hair and bones; now he let loose a shower of stones.
He showered dust and made such darkness that no one could see his own outstretched hand.
lanka.52.cau3: The monkeys were thrown into turmoil at the sight of this illusion; at this rate, it seemed, death had come for them all.
Seeing this trickery, Śrī Rāma smiled; he knew that all the monkeys had taken fright.
lanka.52.cau4: With a single arrow he cut through the whole illusion, as the sun takes away the massed darkness.
He looked on the monkeys and bears with grace, and they grew so mighty that nothing could hold them back in battle.
lanka.52.do52: Asking Śrī Rāma's leave, and with Aṅgada and other monkeys beside him,
Lakṣmaṇa set out in anger, bow and arrows in hand.
lanka.53.cau1: His eyes were blood-red, his chest broad and his arms long; his body, like the snowy Himālaya, had a tinge of red.
On this side Rāvaṇa dispatched his best fighters; they seized missiles and weapons of many kinds and rushed in.
lanka.53.cau2: Armed with mountains, claws and trees, the monkeys charged, crying glory to Śrī Rāma.
All closed with their matches, pair against pair; on this side and on that, the longing to win was in no way small.
lanka.53.cau3: They tore at the demons with fists, kicks and teeth; the victorious monkeys struck them down and then shouted at them in scorn.
The cry went up: kill, kill, seize, seize, seize, kill; break the head, grab the arm and tear it off.
lanka.53.cau4: The din filled all nine regions of the earth, and fearsome headless trunks ran about here and there.
From the sky the hosts of gods watched the spectacle, now in wonder, now in delight.
lanka.53.do53: Blood had filled the hollows and congealed, and dust blew up and settled over it,
as though ash had spread over heaps of glowing embers.
lanka.54.cau1: How did the wounded warriors look? Like palāśa trees in full flower.
Lakṣmaṇa and Meghanāda, both warriors, fought each other in towering rage.
lanka.54.cau2: Neither could defeat the other; the demon fought unfairly, by the strength of trickery.
At this Lakṣmaṇa, Ananta himself, was roused to anger and in a moment shattered both chariot and charioteer.
lanka.54.cau3: Śeṣa struck him in many ways, until the demon had barely his life left.
Rāvaṇa's son reckoned in his mind: I am in peril; he will take my life.
lanka.54.cau4: He hurled the warrior-slaying spear, and that blazing weapon struck Lakṣmaṇa in the chest.
As the weapon struck, he fell into a swoon; then Meghanāda, his fear gone, went up close to him.
lanka.54.do54: Warriors like Meghanāda, a thousand million of them, tried to lift him;
but Śeṣa, on whom the world rests — how could he be raised? They went away abashed.
lanka.55.cau1: Listen, Pārvatī: he whose fiery wrath swiftly burns up the fourteen worlds,
whom gods, men and all creation, moving and unmoving, serve: who could defeat him in battle?
lanka.55.cau2: Only one on whom Śrī Rāma's grace rests understands this play.
When evening came, both armies turned back, and each began to take stock of its own troops.
lanka.55.cau3: The merciful Lord, the all-pervading Brahman, unconquered ruler of the worlds, asked: Where is Lakṣmaṇa?
Just then Hanumān brought him in; seeing his younger brother, the Lord was deeply grieved.
lanka.55.cau4: Jāmbavān said: There is a physician in Laṅkā, Suṣeṇa; whom shall we send to fetch him?
Taking a tiny form, Hanumān went and brought him back at once, house and all.
lanka.55.do55: Suṣeṇa came and laid his head at the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma.
He named the mountain and the herb and said: Son of the Wind, go and fetch it.
lanka.56.cau1: With Śrī Rāma's lotus feet held in his heart, and speaking of his own strength, the son of the Wind set off.
Over there, a spy let out the secret, and Rāvaṇa came to Kālanemi's house.
lanka.56.cau2: Rāvaṇa told him the secret; hearing it, Kālanemi beat his head again and again.
He said: The one who burned your city before your eyes — who can bar his way?
lanka.56.cau3: Worship Śrī Rāma and do yourself good; give up this false prattle, my lord.
Set in your heart the one who delights the eyes, his body dark and lovely as a blue lotus.
lanka.56.cau4: Give up the folly of I and you and mine; you are asleep in the night of great delusion, wake up.
He devours even the serpent of Time: could anyone defeat him in battle even in a dream?
lanka.56.do56: Hearing this, Rāvaṇa flew into a rage, and Kālanemi thought to himself:
Let me rather fall by the hand of Śrī Rāma's messenger; this villain is steeped in heaps of sin.
lanka.57.cau1: So saying he went, and on the way he conjured an illusion, making a lake, a temple and a fine garden.
The son of the Wind saw the pleasant hermitage and thought: I will ask the sage, drink some water, and my weariness will go.
lanka.57.cau2: There sat the demon in a false guise, hoping to beguile the messenger of the Lord of māyā.
Hanumān went and bowed his head, and the demon began to tell of Śrī Rāma's virtues.
lanka.57.cau3: A great battle is being fought between Rāvaṇa and Śrī Rāma; Śrī Rāma will win, of that there is no doubt.
Brother, I see it all while staying here; the power of my inner vision is great.
lanka.57.cau4: When asked for water he held out his water-pot; Hanumān said: So little water will not satisfy me.
Kālanemi said: Bathe in the lake and come back quickly, and I will initiate you so that you gain knowledge.
lanka.57.do57: As Hanumān entered the lake, a she-crocodile, in a frenzy, seized his foot.
He killed her, and she took on a divine body, mounted a celestial car and rose into the sky.
lanka.58.cau1: She said: Hanumān, the sight of you has freed me from sin; dear one, the great sage's curse is ended.
This is no sage but a terrible demon; believe my words, Hanumān, they are true.
lanka.58.cau2: The moment the nymph had said this and gone, Hanumān went straight to the demon.
Hanumān said: Sage, take your teacher's fee first; you can give me the mantra afterwards.
lanka.58.cau3: He wound his tail round the demon's head and dashed him down; as he died, the demon showed his own true body.
Saying Rāma, Rāma, he gave up his life; hearing it, Hanumān went on, glad at heart.
lanka.58.cau4: The mountain he saw, but the herb he could not make out; so Hanumān suddenly uprooted the whole peak.
Holding the mountain, he sped through the night sky and passed over the city of Ayodhyā.
lanka.58.do58: Bharata saw a huge form and, judging in his mind that it was a demon,
drew his bow to his ear and shot an arrow without a head.
lanka.59.cau1: The arrow struck, and he fell senseless to the ground, calling: Rāma, Rāma, O Lord of the Raghus.
At these dear words Bharata ran to him and came to the monkey's side in great haste.
lanka.59.cau2: Seeing the monkey stricken, he clasped him to his breast and tried in many ways to rouse him, but he did not wake.
His face fell and his heart was filled with sorrow; with tears in his eyes he spoke:
lanka.59.cau3: The fate that set me apart from Śrī Rāma has now dealt me this cruel blow too.
If my love for Śrī Rāma's lotus feet is free of guile in mind, word and body,
lanka.59.cau4: then may this monkey be rid of weariness and pain, if Śrī Rāma looks on me with favour.
At these words the monkey chief sat up, crying: Glory, glory to the Lord of Kosala!
lanka.59.so59: Bharata clasped Hanumān to his breast, his body thrilling and his eyes wet with tears.
As he thought of Śrī Rāma, his love was more than his heart could hold.
lanka.60.cau1: Bharata said: Dear one, tell me how the Lord, the home of all joy, is faring, with his younger brother and Mother Jānakī.
Hanumān told him in brief all that had happened; Bharata was grieved and full of regret within.
lanka.60.cau2: Alas, fate, why was I born into the world, when I have been of no use to the Lord in a single task?
Then, knowing it was no time for this, the mighty hero steadied his mind and spoke again to Hanumān:
lanka.60.cau3: Dear one, you will be late getting there, and at daybreak the work will be undone.
Mount my arrow with the mountain, and I shall send you to where the abode of grace is.
lanka.60.cau4: When Hanumān heard this, pride arose in his mind: how will an arrow fly with my weight on it?
Then, thinking again of Śrī Rāma's power, he paid homage at Bharata's feet, and with joined palms he said:
lanka.60.do60क: My lord and master, holding your glory in my heart I shall go at once.
With these words, and with leave given, Hanumān bowed at his feet and set off.
lanka.60.do60ख: Bharata's strength of arm, his gentle nature, his virtues and his boundless love for the Lord's feet:
these the son of the Wind praised again and again in his mind as he went.
lanka.61.cau1: There, gazing at Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma spoke words such as a mortal man would speak:
Half the night is gone and Hanumān has not come. Then Śrī Rāma lifted his younger brother and held him to his breast.
lanka.61.cau2: Brother, the sight of my sorrow was always more than you could bear, so tender has your nature ever been.
For my sake you left father and mother, and endured the forest's cold, its sun and its winds.
lanka.61.cau3: Where is that love now, brother? You do not rise, though you hear my anguished words.
If I had known that the forest would part me from my brother, I would not have heeded even that command of my father.
lanka.61.cau4: Sons, wealth, wife, home and family come and go in the world time after time.
Think of this and wake, dear one: in all the world a brother of one's own blood is not found again.
lanka.61.cau5: As a bird without wings is wretched, a serpent without its jewel, a great elephant without its trunk,
such will my life be without you, brother, if unfeeling fate keeps me alive.
lanka.61.cau6: With what face shall I go to Ayodhyā, having lost my dear brother for the sake of a wife?
Better I had borne the world's reproach: the loss of a wife would have been no special harm.
lanka.61.cau7: Now, my son, this hard and pitiless heart of mine must bear both the disgrace and the grief for you.
You are your mother's only son, dear one, the very support of her life.
lanka.61.cau8: Knowing me to be a giver of every kind of joy and wholly devoted to your good, she put your hand in mine and gave you to my care.
When I go to her, what answer am I to give? Brother, why not rise and tell me what to do?
lanka.61.cau9: He who frees others from sorrow grieved in many ways, and tears flowed from his lotus-petal eyes.
Umā, Śrī Rāma is one and undivided; the Lord, merciful to his devotees, was showing the ways of a man.
lanka.61.so61: The hosts of monkeys were distraught to hear the Lord's lament.
Then Hanumān arrived, like the heroic mood arriving in the midst of the mood of grief.
lanka.62.cau1: Śrī Rāma joyfully embraced Hanumān; the Lord is deeply grateful and supremely wise.
Then the physician quickly applied his remedy, and Lakṣmaṇa sat up, full of joy.
lanka.62.cau2: Holding his brother close to his heart, the Lord embraced him, and the bear and monkey hosts were all glad.
Then Hanumān carried the physician home again, just as he had fetched him.
lanka.62.cau3: Rāvaṇa heard this news and, in deep dejection, beat his head again and again.
In distress he came to Kumbhakarṇa and, by many kinds of effort, roused him.
lanka.62.cau4: Awake, the demon looked like Death himself sitting there in bodily form.
Kumbhakarṇa asked: Tell me, brother, why have your faces gone so dry and drawn?
lanka.62.cau5: The proud one told him the whole story of how he had carried off Sītā, and said:
Brother, every one of the demons has fallen to the monkeys; they have slain the greatest of warriors.
lanka.62.cau6: Durmukha, the foe of the gods, the eater of men, the mighty warriors Atikāya and Akampana,
and other heroes such as Mahodara, all of them steadfast in battle, lie fallen on the field.
lanka.62.do62: Then, hearing Rāvaṇa's words, Kumbhakarṇa cried out in grief:
You carried off the Mother of the world, fool, and now you hope for good?
lanka.63.cau1: Lord of the demons, you did ill. What use is it now to come and wake me?
Even now, brother, give up your pride and worship Śrī Rāma, and good will come to you.
lanka.63.cau2: Rāvaṇa, is Śrī Rāma only a man, he whose servants are the like of Hanumān?
Alas, brother, you did wrong in not coming to tell me at the very start.
lanka.63.cau3: My lord, you have set yourself against that god whose servants are Śiva, Brahmā and the gods.
The sage Nārada once taught me wisdom I meant to pass on to you; that chance is gone now.
lanka.63.cau4: Now, brother, take me in your arms and embrace me; let me go and make my eyes fruitful.
Let me go and see him, dark of body and lotus-eyed, who frees from the three kinds of suffering.
lanka.63.do63: Remembering Śrī Rāma's form and virtues, he was lost in them for a moment.
Rāvaṇa sent for countless jars of wine and many buffaloes.
lanka.64.cau1: He ate the buffaloes, drank the wine, and roared like the crash of a thunderbolt.
Wild with drink and eager for battle, Kumbhakarṇa left the fort and set out, with no army at his side.
lanka.64.cau2: Seeing him, Vibhīṣaṇa came forward, fell at his feet and gave his name.
Kumbhakarṇa lifted his younger brother to his breast and loved him the more, knowing him for Śrī Rāma's devotee.
lanka.64.cau3: Vibhīṣaṇa said: Brother, Rāvaṇa kicked me when I gave him well-considered counsel for his highest good.
Stung by that, I came to Śrī Rāma, and the Lord, seeing me forlorn, was pleased with me.
lanka.64.cau4: Kumbhakarṇa said: Listen, son: Rāvaṇa is in the grip of death; will he heed the best of counsel now?
Blessed, blessed, blessed are you, Vibhīṣaṇa; dear one, you have become an ornament to the demon clan.
lanka.64.cau5: Brother, you have made our line illustrious, for you worshipped Śrī Rāma, the ocean of beauty and joy.
lanka.64.do64: Cast off deceit in word, deed and thought, and worship Śrī Rāma, the steadfast in battle.
Go now, brave one; I can no longer tell my own from others, for I have fallen into the power of death.
lanka.65.cau1: Hearing his brother's words, Vibhīṣaṇa left and came to where Śrī Rāma, the ornament of the three worlds, was.
He said: My Lord, Kumbhakarṇa, steadfast in battle, with a body like a mountain, is coming.
lanka.65.cau2: As soon as the monkeys heard this much, the mighty ones rushed forward with shrill cries.
They lifted trees and mountains and, gnashing their teeth, hurled them upon him.
lanka.65.cau3: Each bear and monkey, at every throw, strikes him with mountain peaks by the million.
Yet his resolve never wavered and his body would not be shifted, try as they might: an elephant struck with arka fruit cares as little.
lanka.65.cau4: Then Hanumān, son of the Wind, struck him with his fist; he fell to the earth, dazed, and beat his head.
Rising again, he struck Hanumān, who reeled and at once fell to the ground.
lanka.65.cau5: Then he threw Nala and Nīla to the ground, and dashed down warriors here and there.
The monkey army fled, stricken with great fear; no one would face him.
lanka.65.do65: He knocked Aṅgada and the other monkeys senseless, Sugrīva with them,
and he, the very bound of boundless strength, went off with the king of the monkeys pressed under his arm.
lanka.66.cau1: Umā, Śrī Rāma is playing a human part, as Garuḍa might play, mingling with a crowd of snakes.
Does such a fight befit him who devours Death itself with a knitting of his brows?
lanka.66.cau2: He will spread a fame that purifies the world, and by singing it again and again people will cross the ocean of worldly existence.
His swoon passed, Hanumān, son of the Wind, came to, and then began to search for Sugrīva.
lanka.66.cau3: Sugrīva too came out of his swoon and slipped free, for Kumbhakarṇa believed him dead.
He bit off his nose and ears and, roaring, made off through the sky; only then did Kumbhakarṇa know.
lanka.66.cau4: Kumbhakarṇa seized him by the feet and dashed him to the ground; with great agility Sugrīva rose and struck him again.
Then the mighty Sugrīva came back to the Lord, crying: Glory, glory, glory to you, treasury of compassion!
lanka.66.cau5: Knowing in his heart that his nose and ears had been cut off, he turned back in anger, mortified.
Fearsome by nature, and now without ears or nose, he struck terror into the monkey ranks at the sight.
lanka.66.do66: Glory, glory, glory to the jewel of Raghu's line! With this war-cry the monkeys charged,
and all at once they let fly at him masses of mountains and trees.
lanka.67.cau1: Kumbhakarṇa, fired for battle, advanced to meet them like Death himself in fury.
He seized monkeys by the million and devoured them, as if locusts were pouring into a mountain cave.
lanka.67.cau2: Millions he seized and crushed against his body; millions he ground to nothing and mixed with the dust of the earth.
Throngs of bears and monkeys come out by way of his mouth, nose and ears, and flee.
lanka.67.cau3: The demon, reeling with the madness of war, was as proud as if Brahmā had made him a gift of the universe to devour.
All the great warriors turned back and would not return when rallied; their eyes saw nothing, and they did not hear when called.
lanka.67.cau4: Kumbhakarṇa scattered the monkey army; hearing of it, the demon host also rushed out.
Śrī Rāma saw his army in distress, and enemy forces of many kinds arriving.
lanka.67.do67: Listen, Sugrīva, Vibhīṣaṇa and my brother: take care of the army.
I will take the measure of this wretch's strength and his host, said the lotus-eyed Śrī Rāma.
lanka.68.cau1: Śārṅga bow in hand, quiver girt about his waist, Śrī Rāma went out to grind the enemy host to pieces.
First the Lord twanged his bow, and at its roar the enemy host was struck deaf.
lanka.68.cau2: Śrī Rāma, true to his word, loosed a hundred thousand arrows, which flew like winged serpents of death.
Iron shafts flew in great numbers everywhere, and fearsome fiendish warriors began to be cut down.
lanka.68.cau3: Feet, chests, heads and mighty arms are lopped away, and many warriors are left lying in a hundred pieces.
The wounded spin round and round and fall to the earth; the stoutest rise, steady themselves and fight again.
lanka.68.cau4: As the arrows strike, they roar like thunderclouds; many flee at the mere sight of those cruel shafts.
Fierce headless trunks run about, raising the cry: Seize, seize! Kill, kill!
lanka.68.do68: In a moment the Lord's arrows cut down the fearsome fiends.
and every arrow came back and slipped into Śrī Rāma's quiver.
lanka.69.cau1: Kumbhakarṇa considered in his mind and saw that the demon host had been slain in a moment.
The mighty warrior grew furious and gave a deep roar like a lion's.
lanka.69.cau2: In his rage he tears up mountains and hurls them where the mighty monkey warriors stand.
Seeing the huge rocks coming, the Lord cut them with his arrows and reduced them to dust.
lanka.69.cau3: Then Śrī Rāma, angered, drew his bow again and loosed many most terrible arrows.
The arrows pass into his body and out again, like lightning vanishing into a cloud.
lanka.69.cau4: The blood streaming over his black body looked like rills of red ochre running down a mountain of lampblack.
Seeing him shaken, the bears and monkeys rushed at him; as soon as they came close, he laughed.
lanka.69.do69: With a mighty roar he bellowed and seized monkeys by the million;
like a great elephant he dashes them to the ground, swearing by Rāvaṇa.
lanka.70.cau1: The troops of bears and monkeys ran, as a flock of sheep runs on seeing a wolf.
Bhavānī, the monkeys and bears ran in panic, crying out in anguished voices.
lanka.70.cau2: They cried: This demon is like a famine that now means to fall upon the land of the monkey race.
Rāma, cloud of mercy, slayer of Khara, remover of the suffering of those who bow to you, save us, save us!
lanka.70.cau3: As soon as he heard their piteous words, the Lord set out, making ready his bow and arrows.
Śrī Rāma kept his army behind him and, mighty beyond measure, went forward in anger.
lanka.70.cau4: He drew the bow and set a hundred arrows to it; once loosed, they sank into the demon's body.
Struck by them, he charged, full of rage; the mountains swayed and the earth shook.
lanka.70.cau5: He tore up a mountain; Śrī Rāma cut off that very arm.
He charged with the mountain in his left arm; the Lord cut off that arm too and laid it on the ground.
lanka.70.cau6: With his arms cut off, how did the wretch look? Like Mount Mandara shorn of its wings.
He glared fiercely at the Lord, as if he wished to swallow the three worlds.
lanka.70.do70: With a fearful, piercing shriek he charged, his mouth gaping wide.
In the sky the siddhas and gods cried out in terror: Alas, alas!
lanka.71.cau1: The Lord, treasury of compassion, saw that the gods were afraid, and drew his bow back to his ear.
He filled the demon's mouth with a mass of arrows; even so, the mighty one did not fall to the ground.
lanka.71.cau2: His mouth stuffed with arrows, he charged straight at the Lord, as if Death's own quiver had come alive and was advancing.
Then the Lord in anger took up a sharp arrow and severed his head from his trunk.
lanka.71.cau3: The head fell before Rāvaṇa, who was as distraught as a serpent that has lost its jewel.
The earth gave way as the fearsome trunk ran on; then the Lord cut it into two pieces.
lanka.71.cau4: The pieces fell to the earth like mountains dropping from the sky, crushing monkeys, bears and demons beneath them.
His radiance entered the Lord's face, and gods and sages alike were filled with wonder.
lanka.71.cau5: The gods beat their drums and rejoice; they sing praises and shower down flowers in plenty.
Having made their prayers, all the gods departed; at that very time the divine sage Nārada came.
lanka.71.cau6: From high in the sky he sang of Śrī Hari's many virtues, and their fine heroic strain pleased the Lord's heart.
The sage left, bidding him slay the wicked one quickly, and Śrī Rāma stood resplendent on the field of battle.
lanka.71.cha1: Śrī Rāma, the Lord of Kosala, of matchless strength, shines on the field of battle.
There are drops of sweat on his face, his lotus eyes are red, and drops of blood are on his body.
With both arms he twirls arrow and bow, and bears and monkeys make a fine sight on every side.
Tulasīdāsa says: Not even Śeṣa, with his many mouths, could describe that beauty.
lanka.71.do71: To that vile demon, a mine of sin, the Lord gave his own abode.
Pārvatī, dull-witted are those who do not worship Śrī Rāma.
lanka.72.cau1: At the close of day both armies turned back; the warriors were sorely wearied by the fight.
By Śrī Rāma's grace the strength of the monkey host grew, as a fire blazes up when it finds grass.
lanka.72.cau2: Day and night the demons dwindle, as merit dwindles when one proclaims it with one's own mouth.
Rāvaṇa laments bitterly, pressing his brother's head to his breast again and again.
lanka.72.cau3: The women weep, beating their breasts with their hands and recounting his great splendour and might.
At that moment Meghanāda arrived and consoled his father with many words.
lanka.72.cau4: Meghanāda said: Tomorrow you will see my prowess; why should I boast much now?
Father, the strength and the chariot I won from my chosen deity: that strength I have not yet shown you.
lanka.72.cau5: While he boasted thus, the day dawned, and monkeys in great numbers pressed against the four gates.
On this side stood monkeys and bears, heroes like Death; on that, demons steadfast in battle.
lanka.72.cau6: The warriors fight, each for his own side's victory; Garuḍa, that battle is beyond description.
lanka.72.do72: Meghanāda mounted his chariot of illusion and rose into the sky.
He roared with a loud peal of laughter, and terror seized the monkey host.
lanka.73.cau1: He hurled spears, pikes, swords, scimitars, missiles and weapons of many kinds, and thunderbolts;
he flung axes, iron clubs and rocks, and began to rain down arrows in multitudes.
lanka.73.cau2: Arrows covered the sky in all ten directions, as though the clouds of Maghā had set in a steady downpour.
Seize him, seize him, strike! — the cry rang in their ears, but no one could tell who was striking.
lanka.73.cau3: The monkeys leap into the sky with rocks and trees, but cannot see him, and come back dismayed.
By the power of illusion he turned the rugged passes, paths, hills and caves into a cage of arrows.
lanka.73.cau4: Where could they go? The monkeys were in distress, like mountains such as Mandara held captive by Indra.
Hanumān, son of the Wind, Aṅgada, Nala and Nīla: all these mighty ones he threw into confusion.
lanka.73.cau5: Next he struck Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa with arrows until their bodies were torn.
Then he began to fight Śrī Rāma; the arrows he loosed turned into serpents as they struck.
lanka.73.cau6: Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara, who is subject to none but himself, infinite, one and changeless, came under the power of the serpent noose.
Like an actor, the one Lord, ever free, performs many feigned acts.
lanka.73.cau7: For the splendour of the battle the Lord let himself be bound in the serpent noose, and the gods took fright.
lanka.73.do73: Pārvatī, he whose name the sages repeat to cut the bonds of worldly existence —
can he, the all-pervading abode of the universe, ever come under bondage?
lanka.74.cau1: Pārvatī, the deeds of Śrī Rāma in his embodied form cannot be reasoned out by the power of intellect or speech.
Knowing this, those who know the truth and are free of attachment leave all argument aside and worship Śrī Rāma.
lanka.74.cau2: Meghanāda threw the army into disarray; then he showed himself and began to speak abuse.
Jāmbavān said: Stand there, villain! Hearing this, his fury rose higher still.
lanka.74.cau3: Meghanāda said: Fool, I spared you because you were old; and now, wretch, you dare challenge me?
So saying, he hurled his flashing trident; Jāmbavān caught that very trident in his hand and ran at him.
lanka.74.cau4: He drove it into Meghanāda's chest, and the slayer of gods spun round and dropped to the earth.
Then in rage Jāmbavān seized him by the feet, whirled him round and dashed him on the earth, showing his own strength.
lanka.74.cau5: By virtue of a boon he would not die though struck; so Jāmbavān seized him by the foot and flung him on to Laṅkā.
Meanwhile the divine sage Nārada had sent Garuḍa, who came swiftly to Śrī Rāma's side.
lanka.74.do74क: Garuḍa, king of birds, seized and devoured all the swarms of illusory serpents.
The illusion was gone, and all the bands of monkeys rejoiced.
lanka.74.do74ख: Wielding rocks, trees and stones, and their claws, the enraged monkeys dashed forward.
The demons, more distraught than ever, fled and climbed up into the fort.
lanka.75.cau1: Meghanāda came out of his swoon, and on seeing his father was deeply ashamed.
At once he went to a cave in a great mountain, resolved to perform a sacrifice that would make him invincible.
lanka.75.cau2: Here Vibhīṣaṇa thought of a plan and said: Listen, my Lord, generous one of matchless strength:
Meghanāda, the wicked sorcerer who torments the gods, is performing an unholy sacrifice.
lanka.75.cau3: My Lord, if he brings it to completion, then, master, he will not be conquered quickly.
Hearing this, Śrī Rāma was greatly pleased and spoke to Aṅgada and many other monkeys:
lanka.75.cau4: Go, all of you, my brothers, with Lakṣmaṇa, and destroy the sacrifice there.
Lakṣmaṇa, you must slay him in battle; it grieves me deeply to see the gods in fear.
lanka.75.cau5: Listen, brother: slay him by strength, wit and stratagem, in such a way that the demon perishes.
Jāmbavān, Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa, you three stay with the army.
lanka.75.cau6: When Śrī Rāma gave the command, Lakṣmaṇa bound his quiver at his waist and made ready his bow;
then, firm in battle, with the Lord's might held in his heart, he spoke words as deep as a rumbling cloud:
lanka.75.cau7: If I return today without killing him, let me not be called Śrī Rāma's servant.
Even if a hundred Śivas come to his aid, I swear by Śrī Rāma, I will slay him.
lanka.75.do75: Bowing his head at Śrī Rāma's feet, Lakṣmaṇa, who is Ananta, set off at once,
and with him went the great warriors Aṅgada, Nīla, Mainda, Nala and Hanumān.
lanka.76.cau1: The monkeys went and saw him sitting there, offering blood and buffaloes as oblations.
They wrecked the whole sacrifice, and when still he did not rise, they began to praise him.
lanka.76.cau2: Even so he did not rise; then they went and seized him by the hair, and kicking him again and again they ran off.
