He gave chase with his trident; the monkeys fled and came to where Lakṣmaṇa stood before them.
lanka.76.cau3: He came on, overcome with fury, roaring again and again with a terrible cry.
Hanumān and Aṅgada rushed at him in anger; he hit them in the chest with the trident and brought them down.
lanka.76.cau4: He flung the fierce trident at Lakṣmaṇa, the Lord; with an arrow Ananta cut it into two pieces.
Hanumān and the crown prince Aṅgada rose again and struck at him furiously, but no blow told on him.
lanka.76.cau5: The heroes fell back, for the foe would not die though struck; then he charged with a terrible roar.
Seeing him come on like Death in wrath, Lakṣmaṇa loosed his dreadful arrows.
lanka.76.cau6: Seeing the arrows come at him like thunderbolts, the villain vanished at once.
Taking on many disguises he fought on, now showing himself, now hidden.
lanka.76.cau7: When they saw that the foe could not be overcome, the monkeys took fright, and Lakṣmaṇa, lord of serpents, became furious beyond measure.
Lakṣmaṇa made up his mind: I have played with this sinner long enough.
lanka.76.cau8: Remembering the glory of the Lord of Kosala, he fitted an arrow with all his might.
He let it fly, and it struck the demon full in the chest; at the moment of death he cast off all deceit.
lanka.76.do76: Where is Rāma's younger brother, where is Rāma? So saying, he gave up his life.
Aṅgada and Hanumān said: Blessed, blessed is your mother!
lanka.77.cau1: Hanumān lifted him without effort, laid him at the gate of Laṅkā and came back.
Hearing of his death, the gods and gandharvas all came into the sky, riding their aerial cars.
lanka.77.cau2: Showering flowers and beating their drums, they sing the spotless glory of Śrī Rāma.
Glory to you, Ananta! Glory to the support of the world! Lord, you have delivered all the gods.
lanka.77.cau3: Having sung their praises, the gods and siddhas departed, and Lakṣmaṇa came back to the ocean of mercy.
The moment Rāvaṇa heard of his son's death, he fainted and fell to the ground.
lanka.77.cau4: Mandodarī wails aloud; she beats her breast and cries out in many ways.
All the people of the city are distraught with grief, and every one of them calls Rāvaṇa vile.
lanka.77.do77: Then Rāvaṇa consoled all the women in many ways:
The whole world is a perishable form; consider it in your hearts and see.
lanka.78.cau1: Rāvaṇa instructed them in wisdom; base as he himself was, his words were auspicious and holy.
Many are skilled at teaching others; but those who live by it themselves are not many.
lanka.78.cau2: The night ended and dawn broke; the bears and monkeys pressed up to all four gates.
Rāvaṇa called his chief warriors and said: Whoever feels his heart waver when facing battle
lanka.78.cau3: had better run away right now; there is no good in turning one's back once in the fight.
I have stoked this enmity by the strength of my own arms; I myself will answer the enemy who has marched against us.
lanka.78.cau4: With these words he had a chariot swift as the wind made ready, and all the instruments of war struck up.
All the heroes, of matchless strength, set out as though a storm of lampblack were sweeping along.
lanka.78.cau5: Countless ill omens appeared at that time, but in the vast pride of his strength of arm he paid them no heed.
lanka.78.cha1: Proud beyond measure, he gave no thought to omens, good or bad; weapons slipped from their hands.
Warriors tumbled from chariots; horses and elephants trumpeted and screamed and bolted from their company.
Jackals, vultures and donkeys raised harsh and fearful cries, and dogs howled in great numbers.
Owls hooted with utterly dreadful voices, as if they were the messengers of death.
lanka.78.do78: Can wealth, good omens or peace of mind come, even in a dream, to one
who is bent on harming living beings, is in the grip of delusion, has turned from Śrī Rāma and delights in desire?
lanka.79.cau1: The boundless demon army set out, the fourfold host in many divisions.
There were mounts, chariots and carriages of every kind, and pennants and flags without number in many colours.
lanka.79.cau2: Many herds of frenzied elephants moved on, like rain-clouds of the monsoon driven by the wind.
There were hosts of famed warriors of every sort, brave in battle and versed in many kinds of magic.
lanka.79.cau3: That most colourful army looked as splendid as if the hero Spring had marshalled his forces.
As the army moved, the elephants of the quarters tottered, the ocean heaved and the mountains shook.
lanka.79.cau4: Dust rose and the sun was hidden; the wind fell still and the earth was in distress.
Drums and kettledrums sounded with a fearful din, like the clouds thundering at the dissolution of the world.
lanka.79.cau5: Kettledrums, trumpets and shehnais sounded the Mārū, the martial strain that delights warriors.
All the heroes gave lion-like roars and boasted of their own strength and valour.
lanka.79.cau6: Rāvaṇa said: Listen, my warriors. Crush the throngs of bears and monkeys.
I will kill the two royal brothers. With these words he moved his army forward to face the foe.
lanka.79.cau7: When all the monkeys learned of this, they rushed out calling on the name of Śrī Rāma.
lanka.79.cha1: The huge and fearsome monkeys and bears, like Death itself, charged,
as if flocks of winged mountains of many hues were flying.
Claws, teeth, rocks and mighty trees were their weapons; strong as they were, they knew no fear.
Hailing Śrī Rāma, the lion to that frenzied elephant Rāvaṇa, they sang of his fair renown.
lanka.79.do79: On both sides they shouted for victory; each warrior singled out an opponent of his own,
and they clashed, the one side praising Śrī Rāma, the other Rāvaṇa.
lanka.80.cau1: Seeing Rāvaṇa in a chariot and Śrī Rāma without one, Vibhīṣaṇa grew uneasy.
His great love stirred a doubt in his mind, and bowing at the Lord's feet he spoke with affection:
lanka.80.cau2: My Lord, you have no chariot, no armour to guard your body, no shoes for your feet; how will you overcome that mighty warrior?
The treasury of compassion said: Listen, friend. The chariot that brings victory is a different one.
lanka.80.cau3: Valour and steadfastness are the wheels of that chariot; truth and good conduct are its unshaken flag and banner.
Its horses are strength, discernment, self-restraint and doing good to others, yoked to it with forgiveness, compassion and equanimity for reins.
lanka.80.cau4: Worship of God is its skilled charioteer; its shield is dispassion, its sword contentment.
Charity is the axe, intellect the fierce lance, and the highest realised knowledge the stiff bow.
lanka.80.cau5: A pure and unwavering mind is the quiver; calm of mind, the yamas and the niyamas are its many arrows.
Reverence for brāhmaṇas and the guru is armour that nothing can pierce; there is no other means of victory to equal this.
lanka.80.cau6: Friend, for one who has such a chariot, made of dharma, there is no enemy anywhere left to conquer.
lanka.80.do80क: That hero can conquer even worldly existence, the great and unconquerable foe,
who has such a firm chariot. Listen, my friend of steady mind.
lanka.80.do80ख: The Lord's words filled Vibhīṣaṇa with joy, and he took hold of his lotus feet and said:
Rāma, treasure of grace and joy, by this means you have given me your teaching.
lanka.80.do80ग: Over there Rāvaṇa was calling out challenges; over here, Aṅgada and Hanumān.
Demons, bears and monkeys all fought, each swearing by his own master.
lanka.81.cau1: Brahmā and the other gods, with many siddhas and sages, watched the battle from the sky in their aerial chariots.
Umā, I too was with them, watching Śrī Rāma's deeds in the fervour of battle.
lanka.81.cau2: The warriors on both sides were drunk with the thrill of battle; the monkeys were winning, by the strength of Śrī Rāma.
They grappled one to one, hurling challenges, and crushed one another and threw each other to the ground.
lanka.81.cau3: They struck, hacked, seized and threw down their foes; they broke off heads and struck others with those heads.
They ripped open bellies, tore away arms, and seized warriors by the feet and dashed them to the ground.
lanka.81.cau4: The bears buried demon warriors in the earth and heaped sand over them.
The brave monkeys, pitted against the foe, seemed like a host of Deaths in wrath.
lanka.81.cha1: Like Yama in his wrath, the monkeys made a splendid sight, blood streaming from their bodies.
Those mighty fighters crushed the warriors of the demon army and thundered like clouds.
With a roar of rebuke they struck with slaps, bit with their teeth and trampled with their kicks.
Monkeys and bears shrieked and used cunning and force to bring the wicked to ruin.
lanka.81.cha2: Seizing their foes, they tore their cheeks, split their chests and hung the entrails about their own necks,
as if the Lord of Prahlāda, Narasiṁha, had taken many bodies and were at play in the arena of war.
Seize, kill, cut, throw down: the dreadful cries filled the sky and the earth.
Glory to Śrī Rāma, who truly makes a straw a thunderbolt and a thunderbolt a straw.
lanka.81.do81: Rāvaṇa saw his army giving way; in his twenty arms he held ten bows.
Mounting his chariot he drove forward, shouting in his arrogance: Turn back, turn back.
lanka.82.cau1: Rāvaṇa charged in towering rage; the monkeys went out to meet him with war-cries.
Lifting trees, stones and mountains in their hands, they hurled them on him all at once.
lanka.82.cau2: The rocks struck his thunderbolt-hard body and burst at once into fragments.
He did not budge but stood fixed, his chariot planted where it was: Rāvaṇa, mad for battle and raging beyond measure.
lanka.82.cau3: Pouncing this way and that and bellowing, he began to crush the monkey warriors, for his anger had risen high.
Bears and monkeys in great numbers fled, crying: Save us, save us, Aṅgada, Hanumān.
lanka.82.cau4: Protect us, protect us, O hero of the Raghus, our master; this wretch is devouring us like Death.
Seeing every monkey in flight, Rāvaṇa set arrows to his ten bows.
lanka.82.cha1: Fitting them to his bows he loosed a storm of arrows, which flew and struck like serpents.
Arrows filled the earth and sky, the quarters and the spaces between; where could the monkeys run?
A great uproar arose; the army of monkeys and bears, in distress, cried out in anguish:
O hero of the Raghus, ocean of compassion, friend of the afflicted, protector of your own, O Hari.
lanka.82.do82: Lakṣmaṇa saw his own army in distress; he tightened the quiver at his waist and took up his bow,
and then, touching his head to Śrī Rāma's feet, he strode out in anger.
lanka.83.cau1: Lakṣmaṇa said: Wretch, why are you killing monkeys and bears? Look upon me: I am your death.
Rāvaṇa said: Slayer of my son, it is you I have been searching for. Today I will strike you down and cool the fire in my breast.
lanka.83.cau2: With these words he loosed fierce arrows; Lakṣmaṇa cut every one into a hundred pieces.
Rāvaṇa hurled weapons by the million; Lakṣmaṇa cut them down to the size of sesame seeds and turned them aside.
lanka.83.cau3: Then he struck back with his own arrows, smashed the chariot and slew the charioteer.
He shot a hundred arrows into each of the ten foreheads, like serpents entering the peaks of a mountain.
lanka.83.cau4: Then he drove a hundred arrows into his chest; Rāvaṇa fell to the ground and knew nothing.
When the swoon passed, the mighty one rose again and hurled the spear that Brahmā had given him.
lanka.83.cha1: The fearsome spear that Brahmā had bestowed found its mark full in the breast of Lakṣmaṇa, Ananta himself.
The hero fell, stricken; the ten-headed one tried to raise him, but for all its fame his peerless strength failed him.
He on one of whose heads the whole mansion of the universe rests like a speck of dust:
him the foolish Rāvaṇa wanted to lift, not knowing the master of the three worlds.
lanka.83.do83: Seeing this, Hanumān, son of the Wind, ran forward, speaking harsh words.
As Hanumān came on, Rāvaṇa dealt him a most terrible blow with his fist.
lanka.84.cau1: Hanumān went down on one knee, yet did not fall; then he steadied himself and rose, full of anger.
Hanumān struck him a single blow with his fist, and Rāvaṇa fell like a mountain hit by a thunderbolt.
lanka.84.cau2: The swoon left him and he came round again, and began to praise Hanumān's great strength.
Hanumān said: Shame, shame on my valour, and shame on me, that you, enemy of the gods, are still alive.
lanka.84.cau3: With these words Hanumān carried Lakṣmaṇa back; Rāvaṇa saw it and was astonished.
Śrī Rāma said: Brother, recall in your heart who you are: you devour Death himself and you protect the gods.
lanka.84.cau4: On hearing these words the compassionate Lakṣmaṇa sat up, and the dreadful spear went off into the sky.
Taking up bow and arrows again he ran, and in eager haste came face to face with the enemy.
lanka.84.cha1: Swiftly again he shattered Rāvaṇa's chariot, killed the charioteer and left him reeling.
His heart pierced by a hundred arrows, Rāvaṇa fell to the ground in still greater distress.
Another charioteer laid him in a chariot and carried him at once to Laṅkā.
Śrī Rāma's brother, a mass of glory, then bowed again at the Lord's feet.
lanka.84.do84: There, coming to his senses, Rāvaṇa set about performing a sacrifice.
The fool, driven by obstinacy and steeped in ignorance, hoped for victory while setting himself against Śrī Rāma.
lanka.85.cau1: Here Vibhīṣaṇa learned all of it, and he went at once and told Śrī Rāma.
My Lord, Rāvaṇa is performing a sacrifice; if it is accomplished, the wretch will not die.
lanka.85.cau2: Send warrior monkeys quickly, my Lord, to lay it waste, and Rāvaṇa will come out to fight.
At daybreak the Lord sent out his finest warriors; Hanumān, Aṅgada and all the rest rushed off.
lanka.85.cau3: Leaping in sport, the monkeys scaled Laṅkā and entered Rāvaṇa's palace without fear.
The moment they saw him at his sacrifice, all the monkeys were filled with fierce anger.
lanka.85.cau4: Shameless one, you ran from the battle and came home, and here you sit in a heron's meditation!
So saying, Aṅgada kicked him; but the wretch, his mind set on his own ends, did not even look up.
lanka.85.cha1: When still he did not look, the monkeys in fury seized him with their teeth and kicked him.
They dragged the women out by the hair, and the women cried out most piteously.
Then he rose, furious as Death himself, and seizing the monkeys by the feet hurled them down.
Meanwhile the monkeys had laid the sacrifice waste; seeing it, he lost heart.
lanka.85.do85: Having laid the sacrifice waste, the monkeys came back safe to Śrī Rāma.
The demon set out in anger, giving up all hope of life.
lanka.86.cau1: As he set out, terrible ill omens appeared; vultures rose and alighted on his heads.
But he was in the grip of death and would listen to no one; he said: Sound the drums of war.
lanka.86.cau2: The boundless army of the demons marched, with many elephants, chariots, foot soldiers and horsemen.
How did the wicked rush at the Lord? As swarms of moths rush at a flame.
lanka.86.cau3: Here the gods offered praise and said: This one has brought dreadful calamity on us.
Do not play with him any longer, Rāma; Sītā grieves exceedingly.
lanka.86.cau4: Hearing the gods, the Lord smiled; Śrī Rāma rose and set his arrows in order.
His matted locks are bound firmly in a knot on his head, with flowers woven in here and there that shine among them.
lanka.86.cau5: Red-eyed, his body dark as a rain-cloud, he is the delight of the eyes of all the worlds.
A sash girds his waist with the quiver fastened on it, and in his hand is the hard Śārṅga bow.
lanka.86.cha1: The Śārṅga bow is in his hand, and a fine quiver, a store of arrows, is fastened at his waist;
his arms are stout, his chest broad and lovely, with the brāhmaṇa's footprint shining on it.
Tulasīdāsa says: As soon as the Lord began to turn his bow and arrows in his hands,
the universe, the elephants of the quarters, the Tortoise, the cosmic Serpent, the earth, the ocean and the mountains all shook.
lanka.86.do86: Seeing this splendour, the gods in delight rained down flowers without end.
Glory, glory, glory to the treasury of compassion, the home of beauty, strength and virtue!
lanka.87.cau1: Meanwhile the demon army came on, dense and jostling.
Seeing it, the monkey warriors advanced to meet it, like the massed clouds at the dissolution of the world.
lanka.87.cau2: Countless swords and sabres flashed, as if lightning gleamed in all ten directions.
Elephants, chariots and horses raised a harsh din, like the roar of terrible clouds.
lanka.87.cau3: The monkeys' many tails spread across the sky, like lovely rainbows risen there.
The dust rose like streams of rain, and arrows fell in a boundless shower of drops.
lanka.87.cau4: From both sides they struck with mountains, like thunderbolts falling again and again.
Śrī Rāma in anger loosed a rain of arrows, and the demon host was wounded.
lanka.87.cau5: Struck by the arrows, the warriors screamed and, reeling round and round, fell to the ground here and there.
Blood streamed from them like great waterfalls from mountains, and a river of blood flowed, striking fear into cowards.
lanka.87.cha1: That river of blood, fearsome to cowards and utterly unholy, flowed on.
The two armies are its banks, the chariots its sand, the wheels its whirlpools; dreadful is its flow.
Elephants, foot soldiers, horses, donkeys and mounts of every kind, past counting, are its water creatures;
arrows, spears and javelins are its snakes, bows its waves, and shields its many tortoises.
lanka.87.do87: Warriors fall like trees on the bank, and marrow flows thick as foam.
Cowards who see it there are afraid, while the hearts of true warriors are glad.
lanka.88.cau1: Ghosts, ghouls, vetālas, pramathas and huge, frightful shaggy goblins bathe in it.
Crows and herons fly off with arms; one snatches from another and eats.
lanka.88.cau2: Some say: Fools, even in such plenty your want does not leave you!
Wounded warriors lie groaning where they fell on the banks, like the dying laid half in the water here and there.
lanka.88.cau3: Vultures on the bank pull at entrails, like anglers intent on their fishing lines.
Many warriors float down with birds riding on them, as though boating on the river.
lanka.88.cau4: Yoginīs fill skull-bowls with blood again and again and store them up; the wives of ghosts and ghouls dance in the sky.
Cāmuṇḍās play warriors' skulls as cymbals and sing in many ways.
lanka.88.cau5: Packs of jackals crunch and gnaw, eat, howl, gorge themselves and snarl at one another.
Millions of trunks roam about without heads, and heads lying on the ground cry: Victory, victory!
lanka.88.cha1: Heads cry Victory, victory, and fierce headless trunks run about.
Tangled among skulls and swords they grapple, and great warriors bring other warriors down.
Proud in Śrī Rāma's strength, the monkeys crush the demon hordes.
Slain by Śrī Rāma's swarms of arrows, warriors sleep in the courtyard of battle.
lanka.88.do88: Rāvaṇa thought in his heart: The demons have been destroyed.
I am alone and the monkeys and bears are many; I will work boundless māyā.
lanka.89.cau1: The gods saw the Lord on foot, and great distress arose in their hearts.
Indra at once sent his own chariot, and Mātali brought it gladly.
lanka.89.cau2: The chariot was a mass of radiance, divine and matchless; the king of Kosala mounted it with joy.
Four lovely, spirited horses drew it, ageless and deathless, swift as thought.
lanka.89.cau3: Seeing Śrī Rāma in the chariot, the monkeys gained fresh strength and charged.
Unable to bear the monkeys' onslaught, Rāvaṇa then spread his māyā.
lanka.89.cau4: Śrī Rāma alone was untouched by that māyā; Lakṣmaṇa and the monkeys took it for real.
In the demon army the monkeys saw many Lords of Kosala, each with his younger brother.
lanka.89.cha1: Seeing many Rāmas and Lakṣmaṇas, the monkeys and bears were struck with groundless fear.
Lakṣmaṇa with them, they stood wherever they were, staring like figures in a painting.
Seeing his army bewildered, the Lord of Kosala smiled and set an arrow to his bow,
and in the twinkling of an eye Śrī Hari took the māyā away; the whole monkey host rejoiced.
lanka.89.do89: Then Śrī Rāma looked round at them all and spoke in a deep voice:
You warriors are all worn out; now watch the single combat.
lanka.90.cau1: So saying, Śrī Rāma drove the chariot forward and bowed his head to the lotus feet of the brāhmaṇas.
Then rage filled the heart of Rāvaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, and he rushed at him, roaring and threatening.
lanka.90.cau2: Rāvaṇa said: Those fighters you defeated in battle, ascetic, mark this, were nothing like me.
My name is Rāvaṇa, my fame is known to the world, and the guardians of the worlds lie in my prison.
lanka.90.cau3: You killed Khara, Dūṣaṇa and Virādha, and slew poor Vāli like a hunter.
You destroyed hosts of demon warriors and killed Kumbhakarṇa and Meghanāda.
lanka.90.cau4: Today I will settle the whole feud, king, unless you run from the battle.
This day I will deliver you to Death for certain; you have fallen into the hands of the hard Rāvaṇa.
lanka.90.cau5: Hearing his harsh words and knowing him doomed, Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, laughed and said:
All your greatness is true, quite true; but do not prattle, show your manhood.
lanka.90.cha1: Do not destroy your fair fame by prattling; hear what is right, and pardon me.
In the world there are three kinds of men, like the pāṭala, the mango and the jackfruit.
One gives flowers, one flowers and fruit, and one bears fruit alone.
So one man talks; another talks and acts; and one acts and does not go about talking of it.
lanka.90.do90: Hearing Śrī Rāma's words, Rāvaṇa laughed and said: You would teach me wisdom!
You were not afraid when you made this enmity; now your life has grown dear to you.
lanka.91.cau1: With these harsh words, the furious Rāvaṇa began to loose arrows like thunderbolts.
Arrows of many shapes sped out and covered the quarters, the spaces between them, the sky and the earth.
lanka.91.cau2: Śrī Rāma loosed a fire arrow, and in an instant the demon's shafts were burnt up.
In vexation he hurled a keen spear; with an arrow the Lord sent it back.
lanka.91.cau3: He flings millions of discuses and tridents; the Lord cuts them down and wards them off without effort.
How do Rāvaṇa's arrows come to nothing? As all the wicked man's desires do.
lanka.91.cau4: Then he struck the charioteer with a hundred arrows; he fell to the ground crying: Glory to Śrī Rāma!
Śrī Rāma graciously raised the charioteer up; then the Lord grew fiercely angry.
lanka.91.cha1: When Śrī Rāma turned in anger on his foe in battle, the arrows stirred restlessly in his quiver.
At the fierce twang of his bow all the man-eaters stood rigid, as if struck by a seizure.
Mandodarī's heart shook and trembled; the Tortoise, the earth and the mountains were afraid.
The elephants of the quarters trumpeted, gripping the earth with their tusks; watching the spectacle, the gods laughed.
lanka.91.do91: He drew the bow back to his ear and loosed terrible shafts.
Śrī Rāma's flights of arrows sped on like writhing snakes.
lanka.92.cau1: The arrows flew like winged serpents; first they killed the charioteer and the horses.
They shattered the chariot and struck down the flag and pennon; Rāvaṇa roared mightily, but within, his strength was spent.
lanka.92.cau2: Vexed, he quickly mounted another chariot and loosed missiles and weapons of many kinds.
All his efforts failed, as do those of a mind bent on harming others.
lanka.92.cau3: Then Rāvaṇa hurled ten lances and struck the four horses to the ground.
Raising the horses up, Śrī Rāma in anger drew his bow and loosed his arrows.
lanka.92.cau4: Śrī Rāma's arrows went forth in a line like bees, to roam the lotus-grove of Rāvaṇa's heads.
He struck each of the ten brows with ten arrows; they passed right through, and blood ran in torrents.
lanka.92.cau5: Streaming blood, the mighty demon charged; once again the Lord set arrows to the bow.
Śrī Rāma loosed thirty arrows and brought the heads, with the arms, down to the ground.
lanka.92.cau6: As soon as they were cut they grew anew; Śrī Rāma cut off the arms and heads again.
Many times the Lord struck off arms and heads, and as they fell they were at once made new.
lanka.92.cau7: The Lord of Kosala, who loves his sport, keeps cutting off the arms and heads.
Heads and arms filled the sky, like countless Ketus and Rāhus.
lanka.92.cha1: It was as though many Rāhus and Ketus were racing along the paths of the sky, streaming blood.
Śrī Rāma's fierce arrows keep striking them, so they never get to fall to the ground.
Each arrow has pierced a cluster of heads, and as they fly through the sky they look
as if the sun's rays in anger were threading Rāhus on strings here and there.
lanka.92.do92: The more the Lord strikes off his heads, the more endless they grow,
as desire grows fresh day after day when the objects of sense are indulged.
lanka.93.cau1: Seeing his heads multiply, Rāvaṇa forgot about death, and a fierce anger rose in him.
The deluded, overweening one roared and charged, all ten bows drawn.
lanka.93.cau2: On the field of battle Rāvaṇa raged and buried Śrī Rāma's chariot under a shower of arrows.
For one daṇḍa (about twenty-four minutes) the chariot could not be seen at all, as though the sun had hidden in mist.
lanka.93.cau3: When the gods cried out in dismay, the Lord grew angry and took up his bow.
Warding off the arrows, he cut off the enemy's heads, and they filled the quarters and the spaces between them, the sky and the earth.
lanka.93.cau4: The severed heads race along the paths of the sky, shouting victory and spreading fear:
Where is Lakṣmaṇa? Where is Sugrīva, king of the monkeys? Where is Rāma, hero of the Raghus, lord of Kosala?
lanka.93.cha1: The hosts of heads rushed on, crying: Where is Rāma? At the sight of them the monkeys fled.
Śrī Rāma smiled, set arrows to his bow and pierced the heads squarely.
Many Kālikās gathered in band upon band, garlands of heads in their hands,
as if, fresh from bathing in a river of blood, they were off to worship the banyan of war.
lanka.93.do93: Then Rāvaṇa, enraged, let loose a fearsome lance.
It flew at Vibhīṣaṇa head-on, like Death's own rod.
lanka.94.cau1: Seeing that dreadful lance coming, Śrī Rāma thought: My vow is to end the distress of those who bow to me.
At once he put Vibhīṣaṇa behind him and, standing in front, took the spear upon himself.
lanka.94.cau2: The lance struck and he swooned a little; it was the Lord's play, but the gods were thrown into distress.
Seeing the Lord in pain, Vibhīṣaṇa seized a mace in his hand and rushed forward in anger.
lanka.94.cau3: Vibhīṣaṇa said: You ill-starred, wicked, base, evil-minded wretch, you have made enemies of gods, men, sages and nāgas.
You offered your heads to Śiva with reverence, and so for each one you have received millions.
lanka.94.cau4: That is why, villain, you have lived till now; but now your death is dancing over your head.
Fool, you turn your back on Rāma and still want prosperity? So saying, he struck him with the mace full in the chest.
lanka.94.cha1: As the mace's terrible, crushing blow struck him in the middle of the chest, Rāvaṇa fell to the ground.
Blood streaming from his ten mouths, he recovered and rushed in again, full of rage.
The two mighty ones grappled in a wrestling bout, face to face, each striking the other.
Proud in the strength of Śrī Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa does not count him as worth the least trifle.
lanka.94.do94: Umā, did Vibhīṣaṇa ever so much as look Rāvaṇa in the face?
Now he grapples with him like Death itself: such is the power of Śrī Rāma.
lanka.95.cau1: Seeing Vibhīṣaṇa sorely wearied, Hanumān came running with a mountain in his hands.
He struck down the chariot, the horses and the charioteer, and kicked Rāvaṇa in the middle of the chest.
lanka.95.cau2: His body trembling hard, Rāvaṇa still kept his feet; Vibhīṣaṇa went to where the protector of his people stood.
Then Rāvaṇa challenged Hanumān and struck him, and Hanumān rose into the sky with his tail spread out.
lanka.95.cau3: Rāvaṇa grabbed the tail, and Hanumān flew off with him; then the mighty Hanumān wheeled round and grappled with him.
Equal fighters both, they battle in the sky, each hitting the other in his anger.
lanka.95.cau4: Shining in the sky, they plied trick upon trick and feat upon feat of strength, like a mountain of lampblack locked in battle with Mount Sumeru.
The demon would not fall to cunning or to force; so Hanumān, son of the Wind, remembered the Lord.
lanka.95.cha1: Remembering Śrī Rāma, steadfast Hanumān challenged Rāvaṇa and struck him.
Both fall to the ground, rise and fight again; the gods cried victory to the pair of them.
Seeing Hanumān hard pressed, the monkeys and bears ran in, beside themselves with anger.
But Rāvaṇa, drunk with battle, trampled all those brave warriors with the fierce might of his arms.
lanka.95.do95: Then, at Śrī Rāma's rallying call, the fierce monkeys charged.
Seeing how great the monkeys' strength was, Rāvaṇa brought out his deceit.
lanka.96.cau1: For a moment he vanished; then the wicked one appeared in many forms.
As many bears and monkeys as there were in Śrī Rāma's army, so many Rāvaṇas appeared on every side.
lanka.96.cau2: The monkeys saw Rāvaṇas beyond counting, and bears and monkeys fled this way and that.
The monkeys ran, their courage gone, crying: Save us, save us, O Lakṣmaṇa, O hero of the Raghus!
lanka.96.cau3: Millions of Rāvaṇas rush about in all ten directions, roaring dreadfully, harshly, terrifyingly.
All the gods took fright and fled, saying: Brothers, give up all hope of victory now.
lanka.96.cau4: One Rāvaṇa alone conquered all the gods; now there are many of him. Look for caves in the mountains.
Only Brahmā, Śiva and the wise sages held their ground, all those who had known something of the Lord's greatness.
lanka.96.cha1: Those who knew the Lord's might stayed fearless, but the monkeys took those enemies to be real.
All the monkeys and bears broke and fled in panic, crying: Protect us, compassionate Lord!
Hanumān, Aṅgada, Nīla and Nala, mighty and valiant in war, fought on
and crush the Rāvaṇas by millions upon millions, warriors sprung up like shoots from a soil of deceit.
lanka.96.do96: Seeing the gods and the monkeys in distress, the Lord of Kosala laughed,
and fitting a single arrow to his bow Śārṅga, he slew all the Rāvaṇas.
lanka.97.cau1: In a moment the Lord had cut away all the illusion, just as the dark splits and scatters once the sun comes up.
With but one Rāvaṇa before them, the gods were glad; they returned and showered the Lord with flowers.
lanka.97.cau2: Śrī Rāma raised his arm and brought the monkeys back; back they came, calling to one another.
Strengthened by the Lord, the bears and monkeys ran forward and, swift and fired up, came onto the battlefield.
lanka.97.cau3: Seeing the gods singing praises, Rāvaṇa said: So by their reckoning I am only one now!
Fools, you have always been the ones I beat. So saying, he rushed up into the sky in fury.
lanka.97.cau4: The gods fled, crying out in terror. Rāvaṇa shouted: Villains, where can you run from me?
Seeing the gods in distress, Aṅgada ran up, leapt, seized him by the foot and brought him down to the ground.
lanka.97.cha1: Having seized him, thrown him down and kicked him, Vāli's son went back to the Lord.
Recovering, the ten-headed one rose and roared with a dreadful, grating roar.
In his arrogance he strung all ten bows and, fitting arrows to them, rained down arrows in plenty.
He left every warrior wounded and frantic with fear, and he exulted to see his own strength.
lanka.97.do97: Then Śrī Rāma cut off Rāvaṇa's heads and arms, his arrows and his bows;
but they grew back, many more of them, as sins committed at a holy place grow.
lanka.98.cau1: When they saw the enemy's heads and arms grow back, the bears and monkeys were filled with rage.
This fool does not die though his heads and arms are cut! The bear and monkey warriors rushed at him in fury.
lanka.98.cau2: Aṅgada son of Vāli, Hanumān son of the Wind, Nala, Nīla, Sugrīva king of the monkeys, and the mighty Dvivida
pelt him with trees and mountains; he catches those same mountains and trees and strikes the monkeys with them.
lanka.98.cau3: One tears the enemy's body with his nails and runs off; another kicks him and runs.
Then Nala and Nīla clambered up onto his heads and ripped at his brows with their nails.
lanka.98.cau4: At the sight of the blood he was sorely dismayed, and he stretched out his arms to seize them.
They slipped every grasp and roamed about on his hands, two bees at large in a forest of lotuses.
lanka.98.cau5: Furious, he sprang and seized both of them once more; he was hurling them to the earth when they wrenched his arms round and escaped.
Then, furious, he took up his ten bows and wounded the monkeys with his arrows.
lanka.98.cau6: Rāvaṇa had struck Hanumān and the rest of the monkeys senseless, and evening had come; he was glad.
Seeing all the monkey heroes senseless, Jāmbavān, steadfast in battle, ran forward.
lanka.98.cau7: The bears with him, carrying mountains and trees, began to strike Rāvaṇa, challenging him again and again.
Mighty Rāvaṇa flew into a rage and, seizing them by the feet, dashed warrior after warrior to the ground.
lanka.98.cau8: Seeing his host struck down, the king of the bears in his anger kicked Rāvaṇa full in the chest.
lanka.98.cha1: The fierce blow of the kick to his chest left Rāvaṇa reeling, and he fell from his chariot to the earth.
He was clutching bears in all twenty hands, like bees lodged in lotuses at night.
Finding him senseless, the king of the bears kicked him once more and went to the Lord.
Knowing that night had come, the charioteer laid him in the chariot and set about bringing him round.
lanka.98.do98: Their swoon over, all the bears and monkeys came to the Lord.
All the demons, in great dread, stayed gathered round Rāvaṇa.
lanka.99.cau1: That very night Trijaṭā went to Sītā and told her all that had happened.
When Sītā heard how the enemy's heads and arms kept growing, a great fear filled her heart.
lanka.99.cau2: Her face clouded and anxiety rose in her mind; then Sītā said to Trijaṭā:
Mother, why do you not tell me what will happen? How is he to die, this tormentor of the world?
lanka.99.cau3: Even with his heads cut off by Śrī Rāma's arrows he does not die; Fate is turning everything the wrong way.
What keeps him alive is my ill fortune, which tore me from Śrī Hari's lotus feet.
lanka.99.cau4: The Fate that conjured the false golden deer of deceit is still angry with me;
the Fate that made me bear unbearable sorrow and made me speak bitter words to Lakṣmaṇa,
lanka.99.cau5: that has taken aim again and again and struck me with the heavy, poisoned arrows of separation from Śrī Rāma,
and that keeps me alive even in such sorrow: that same Fate keeps him alive, and no other.
lanka.99.cau6: Jānakī laments in many ways, recalling again and again the treasury of compassion.
Trijaṭā said: Hear me, princess. Let an arrow strike the gods' enemy in the heart, and he dies.
lanka.99.cau7: But the Lord does not strike him in the heart, because you, Vaidehī, dwell in his heart.
lanka.99.cha1: The Lord reasons: Jānakī dwells in his heart, and in Jānakī's heart is my dwelling;
in my belly are many worlds, and once the arrow strikes, all of them will perish.
Hearing this, Sītā felt great joy and great sorrow at once; seeing it, Trijaṭā spoke again:
Listen, fair one, this is how the enemy will now die; put away your great doubt.
lanka.99.do99: As his heads are cut off he will grow frantic, and his mind will lose its hold on you.
Then Śrī Rāma, who knows all, will strike Rāvaṇa in the heart.
lanka.100.cau1: With these words, after comforting her in many ways, Trijaṭā went back to her own house.
Remembering Śrī Rāma's nature, Vaidehī was seized by the bitter pain of separation.
lanka.100.cau2: She finds fault with the night and with the moon in many ways: the night has become as long as an age and does not pass.
Grieving in separation from Śrī Rāma, Jānakī weeps bitterly within her heart.
lanka.100.cau3: When the burning of separation in her heart grew unbearable, her left eye and arm throbbed.
She read it as a good omen and grew calm within: now the compassionate Śrī Rāma will come to me.
lanka.100.cau4: Meanwhile, at midnight, Rāvaṇa woke and began to rage at his charioteer:
Fool, you took me away from the battlefield! Shame, shame on you, you base, dull-witted wretch!
lanka.100.cau5: Holding his feet, the charioteer talked him round in many ways; at daybreak Rāvaṇa mounted his chariot and charged again.
When they heard that the ten-headed one was coming, a great commotion broke out in the monkey host.
lanka.100.cau6: The great warriors uprooted mountains and trees on every side and charged, grinding their teeth.
lanka.100.cha1: Fearsome monkeys and dreadful bears rushed in, gripping mountains.
They strike in towering rage, and under their blows the demons fled.
The strong monkeys broke the demon host and then hemmed Rāvaṇa in again.
From all four sides they slapped him and tore at his body with their nails, until he was in agony.
lanka.100.do100: Seeing how mighty the monkeys were, Rāvaṇa thought it over,
and vanishing in the twinkling of an eye, he spread out his illusion far and wide.
lanka.101.cha1: When he worked this deceit, fierce creatures appeared:
vampires, ghosts and ghouls, holding bows and iron arrows in their hands.
lanka.101.cha2: Yoginīs grip swords, and in one hand they hold human skulls.
Drinking fresh blood, they dance and sing many songs.
lanka.101.cha3: They raise a terrible cry of Seize! Kill!, and the sound fills every quarter.
They rush with gaping mouths to devour; then the monkeys began to flee.
lanka.101.cha4: Wherever the monkeys run, they see fire burning there.
The monkeys and bears were distraught; then sand began to rain down.
lanka.101.cha5: Leaving the monkeys stunned and helpless here and there, Rāvaṇa roared again.
All the warriors, Lakṣmaṇa and Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, among them, fell senseless.
lanka.101.cha6: Crying Alas, Rāma! Alas, Lord of the Raghus!, the great warriors wring their hands.
Having thus broken the strength of all, he worked another deceit.
lanka.101.cha7: He made many Hanumāns appear, who rushed forward holding rocks.
Forming hosts on every side, they went and surrounded Śrī Rāma.
lanka.101.cha8: Kill him! Seize him! Do not let him go! they cry, gnashing their teeth with tails raised.
Tails gleam in all ten directions, and in their midst stands the king of Kosala.
lanka.101.cha1_2: In their midst the beautiful dark body of the king of Kosala shone with such splendour
as if many rainbows had made a fine hedge round a tall tamāla tree.
Seeing the Lord so, the gods felt joy and grief at once in their hearts and cried: Victory, victory, victory!
Then Śrī Rāma, in anger, dispelled the illusion with a single arrow in the twinkling of an eye.
lanka.101.cha2_2: The illusion gone, the monkeys and bears were glad, and every one of them turned back with trees and mountains in hand.
Śrī Rāma loosed a multitude of arrows, and Rāvaṇa's arms and heads fell to the ground once more.
Those who might sing of the deeds of the battle between Śrī Rāma and Rāvaṇa for many aeons,
though they were hundreds of Śeṣas, Sarasvatīs, Vedas and poets, would still not reach the end of them.
lanka.101.do101क: Of its many glories dull-witted Tulasīdāsa has told a few,
just as a fly rises into the sky only as far as its own strength allows.
lanka.101.do101ख: His heads and arms were cut off many times, yet the warrior lord of Laṅkā did not die.
The Lord is at play, but gods, siddhas and sages are distressed to see the ordeal.
lanka.102.cau1: As they are cut, the heads multiply, as greed grows with every gain.
The enemy would not die and the toil had grown great; then Śrī Rāma looked towards Vibhīṣaṇa.
lanka.102.cau2: Umā, the Lord at whose will Death itself dies is testing his servant's love.
Vibhīṣaṇa said: Listen, all-knowing one, lord of all that moves and does not move, protector of those who bow to you, giver of joy to gods and sages.
lanka.102.cau3: In the hollow of his navel lies nectar; it is by its power, my Lord, that Rāvaṇa lives.
On hearing Vibhīṣaṇa's words, the compassionate Lord gladly took up fearsome arrows in his hand.
lanka.102.cau4: Then ill omens of many kinds began: donkeys, jackals and many dogs howled;
birds cried out, foretelling distress for the world, and comets appeared here and there in the sky.
lanka.102.cau5: A fierce burning glow spread through all ten quarters, and the sun was eclipsed though it was not the day for it.
Mandodarī's heart trembled violently, and the images shed water from their eyes.
lanka.102.cha1: Images wept, thunderbolts fell from the sky, a fierce wind blew and the earth quaked.
Clouds rained blood, hair and dust; who could tell how many ill omens there were?
Seeing countless portents, the gods in the sky grew distraught and cried: Victory! Victory!
Knowing the gods to be afraid, the compassionate Lord fitted arrows to his bow.
lanka.102.do102: Drawing the bow back to his ear, he loosed thirty-one arrows.
Śrī Rāma's arrows sped on like great serpents of death.
lanka.103.cau1: One arrow dried up the pool at his navel; the others struck his arms and heads in fury.
The arrows went off carrying the heads and arms, and the trunk, without heads or arms, danced upon the ground.
lanka.103.cau2: The trunk rushed about so fiercely that the earth sank beneath it; then the Lord struck it with an arrow and cut it in two.
Dying, he roared with a great and terrible cry: Where is Rāma? Let me challenge him and kill him in battle.
lanka.103.cau3: As Rāvaṇa fell, the earth shook, and the oceans, rivers, elephants of the quarters and mountains were thrown into turmoil.
He fell to the ground with his two halves stretched out, crushing hosts of bears and monkeys beneath them.
lanka.103.cau4: The arrows laid the arms and heads before Mandodarī and went back to where the Lord of the world was.
They all went and entered the quiver; seeing this, the gods beat their kettledrums.
lanka.103.cau5: His radiance passed into the Lord's face; seeing it, Śiva and four-faced Brahmā rejoiced.
The whole universe rang with the cry of victory: Glory to the hero of the Raghus, mighty of arm!
lanka.103.cau6: Hosts of gods and sages shower flowers: Glory to the compassionate one, glory, glory to Mukunda!
lanka.103.cha1: Glory to you, Lord, source of grace, Mukunda, remover of the pairs of opposites, giver of joy to those who come for refuge;
destroyer of the hosts of the wicked, supreme cause, ever compassionate, all-pervading one.
The gods, full of joy, shower flowers, and kettledrums resound loudly.
On the field of battle Śrī Rāma's limbs took on the beauty of many Kāmadevas.
lanka.103.cha2: On his head the crown of matted locks, with flowers here and there among them, looks most lovely,
as if stars were shining with sheets of lightning on a blue mountain.
As he twirls arrows and bow with his mighty arms, the drops of blood on his body look very fine,
as if red munia birds were perched on a tamāla tree in great contentment.
lanka.103.do103: Showering his gracious glance upon them, the Lord freed the hosts of gods from fear.
All the bears and monkeys rejoiced: Glory to Mukunda, abode of joy!
lanka.104.cau1: At the sight of her husband's heads Mandodarī fainted in anguish and fell to the ground.
Crowds of young women rose and ran, weeping; they lifted her up and came to Rāvaṇa.
lanka.104.cau2: Seeing their husband's state, they cried aloud; their hair came loose and they took no care of their bodies.
They beat their breasts in many ways and, weeping, recounted his might.
lanka.104.cau3: They said: My lord, by your might the earth was ever trembling, and fire, moon and sun lost their brightness.
That body whose weight Śeṣa and the cosmic tortoise could not bear lies on the ground, covered in dust.
lanka.104.cau4: Varuṇa, Kubera, Indra and the Wind: not one of them could stand firm before you in battle.
By the strength of your arms, my lord, you conquered Time and Yama; today you lie like one who has no protector.
lanka.104.cau5: Your lordship is known throughout the world; the strength of your sons and kin is beyond telling.
Turned away from Śrī Rāma, you have come to such a state that not one of your line is left to mourn you.
lanka.104.cau6: My lord, all of Brahmā's creation was under your sway, and the guardians of the quarters, afraid, bowed down to you every day.
Now jackals eat your heads and arms; there is nothing improper in this for one who turns from Śrī Rāma.
lanka.104.cau7: Under the sway of Death, my husband, you would not heed what you were told, and took the Lord of all things moving and unmoving for a man.
lanka.104.cha1: You took for a man Śrī Hari himself, the fire that burns the forest of demons.
Beloved, you did not worship the compassionate one, to whom Śiva, Brahmā and the gods bow.
From birth this body of yours delighted in harming others and was full of a flood of sins.
Even to you Śrī Rāma has given his own abode; I bow to Rāma, the Brahman free from every ill.
lanka.104.do104: Ah, my lord, there is no other ocean of mercy like Śrī Rāma.
The Lord has given you the state that hosts of yogīs find hard to attain.
lanka.105.cau1: Hearing Mandodarī's words, gods, sages and siddhas all were glad.
Brahmā, Maheśa, Nārada, Sanaka and his brothers, and all the great sages who speak of the highest truth
lanka.105.cau2: gazed their fill on Śrī Rāma and, lost in love, were all filled with joy.
Vibhīṣaṇa saw all the women weeping, and went to them with a heavy heart.
lanka.105.cau3: Seeing his brother's state, he grieved; then the Lord gave a command to his younger brother.
Lakṣmaṇa consoled him in many ways, and then Vibhīṣaṇa came back to the Lord.
lanka.105.cau4: The Lord turned a gracious glance on him and said: Leave off all grief and carry out the last rites.
Obeying the Lord's command, and bearing in mind the place and the time, he performed the rites as prescribed.
lanka.105.do105: Mandodarī and all the others offered him libations of sesame and water,
and went to the palace, recounting in their minds the many virtues of Śrī Rāma.
lanka.106.cau1: Vibhīṣaṇa came and bowed his head again; then the ocean of mercy called his younger brother.
He said: You, Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, Aṅgada, Nala, Nīla, Jāmbavān and Hanumān, wise in counsel,
lanka.106.cau2: go all together with Vibhīṣaṇa and perform his installation, said Śrī Rāma.
Bound by my father's word, I do not enter a city; so I send the monkeys and my brother, who are as my own self.
lanka.106.cau3: The monkeys left at once on hearing the Lord's words, and there they set about arranging the coronation.
They respectfully placed Vibhīṣaṇa on the throne, and once the tilaka was done they began to sing his praise.
lanka.106.cau4: All of them bowed their heads with joined palms, and came with Vibhīṣaṇa to the Lord.
Then Śrī Rāma called the monkeys to him and, speaking kind words, made them all happy.
lanka.106.cha1: He made them happy with words like nectar: It is by your strength that the enemy has been slain.
Vibhīṣaṇa has gained the kingdom, and your fame will stay ever new in the three worlds.
Those who sing with deep love of your auspicious glory together with mine
will cross the boundless ocean of worldly existence without effort.
lanka.106.do106: The hosts of monkeys hear the Lord's words and cannot have enough of them.
Again and again they all bow their heads and clasp his lotus feet.
lanka.107.cau1: Then the Lord called Hanumān to him. The Lord said: Go to Laṅkā.
Tell Jānakī the news, and come back with word of her welfare.
lanka.107.cau2: Then Hanumān came into the city; hearing of it, the demons and demonesses came running.
They honoured him in many ways, and then showed him Janaka's daughter.
lanka.107.cau3: Hanumān bowed to her from a distance, and Jānakī knew him for Śrī Rāma's messenger.
Sītā said: Tell me, dear one, is all well with the Lord, abode of grace, and his younger brother and the monkey army?
lanka.107.cau4: Hanumān said: Mother, the Lord of Kosala is well in every way; he has conquered Rāvaṇa in battle.
Vibhīṣaṇa has gained a kingdom that will not be shaken. Hearing Hanumān's words, Sītā's heart filled with joy.
lanka.107.cha1: Her mind overjoyed, her body thrilling, her eyes full of tears, Sītā, who is Ramā herself, said again and again:
What can I give you, Hanumān? In the three worlds there is nothing at all to equal these words.
Hanumān said: Listen, Mother: today, beyond doubt, I have gained the kingdom of the whole world,
for I see Śrī Rāma, victorious in battle over the enemy host, safe and well, with his brother.
lanka.107.do107: Sītā said: Listen, my son Hanumān: may every virtue make its home in your heart,
and may the king of Kosala, together with Lakṣmaṇa, who is Ananta, always look on you with favour.
lanka.108.cau1: Now, dear son, make such an effort that my eyes may see the Lord in his dark and tender form.
Then Hanumān went to Śrī Rāma and told him that Sītā was well.
lanka.108.cau2: Hearing the message, the ornament of the solar race sent for Prince Aṅgada and Vibhīṣaṇa and said:
Go with the son of the Wind, and bring Sītā here with due honour.
lanka.108.cau3: They all went straight to Sītā; every one of the demonesses there was serving her meekly.
Vibhīṣaṇa quickly instructed them, and they bathed her with every kind of care.
lanka.108.cau4: They put many kinds of ornaments on her, then made ready a fine palanquin and brought it.
Remembering the loving Śrī Rāma, the abode of bliss, Sītā joyfully mounted it.
lanka.108.cau5: Guards with canes in hand walked on every side, and all went along with hearts full of joy.
The bears and monkeys all came to see her, and the guards rushed angrily to hold them off.
lanka.108.cau6: Śrī Rāma said: Friend, do as I say: bring Sītā on foot,
so that the monkeys may look on her as on a mother. So the Lord Śrī Rāma said, smiling.
lanka.108.cau7: The bears and monkeys rejoiced at the Lord's words, and the gods showered many flowers from the sky.
Sītā had earlier been placed in the fire; now the Witness within all wished to bring her forth.
lanka.108.do108: For this reason the treasury of compassion spoke a few harsh words.
Hearing them, all the demonesses began to grieve.
lanka.109.cau1: Sītā, pure in mind, deed and word, took the Lord's words upon her head and said:
Lakṣmaṇa, assist me in this rite of dharma, and kindle a fire at once.
lanka.109.cau2: Lakṣmaṇa heard Sītā's words, steeped in the pain of separation, in discernment, in dharma and in right counsel.
His eyes filled with tears and he stood with palms joined; he too could say nothing to the Lord.
lanka.109.cau3: Seeing Śrī Rāma's look, Lakṣmaṇa ran, kindled the fire and brought plenty of wood.
Seeing the fierce fire, Sītā felt joy in her heart, and no fear at all.
lanka.109.cau4: Sītā said: If in mind, word and deed there is in my heart no refuge other than Śrī Rāma,
then may Fire, who knows the state of every heart, be as sandalwood to me.
lanka.109.cha1: Remembering the Lord, Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, entered the fire as if it were sandalwood.
She hailed the Lord of Kosala, whose feet, worshipped by Śiva, she loves with a love wholly pure.
Her reflected image and the stain of worldly reproach burned away in the blazing fire.
No one perceived the Lord's play; gods, siddhas and sages stood in the sky, watching.
lanka.109.cha2: Then Fire took a bodily form and held the hand of the true Śrī (Sītā), known to the Vedas and the world,
and, as the Ocean of Milk once gave Indirā to Viṣṇu, brought her and gave her to Śrī Rāma.
She shone at Śrī Rāma's left side, her beauty exceedingly lovely,
as though a bud of golden lotus stood beside a fresh blue lotus.
lanka.109.do109क: The gods joyfully shower flowers, and kettledrums sound in the sky.
Kinnaras sing, and celestial women dance, riding in their aerial cars.
lanka.109.do109ख: The beauty of the Lord with Sītā is measureless and boundless.
Seeing it, the bears and monkeys rejoiced and cried: Glory to the Lord of the Raghus, essence of all joy!
lanka.110.cau1: Then, given leave by Śrī Rāma, Mātali bowed his head at his feet and departed.
Then came the gods, ever intent on their own ends, speaking as if they sought only the highest good.
lanka.110.cau2: Friend of the lowly, compassionate king of the Raghus, O God, you have shown mercy to the gods.
Bent on enmity against the whole world, this lustful villain, who walked the crooked path, has fallen by his own sin.
lanka.110.cau3: You are the imperishable Brahman, the same towards all, ever unvarying and by nature detached;
without parts, beyond the guṇas, unborn, sinless, untouched by ill, unconquerable, of unfailing power and full of compassion.
lanka.110.cau4: You took the forms of the Fish, the Tortoise, the Boar, the Man-Lion, the Dwarf and Paraśurāma.
Whenever the gods have suffered, my Lord, you yourself have taken many bodies and ended it.
lanka.110.cau5: This wicked one was impure, ever hostile to the gods, sunk in desire, greed and pride, and full of wrath;
that this chief of the vile should attain your state fills our minds with wonder.
lanka.110.cau6: We gods, though highly qualified, were bent on self-interest and forgot devotion to the Lord.
We have always been caught in the current of worldly existence. Now, Lord, we have come for refuge: protect us.
lanka.110.do110: Their prayer made, all the gods and siddhas stood where they were with palms joined.
Then Brahmā, his body thrilling with deep love, began to praise him:
lanka.111.cha1: Glory to you, Rāma, ever the home of bliss, O Hari, O Lord of the Raghus who bears bow and arrows.
O Lord, you are a lion to the elephant of worldly existence, splitting it apart; ocean of virtues, all-wise, Master, all-pervading one.
lanka.111.cau2: Your form has the beauty of many Kāmadevas and is beyond compare; siddhas, great sages and poets sing your virtues.
Your glory purifies; as Garuḍa in anger seizes a great serpent, so you seized Rāvaṇa.
lanka.111.cau3: Lord, you delight your devotees and break their grief and fear; you are ever free of anger, pure awareness.
Your incarnation is noble and of boundless virtues; you destroy the earth's burden and are knowledge in its fullness.
lanka.111.cau4: Unborn, all-pervading, one, ever without beginning: compassionate Rāma, I bow to you with joy.
Ornament of Raghu's line, slayer of Dūṣaṇa, you made a king of the lowly Vibhīṣaṇa.
lanka.111.cau5: Treasury of virtue and knowledge, free of pride, unborn, all-pervading and stainless: Rāma, I bow to you always.
The might and strength of your arms are fierce; you are most skilled in rooting out the hosts of the wicked.
lanka.111.cau6: Kind without cause to the lowly and seeking their good, abode of beauty, I bow to you with Sītā, who is Ramā herself.
You carry souls across worldly existence, you are beyond cause and effect, and you take away the dreadful faults born in the mind.
lanka.111.cau7: You bear lovely arrows, bow and quiver; your eyes are like red lotuses; you are the best of kings.
Temple of joy, beautiful, Lord of Śrī, you quell pride, lust and false attachment.
lanka.111.cau8: You are faultless, undivided, beyond the reach of the senses; you are ever all forms, and yet you have not become all things.
So the Vedas say; it is no idle tale: just as the sun and its light are distinct and yet not distinct.
lanka.111.cau9: All-pervading Lord, these monkeys have all fulfilled their lives, gazing reverently on your face.
Shame on our life and our divine bodies, O Hari, for without devotion to you we lie lost in worldly existence.
lanka.111.cau10: Compassionate to the lowly, show mercy now and take away my mind that makes divisions,
by which I act perversely and, taking that sorrow for joy, go about content.
lanka.111.cau11: You break the wicked and adorn the lovely earth; your lotus feet are served by Śambhu and Umā.
Lord of kings, give me this boon: that I may always have a love for your lotus feet that brings every good.
lanka.111.do111: Brahmā, the four-faced, made his prayer, his body thrilling with love.
Gazing on the ocean of beauty, his eyes could not have their fill.
lanka.112.cau1: At that moment Daśaratha came there; seeing his son, his eyes brimmed with tears.
The Lord and his younger brother bowed to him, and then the father gave his blessing.
lanka.112.cau2: The Lord said: Father, it is all the power of your merit that I have conquered the invincible king of the demons.
Hearing his son's words, his love grew greatly; his eyes filled and the hair on his body stood on end.
lanka.112.cau3: Śrī Rāma, mindful of his father's love of old, looked at him and gave him firm knowledge.
Umā, that is why Daśaratha did not attain liberation: he had set his heart on devotion that keeps the Lord and the devotee distinct.
lanka.112.cau4: Those who worship the Lord with form do not take liberation; to them Śrī Rāma gives devotion to himself.
Bowing to the Lord again and again, Daśaratha went gladly to the abode of the gods.
lanka.112.do112: The Lord of Kosala stood safe and well with his younger brother and Jānakī.
Seeing their beauty, Indra, lord of the gods, rejoiced at heart and began to praise him:
lanka.113.cha1: Glory to you, Rāma, abode of beauty, giver of rest to those who bow before you.
You bear a fine quiver, arrows and bow; your arms are mighty and glorious.
lanka.113.cha2: Glory to you, foe of Dūṣaṇa and Khara, crusher of the demon hosts.
My Lord, you have slain this wicked one, and all the gods now have a protector.
lanka.113.cha3: Glory to you who lift the earth's burden; your greatness is noble and boundless.
Glory to you, merciful foe of Rāvaṇa, who left the demons broken.
lanka.113.cha4: The lord of Laṅkā, swollen with pride in his strength, had brought gods and gandharvas under his sway.
Sages, siddhas, men, birds and nāgas: he stubbornly dogged the steps of them all.
lanka.113.cha5: Given to malice towards others and utterly wicked, that great sinner has reaped his fruit.
Now listen, you who are kind to the lowly, whose eyes are large as lotuses:
lanka.113.cha6: I was full of pride, thinking there was none my equal.
Now that I have seen the Lord's lotus feet, the pride that brought heaps of sorrow is gone.
lanka.113.cha7: Some meditate on Brahman without attributes, whom the Vedas hymn as unmanifest.
But the one I love is the king of Kosala, Śrī Rāma in his form with attributes.
lanka.113.cha8: With Sītā and your younger brother, make your home in my heart.
Know me as your own servant, abode of Ramā, and give me devotion.
lanka.113.cha9: Give me devotion, abode of Ramā, remover of fear, giver of joy to those who seek refuge.
Home of joy, Rāma, Lord of the Raghus, lovely as many Kāmadevas, I bow to you.
Delight of the hosts of gods, destroyer of the pairs of opposites, wearing a human body, of matchless strength,
Rāma, worshipped by Brahmā, Śaṅkara and the rest, tender with compassion, I bow to you.
lanka.113.do113: Now look on me with grace, merciful Lord, and give me your command:
what shall I do? Hearing these pleasing words, the Lord, compassionate to the lowly, spoke:
lanka.114.cau1: Listen, Indra: the monkeys and bears of ours whom the demons killed are lying on the ground.
For my sake they gave up their lives; wise lord of the gods, bring them all back to life.
lanka.114.cau2: Listen, Garuḍa: these words of the Lord are very deep, and only sages rich in knowledge understand them.
The Lord could slay the three worlds and bring them to life again; here he simply gave the honour to Indra.
lanka.114.cau3: Showering nectar, Indra brought the monkeys and bears back to life, and they all rose up joyfully and came to the Lord.
The rain of nectar fell on both armies, yet only the bears and monkeys revived, not the demons.
lanka.114.cau4: The minds of those demons had taken on the form of Śrī Rāma; they were set free, the bonds of worldly existence loosed.
The monkeys and bears were all born of portions of the gods, and all of them revived by the will of Śrī Rāma.
lanka.114.cau5: Who is such a friend to the lowly as Śrī Rāma, who set free the demons, every one of them?
Rāvaṇa, wicked, a home of impurity and given to lust, attained a state that the greatest sages do not attain.
lanka.114.do114क: Having showered flowers, the gods all mounted their beautiful aerial cars and departed.
Seeing that the moment was right, the wise Śiva came to the Lord.
lanka.114.do114ख: With supreme love, joining both his hands, his lotus eyes filled with tears,
his body thrilling and his voice choked, Śiva, the foe of Tripura, prays:
lanka.115.cha1: Protect me, O Lord of Raghu's line, who hold the excellent bow and arrows in your beautiful hands.
You are the wind that scatters the vast, dense veil of the clouds of delusion, the fire to the forest of doubt, the delight of the gods.
lanka.115.cau2: Without attributes and with attributes, abode of virtues and beautiful, you are the sun of mighty splendour to the darkness of error.
Lion to the elephants of desire, anger and pride, dwell for ever in the forest of your devotee's mind.
lanka.115.cau3: To the lotus beds of the throngs of sensual cravings you are a hard frost; you are generous, and beyond the reach of the mind.
Mount Mandara to the ocean of worldly existence, drive away my great fear and carry me across the round of births, so hard to cross.
lanka.115.cau4: Dark of body, lotus-eyed, friend of the lowly, deliverer of those who bow to you from their distress,
O King Rāma, dwell for ever within my heart, with your younger brother and Sītā.
lanka.115.cau5: Joy of the sages, ornament of the circle of the earth, Tulasīdāsa's Lord who shatters fear.
lanka.115.do115: My Lord, when your coronation takes place in the city of Kosala,
I will come, O ocean of mercy, to see your noble deeds.
lanka.116.cau1: When Śiva had made his prayer and departed, Vibhīṣaṇa came close to the Lord.
Bowing his head at his feet, he said in gentle words: My Lord, wielder of the Śārṅga bow, hear my plea.
lanka.116.cau2: My Lord, you have slain Rāvaṇa with his family and his army, and spread your holy fame through the three worlds.
On me, wretched and unclean, poor in understanding and low in birth, you have shown grace in many ways.
lanka.116.cau3: Now, my Lord, sanctify your servant's house; bathe there, and let the weariness of battle fall away.
Look over the treasury, the palaces and the wealth, O compassionate one, and give gladly to the monkeys.
lanka.116.cau4: My Lord, accept me wholly as yours; then, when you go to Ayodhyā, take me along.
As he heard these gentle words, both the large eyes of the Lord, kind to the lowly, filled with tears.
lanka.116.do116क: Śrī Rāma said: Listen, brother, this is the truth: your treasury and your house are all mine.
But when I remember Bharata's state, each moment passes for me like an aeon.
lanka.116.do116ख: In the garb of an ascetic, his body worn thin, he repeats my name without ceasing.
My friend, I beg you, find a way for me to see him soon.
lanka.116.do116ग: If I go when the appointed time has passed, I shall not find my brother alive.
As he remembered his younger brother's love, the Lord's body thrilled again and again.
lanka.116.do116घ: The Lord went on: Rule for a whole aeon, and keep me in mind within your heart.
Then you will reach my abode, where all the saints go.
lanka.117.cau1: Hearing Śrī Rāma's words, Vibhīṣaṇa joyfully clasped the feet of the abode of grace.
All the monkeys and bears rejoiced, and holding the Lord's feet they told of his spotless virtues.
lanka.117.cau2: Then Vibhīṣaṇa went to his palace and had the aerial car loaded with heaps of gems and with clothes.
He brought the Puṣpaka and placed it in front of the Lord; then the ocean of mercy smiled and said:
lanka.117.cau3: Listen, my friend Vibhīṣaṇa: mount the aerial car, go up into the sky and rain down clothes and ornaments.
Vibhīṣaṇa went up into the sky that very moment and rained down every gem and garment.
lanka.117.cau4: Each takes whatever pleases his fancy; the monkeys put the gems in their mouths and spit them out again.
Śrī Rāma laughed, with Sītā and his younger brother, he who delights in play, the abode of grace.
lanka.117.do117क: He whom sages do not reach even in meditation, of whom the Vedas say neti neti, not this, not this,
that same ocean of mercy is sporting in many ways with the monkeys.
lanka.117.do117ख: Umā, for yoga, japa, charity, austerity, many kinds of sacrifice, vows and rules of observance
Śrī Rāma does not show such grace as he does for love, pure and unmixed.
lanka.118.cau1: The bears and monkeys received clothes and ornaments, and decked out in them came to Śrī Rāma.
Seeing all the monkeys in such variety, the Lord of Kosala laughs again and again.
lanka.118.cau2: Looking at them all, Śrī Rāma showed them kindness and spoke gentle words:
By your strength I slew Rāvaṇa, and then crowned Vibhīṣaṇa.
lanka.118.cau3: Now go, all of you, each to your own home; remember me, and fear no one.
Hearing these words, the monkeys were overcome with love, and all of them said with joined palms and respect:
lanka.118.cau4: My Lord, whatever you say becomes you; but hearing such words we are bewildered.
You counted us monkeys poor and lowly and gave us a master in yourself; you, O Lord of the Raghus, rule the three worlds.
lanka.118.cau5: Hearing the Lord's words, we are dying of shame: do mosquitoes ever do Garuḍa a service?
Seeing Śrī Rāma's countenance, the bears and monkeys were lost in love and had no wish to go home.
lanka.118.do118क: At the Lord's prompting, all the monkeys and bears, keeping Śrī Rāma's form in their hearts,
set out with joy and sorrow mingled, after making their humble pleas in many ways.
lanka.118.do118ख: Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, Nīla, Jāmbavān, king of the bears, Aṅgada, Nala and Hanumān,
together with Vibhīṣaṇa and the other mighty monkey troop leaders,
lanka.118.do118ग: could say nothing, overcome by love, their eyes filling with tears again and again.
Facing Śrī Rāma, they gazed at him, holding back even the blink of their eyes.
lanka.119.cau1: Seeing their exceeding love, Śrī Rāma took them all up into the aerial car.
Bowing his head in his heart at the feet of the brāhmaṇas, he set the car moving northward.
lanka.119.cau2: As the car moves off there is a great clamour, everyone crying: Glory to the hero of the Raghus.
There is a throne, very high and lovely; on it the Lord took his seat with Sītā.
lanka.119.cau3: Śrī Rāma with his lady shines as though cloud and lightning rested on a summit of Mount Meru.
The beautiful car sped on in great haste; the gods rejoiced and rained down flowers.
lanka.119.cau4: A most pleasant breeze blew, cool, gentle and fragrant; the waters of ocean, lake and river were pure.
Fair omens appear all around; hearts are glad, and the sky and the quarters are clear.
lanka.119.cau5: Śrī Rāma said: Look at the battlefield, Sītā. Here Lakṣmaṇa slew Meghanāda, conqueror of Indra.
Struck down by Hanumān and Aṅgada, mighty demons lie fallen on the field.
lanka.119.cau6: Kumbhakarṇa and Rāvaṇa, the two brothers who tormented gods and sages, were slain here.
lanka.119.do119क: Here I built the bridge and installed Śiva, the home of bliss.
Then the compassionate Lord, with Sītā, bowed to Śiva.
lanka.119.do119ख: Every place in the forest where the ocean of mercy had stayed and rested
he showed to Sītā, and told her the names of them all.
lanka.120.cau1: Swiftly the car came to where the lovely Daṇḍaka forest lay.
Śrī Rāma went to the dwellings of all the many great sages, Agastya and the rest.
lanka.120.cau2: Having received the blessings of all the seers, the Lord of the world came to Citrakūṭa.
There he gladdened the sages, and the car flew swiftly on from there.
lanka.120.cau3: Next Śrī Rāma showed Sītā the lovely Yamunā, which takes away the taint of the Kali age.
Then they saw the holy Gaṅgā, and Śrī Rāma said: Sītā, bow to her.
lanka.120.cau4: Now see Prayāga, king of holy places, at the sight of which the sins of ten million births take flight.
Then see the most purifying Triveṇī, which takes away grief and is a ladder to the world of Śrī Hari.
lanka.120.cau5: And now see the city of Ayodhyā, most purifying, which destroys the threefold affliction and the disease of worldly existence.
lanka.120.do120क: With Sītā, the compassionate Lord bowed to Ayodhyā.
His eyes filled with tears and his body thrilled; again and again Śrī Rāma was overjoyed.
lanka.120.do120ख: Then the Lord came to the Triveṇī and bathed there joyfully,
and together with the monkeys he gave gifts of many kinds to the brāhmaṇas.
lanka.121.cau1: The Lord explained to Hanumān: Take the form of a young brahmacārī and go to Ayodhyā.
Give Bharata the news that we are well, and come back with news from there.
lanka.121.cau2: Hanumān, son of the Wind, set off at once. Then the Lord went to Bharadvāja.
The sage worshipped him with many rites, sang his praises and then gave his blessing.
lanka.121.cau3: Bowing at the sage's feet with both palms joined, the Lord mounted the aerial car and went on again.
Here the Niṣāda heard that the Lord had come, and called his people, crying: A boat! Where is a boat?
lanka.121.cau4: Then the aerial car came over the Gaṅgā and, at the Lord's command, came down on the bank.
Then Sītā worshipped the Gaṅgā, and after that fell at her feet in many ways.
lanka.121.cau5: Gaṅgā, glad at heart, gave her blessing: Fair lady, may your married happiness never be broken.
As soon as he heard, Guha ran, overcome with love, and came near, brimming with the highest joy.
lanka.121.cau6: Seeing the Lord with Vaidehī, he fell to the ground, aware of his body no longer.
Seeing his great love, Śrī Rāma joyfully raised him up and pressed him to his heart.
lanka.121.cha1: The Lord of Ramā, treasury of mercy, king among the wise, pressed him to his heart,
seated him very close and asked how he was. Then he made his entreaty:
Now that I have seen your lotus feet, which Brahmā and Śaṅkara serve, all is well with me.
O Rāma, abode of joy, whose every wish is fulfilled, I bow to you; Rāma, I bow to you.
lanka.121.cha2: Śrī Hari pressed the Niṣāda, lowly in every way, to his heart as he would Bharata.
Dull-witted Tulasīdāsa, in the grip of delusion, has forgotten such a Lord.
This holy story of Śrī Rāma, Rāvaṇa's foe, ever grants love for Śrī Rāma's feet.
It takes away desire and the other passions and gives realised knowledge; gods, siddhas and sages sing it with joy.
lanka.121.do121क: To those of understanding who hear the deeds of Śrī Rāma's victory in battle,
the Lord gives victory, discernment and prosperity, day after day.
lanka.121.do121ख: This age of Kali is a home of impurity: reflect in your mind and see.
Apart from the name of Śrī Rāma, there is no other support.
